griqualand-west-colony.t: The short-lived British Crown colony around the Kimberley diamond fields, the cradle of South Africa's mining industry.
griqualand-west-colony.o: After the 1871 [[e:keate-award|Keate Award]] upheld [[e:nicolaas-waterboer|Nicolaas Waterboer's]] claim to the diamond diggings of [[s:griqualand-west|Griqualand West]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] annexed the area. It was governed at first through the Cape and was proclaimed a separate [[e:crown-colony|Crown colony]] in 1873, with [[e:richard-southey|Richard Southey]] as lieutenant-governor and [[e:kimberley|Kimberley]], the town around the [[e:big-hole|Big Hole]], as its capital.
griqualand-west-colony.r: Tens of thousands of diggers and African migrant workers poured in. Claim holders were mostly white, and disputes over labour, permits and illicit diamond buying shaped politics. The [[e:black-flag-rebellion|Black Flag Rebellion]] of white diggers in 1875 forced [[e:richard-southey|Southey]]'s recall. A [[e:griqua|Griqua]] and [[s:batlhaping-chiefdom|Tlhaping]] rising in 1878 was suppressed.
griqualand-west-colony.e: The colony was annexed to the [[s:cape-colony|Cape Colony]] in 1880. Its diamond fields became the base of [[e:cecil-rhodes|Cecil Rhodes's]] [[e:de-beers|De Beers]] company, and the methods used there, such as closed labour compounds, shaped South African mining.

gaya-confederacy.t: A league of iron-rich statelets in southern Korea that stood between Baekje and Silla for five centuries and traded closely with Japan.
gaya-confederacy.o: Gaya developed from the [[s:byeonhan|Byeonhan]] statelets of the lower [[e:nakdong-river|Nakdong]] river. Tradition dates its founding to 42 CE, when six golden eggs descended from heaven at [[e:gimhae|Gimhae]] and hatched the founders of six Gaya states, the eldest being [[e:suro-of-geumgwan-gaya|Suro of Geumgwan Gaya]].
gaya-confederacy.r: Gaya never unified into a single kingdom. Its members, including [[s:geumgwan-gaya|Geumgwan Gaya]], [[s:ara-gaya|Ara Gaya]] and [[s:daegaya|Daegaya]], were led first by [[e:gimhae|Gimhae]] and, after a [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] expedition of 400 broke its power, by Daegaya at [[e:goryeong|Goryeong]]. Gaya exported iron ingots and armour, made fine stoneware, and kept close ties with Wa; the [[e:nihon-shoki|Nihon shoki]] calls part of it Mimana. [[e:king-gasil|King Gasil]] of Daegaya is credited with devising the gayageum zither, for which the musician [[e:ureuk|Ureuk]] composed music.
gaya-confederacy.e: [[s:silla|Silla]] absorbed the states one by one: [[s:geumgwan-gaya|Geumgwan Gaya]] surrendered in 532 and [[s:daegaya|Daegaya]] fell to [[e:jinheung-of-silla|King Jinheung]] in 562. Gaya's elite and craftsmen were integrated into Silla, notably the family of the general [[e:kim-yu-sin|Kim Yu-sin]].

greater-republic-of-central-america.t: Union of Honduras, Nicaragua and El Salvador formed in 1896, one of several failed attempts to revive the Central American federation.
greater-republic-of-central-america.o: The liberal presidents [[e:policarpo-bonilla|Policarpo Bonilla]] of [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]], [[e:jose-santos-zelaya|José Santos Zelaya]] of [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] and [[e:rafael-antonio-gutierrez|Rafael Antonio Gutiérrez]] of [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]] signed the Pact of [[e:amapala|Amapala]] in June 1896, creating the Greater Republic of [[e:central-america|Central America]]. [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]] and [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]] were invited but stayed out.
greater-republic-of-central-america.r: The union was a confederation in which each state kept its internal government. A Diet of delegates, meeting at the Honduran island port of [[e:amapala|Amapala]], handled foreign affairs and was recognised by the [[s:united-states|United States]]. In 1898 a constitution converted it into a federation called the [[e:united-states|United States]] of [[e:central-america|Central America]], due to take effect on 1 November 1898.
greater-republic-of-central-america.e: Within days, General [[e:tomas-regalado|Tomás Regalado]] seized power in [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]] and withdrew it from the union, which then dissolved in late 1898. The episode showed how fragile the unionist ideal had become; another attempt followed with the [[s:federation-of-central-america-1921-1922|Federation of Central America]] in 1921.

gutian-rule.t: The period when the Gutians, a mountain people of the Zagros, dominated parts of Mesopotamia after the fall of Akkad, later remembered as an age of chaos.
gutian-rule.o: The [[e:gutians|Gutians]] came from the central [[e:zagros-mountains|Zagros]] and raided the plains as the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]] weakened. After the death of Shar-kali-sharri around 2154 BCE they took control of much of [[e:akkad|Akkad]] and northern [[e:sumer|Sumer]], and the [[e:sumerian-king-list|Sumerian King List]] gives about 21 Gutian kings reigning for around a century, though many reigns were short.
gutian-rule.r: Gutian rule was loose and patchy. Some kings, such as [[e:erridupizir|Erridupizir]], left Akkadian inscriptions at [[s:nippur|Nippur]] imitating Akkadian royal style, but southern cities like [[s:lagash|Lagash]] under [[e:gudea|Gudea]] and Ur and [[s:uruk|Uruk]] carried on largely independently. Their language is almost unknown. Later Mesopotamian texts, such as the [[e:curse-of-agade|Curse of Agade]], portrayed the [[e:gutians|Gutians]] as barbarians sent by the gods to punish [[e:akkad|Akkad]].
gutian-rule.e: Around 2119 BCE [[e:utu-hengal|Utu-hengal]] of [[s:uruk|Uruk]] defeated the last Gutian king, [[e:tirigan|Tirigan]], and expelled the [[e:gutians|Gutians]]. [[e:ur-nammu|Ur-Nammu]] soon founded the [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]]. 'Gutian' became a general term for eastern highlanders in later Mesopotamian writing.

gwandu-emirate.t: The western capital of the Sokoto Caliphate, ruled by the family of Abdullahi dan Fodio and overseeing the emirates of the west.
gwandu-emirate.o: After the victory of the [[e:jihad|jihad]], [[e:usman-dan-fodio|Usman dan Fodio]] divided responsibility for his realm around 1812: his son [[e:muhammad-bello|Muhammad Bello]] took the east from [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]], while his brother [[e:abdullahi-dan-fodio|Abdullahi dan Fodio]] took the west from Gwandu, a town he had fortified in 1808. Abdullahi, a respected scholar and poet, ruled until his death in 1829.
gwandu-emirate.r: Gwandu ranked second to [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]] and supervised [[e:emirate|emirates]] such as [[s:ilorin-emirate|Ilorin]], [[e:nupe-kingdom|Nupe]], [[s:emirate-of-liptako|Liptako]] and the lands of the [[s:dendi-kingdom|Dendi kingdom]], receiving their tribute. Its rulers were scholars as well as administrators, and the emirate fought long wars with the [[e:hausa|Hausa]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-kebbi|Kingdom of Kebbi]], who built the rival [[s:argungu-emirate|Argungu Emirate]]. Abdullahi's son Khalilu ruled from 1833 to 1858.
gwandu-emirate.e: British forces occupied Gwandu in 1903, and the Anglo-French boundary split its lands. The Nigerian part became an [[e:emirate|emirate]] in [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Northern Nigeria]], and the [[e:emir|Emir]] of Gwandu still reigns in [[s:kingdom-of-kebbi|Kebbi]] State.

great-perm.t: A Komi principality on the upper Kama, Christianised by Saint Stephen of Perm and absorbed into Muscovy in 1505.
great-perm.o: The [[e:komi-permyaks|Komi-Permyak]] lands on the upper [[e:kama-river|Kama]] were long a source of [[e:fur-trade|furs]] for [[e:veliky-novgorod|Novgorod]]. In the late 14th century [[e:stephen-of-perm|Saint Stephen of Perm]] converted many of the [[e:komi-peoples|Komi]] and created the Old Permic alphabet for their language. By the mid 15th century the land was ruled by local princes dependent on [[e:moscow|Moscow]], with [[e:cherdyn|Cherdyn]] as their centre.
great-perm.r: Great Perm was a land of forests, fur trapping and salt, linking the Russian north with the [[e:ural-mountains|Urals]] and [[e:siberia|Siberia]]. Its princes, such as [[e:mikhail-ermolaevich|Mikhail Ermolaevich]], were baptised and served the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]] while ruling local communities. In 1472 [[e:ivan-iii|Ivan III]] sent an army that took [[e:cherdyn|Cherdyn]] and tightened [[e:moscow|Moscow's]] control.
great-perm.e: Local princely rule lasted until 1505, when [[e:moscow|Moscow]] replaced Prince Matvey Mikhailovich with its own governor. The region became a base for the [[e:stroganov-family|Stroganov family]] and for Russian expansion across the [[e:ural-mountains|Urals]] into [[e:siberia|Siberia]].

golconda-sultanate.t: The Qutb Shahi sultanate of the eastern Deccan, founder of Hyderabad and the Charminar, enriched by the world-famous Golconda diamonds.
golconda-sultanate.o: [[e:quli-qutb-mulk|Sultan Quli]], a [[e:turkmen|Turkmen]] noble from [[e:hamadan|Hamadan]] in [[e:persia|Persia]], served the [[s:bahmani-sultanate|Bahmani Sultanate]] as governor of [[e:telangana|Telangana]]. As Bahmani authority collapsed he ruled independently from the fort of [[e:golconda-fort|Golconda]] from 1518, founding the [[e:qutb-shahi-dynasty|Qutb Shahi dynasty]], which formally adopted the royal title under his successors.
golconda-sultanate.r: The [[e:qutb-shahi-dynasty|Qutb Shahs]] were Shia Muslims who governed a largely [[e:telugu-language|Telugu]]-speaking population and patronised Telugu as well as Persian and Dakhini literature. [[e:muhammad-quli-qutb-shah|Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah]] founded [[e:hyderabad|Hyderabad]] in 1591 and built the [[e:charminar|Charminar]]. [[e:golconda-fort|Golconda]] was famous for its diamond mines, which produced the [[e:koh-i-noor|Koh-i-Noor]], and for [[e:cotton|cotton]] textiles exported from [[e:machilipatnam|Masulipatnam]].
golconda-sultanate.e: The [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]] forced the [[e:qutb-shahi-dynasty|Qutb Shahs]] into tribute in 1636. [[e:aurangzeb|Aurangzeb]] besieged [[e:golconda-fort|Golconda]] for eight months and took it by treachery in 1687, imprisoning the last sultan, [[e:abul-hasan-qutb-shah|Abul Hasan Tana Shah]]. [[e:hyderabad|Hyderabad]] later became the capital of the [[e:nizam-of-hyderabad|Nizams]].

grand-duchy-of-frankfurt.t: Napoleonic grand duchy centred on Frankfurt, created for Karl Theodor von Dalberg and destined for Napoleon's stepson.
grand-duchy-of-frankfurt.o: In 1810 [[e:karl-theodor-von-dalberg|Dalberg]] ceded [[s:free-imperial-city-of-regensburg|Regensburg]] to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] and in exchange received [[s:county-of-hanau-munzenberg|Hanau]] and Fulda. These were combined with [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]], [[e:aschaffenburg|Aschaffenburg]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-wetzlar|Wetzlar]] to form the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt, with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] stepson [[e:eugene-de-beauharnais|Eugène de Beauharnais]] named as Dalberg's successor.
grand-duchy-of-frankfurt.r: The grand duchy was divided into four [[e:departement|departments]] on the French model. A constitution of 1810 introduced the [[e:napoleonic-code|Napoleonic Code]] and equal rights, and the [[e:jews|Jews]] of [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] bought their civic equality in 1811. Frankfurt remained a major trading and banking centre, but the [[e:continental-system|Continental System]] hurt trade and the state had to provide troops for [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]].
grand-duchy-of-frankfurt.e: After the battle of [[e:leipzig|Leipzig]] [[e:karl-theodor-von-dalberg|Dalberg]] abdicated in October 1813, and [[e:eugene-de-beauharnais|Eugène]] never succeeded. The allies placed it under provisional administration; [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] became a free city, while [[s:county-of-hanau-munzenberg|Hanau]] and [[e:fulda|Fulda]] went to the [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Electorate of Hesse]] and [[e:aschaffenburg|Aschaffenburg]] to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]].

grand-duchy-of-berg.t: Napoleonic model state on the lower Rhine, ruled first by Joachim Murat and used to spread French law in Germany.
grand-duchy-of-berg.o: The [[s:duchy-of-berg|Duchy of Berg]] on the right bank of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] belonged to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]], which ceded it to [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] in 1806. He combined it with [[e:kleve|Cleves]] and other lands and gave it to his brother-in-law [[e:joachim-murat|Joachim Murat]] as the Grand Duchy of Berg, with [[e:dusseldorf|Düsseldorf]] as capital.
grand-duchy-of-berg.r: When [[e:joachim-murat|Murat]] became King of [[e:naples|Naples]] in 1808, [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] ruled Berg himself on behalf of his young nephew [[e:napoleon-louis-bonaparte|Napoleon Louis]]. The grand duchy was organised in French-style [[e:departement|departments]], abolished [[e:serfdom|serfdom]] and introduced the [[e:napoleonic-code|Napoleonic Code]]. The industrial region of [[e:elberfeld|Elberfeld]] and [[e:barmen|Barmen]], with textile and metal trades, suffered from the [[e:continental-system|Continental System]], which cut it off from British markets, and conscription led to riots in 1813.
grand-duchy-of-berg.e: After [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] defeat at [[e:leipzig|Leipzig]], allied troops took Berg in late 1813. It was placed under provisional administration, and in 1815 the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] gave it to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] as part of the [[e:rhine-province|Rhine Province]].

german-east-africa.t: Germany's largest colony, covering mainland Tanzania, Rwanda and Burundi, the scene of the Maji Maji war and a long First World War campaign.
german-east-africa.o: In 1884 [[e:carl-peters|Carl Peters]] made treaties with chiefs inland from the [[s:sultanate-of-zanzibar|Zanzibar]] coast, and in 1885 the [[e:german-east-africa-company|German East Africa Company]] received an imperial charter. The coastal Abushiri revolt of 1888 to 1889 against the company forced the German state to intervene under [[e:hermann-von-wissmann|Hermann von Wissmann]], and in 1891 the territory became a crown colony with its capital at [[e:dar-es-salaam|Dar es Salaam]].
german-east-africa.r: German rule relied on military stations, African soldiers (askari), coastal officials called akida and taxes paid in cash or labour. Settlers and plantations grew sisal, [[e:cotton|cotton]] and [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]], and the Central Railway linked [[e:dar-es-salaam|Dar es Salaam]] to [[e:lake-tanganyika|Lake Tanganyika]]. Forced cotton growing provoked the Maji Maji rebellion of 1905 to 1907, crushed with famine tactics; estimates of the dead range from about 75,000 to 300,000.
german-east-africa.e: In the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] [[e:paul-von-lettow-vorbeck|Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck's]] forces fought a long [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] campaign. By the [[e:treaty-of-versailles|Treaty of Versailles]] the colony was divided: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] received [[s:tanganyika-territory|Tanganyika Territory]], [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]] took [[s:ruanda-urundi|Ruanda-Urundi]] and Portugal the small [[e:kionga-triangle|Kionga Triangle]].

governorate-of-new-castile.t: The Spanish governorate granted to Francisco Pizarro, under which the conquest of the Inca Empire took place and Lima was founded.
governorate-of-new-castile.o: By the Capitulation of [[e:toledo|Toledo]] in 1529, [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] named [[e:francisco-pizarro|Francisco Pizarro]] governor and captain-general of New Castile, a strip extending 200 leagues south from the [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] river in [[s:republic-of-ecuador|Ecuador]]. Pizarro sailed from [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]] in 1530 and began the conquest of the [[s:inca-empire|Inca Empire]], capturing [[e:atahualpa|Atahualpa]] at [[e:cajamarca|Cajamarca]] in 1532.
governorate-of-new-castile.r: New Castile was governed by [[e:francisco-pizarro|Pizarro]] with his brothers [[e:hernando-pizarro|Hernando]], Gonzalo and Juan. He founded [[e:piura|San Miguel de Piura]] in 1532 and the City of the Kings, [[e:lima|Lima]], in 1535. Lands and native people were divided into [[e:encomienda|encomiendas]] among the conquerors. The boundary with [[e:diego-de-almagro|Diego de Almagro's]] [[s:governorate-of-new-toledo|Governorate of New Toledo]], especially the possession of [[e:cusco|Cusco]], led to civil war, and Almagro was executed in 1538.
governorate-of-new-castile.e: [[e:diego-de-almagro|Almagro]]'s followers assassinated [[e:francisco-pizarro|Pizarro]] in [[e:lima|Lima]] in 1541. In 1542 the [[e:new-laws|New Laws]] created the [[s:viceroyalty-of-peru|Viceroyalty of Peru]], which absorbed New Castile and [[e:governorate-of-new-toledo|New Toledo]] under a [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]]. Lima remained the capital of Spanish [[e:south-america|South America]] for nearly three centuries.

gabali.t: Mountain people of the Lozère, clients of the Arverni, who gave their name to the Gévaudan.
gabali.o: The Gabali lived on the granite plateaus and valleys of the southern [[e:massif-central|Massif Central]], in the modern [[e:lozere|Lozère]]. Caesar names them as clients of the [[s:arverni|Arverni]].
gabali.r: [[e:strabo|Strabo]] mentions their [[e:silver|silver]] mines, and [[e:pliny-the-elder|Pliny]] praises the cheese of their district, which was sold in [[e:rome|Rome]]. No rulers or institutions are recorded.
gabali.e: They took part in the revolt of [[e:vercingetorix|Vercingetorix]] in 52 BCE, attacking the [[s:helvii|Helvii]] on the border of the Province. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their chief town was [[e:javols|Anderitum]] (Javols), and their name lived on in the medieval county and bishopric of [[e:gevaudan|Gévaudan]].

geshur.t: Geshur, a small Aramaean kingdom on the north-east shore of the Sea of Galilee, tied by marriage to King David.
geshur.o: Geshur occupied the southern [[e:golan-heights|Golan]] and the north-eastern shore of the [[e:sea-of-galilee|Sea of Galilee]]. It appears in the [[e:hebrew-bible|Hebrew Bible]] as an Aramaean kingdom of the 10th century BCE, and excavations at [[e:bethsaida|Bethsaida]] and Tel Hadar have revealed fortified towns of the period.
geshur.r: [[e:bethsaida|Bethsaida]] had a large city gate with a stele showing a bull-headed god. According to the [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]], King Talmai of Geshur gave his daughter [[s:aram-maacah|Maacah]] in marriage to [[e:david|David]] of the [[s:united-kingdom-of-israel|United Kingdom of Israel]]; their son [[e:absalom|Absalom]] later took refuge in Geshur.
geshur.e: Geshur disappears from records in the 9th century BCE, probably absorbed by [[s:aram-damascus|Aram-Damascus]].

gaoche.t: A kingdom of the Tiele 'high cart' tribes north-west of Turpan, which broke away from the Rouran in 487 and fought them for half a century.
gaoche.o: The Gaoche, named by the Chinese for their high-wheeled carts, were Turkic-speaking [[e:tiele|Tiele]] tribes. In 487 their leader Afuzhiluo refused to join a [[s:rouran-khaganate|Rouran Khaganate]] campaign and led some 100,000 households west to [[s:dzungar-khanate|Dzungaria]], north-west of [[e:turfan|Turpan]], where he proclaimed an independent kingdom.
gaoche.r: The Gaoche were nomadic herders organised in clans under a king. They allied with the [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] against their common enemy the [[s:rouran-khaganate|Rouran]], and competed for control of [[e:turfan|Turpan]] and the oasis routes. The [[s:hephthalite-empire|Hephthalites]] intervened in their succession disputes, installing rulers of their choosing.
gaoche.e: After decades of war, the [[s:rouran-khaganate|Rouran]] killed the Gaoche king Mi'etu in 516, and around 541 they finally destroyed the kingdom. The [[e:tiele|Tiele]] tribes later came under the [[s:gokturk-empire|Gokturk Empire]], and groups descended from them included the [[e:uyghurs|Uyghurs]].

golden-horde.t: The Mongol khanate of the western steppe that ruled the Rus' principalities for over two centuries and grew rich on trade from Sarai.
golden-horde.o: Founded by [[e:batu-khan|Batu]], son of Jochi, after the great western campaign of 1236 to 1242, the khanate took the steppe from the [[e:danube|Danube]] to the [[e:irtysh|Irtysh]], with [[e:sarai|Sarai]] on the lower [[e:volga|Volga]] as its capital. It ruled the conquered Rus' principalities through tribute and the grant of patents to princes.
golden-horde.r: Its khans ruled a largely [[e:kipchak-languages|Kipchak Turkic]] population, and Mongol rule merged into Turkic culture. [[e:uzbek-khan|Uzbek Khan]] made [[e:islam|Islam]] the state religion in the early 14th century. [[e:sarai|Sarai]] became a large trading city on routes linking the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]], Genoese [[e:crimea|Crimea]], [[e:central-asia|Central Asia]] and [[e:egypt|Egypt's]] [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]]. The khans collected Rus' tribute through Muscovite grand princes.
golden-horde.e: From the 1360s civil war, the '[[e:great-troubles|Great Troubles]]', and [[e:timur|Timur's]] campaigns against [[e:tokhtamysh|Tokhtamysh]] in 1395 wrecked its economy. It broke into the [[s:khanate-of-kazan|Khanate of Kazan]], the Crimean and [[e:astrakhan-khanate|Astrakhan Khanates]] and the [[s:great-horde|Great Horde]], and [[e:moscow|Moscow]] ended tribute after 1480.

grand-duchy-of-luxembourg.t: The world's only remaining grand duchy, created in 1815 and grown from a fortress state into a founding member of the European Union and a financial centre.
grand-duchy-of-luxembourg.o: The [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] made the former [[s:county-of-luxembourg|Duchy of Luxembourg]] a grand duchy, held by [[e:william-i-of-the-netherlands|William I of the Netherlands]] in personal union and a member of the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]], with a Prussian garrison in its fortress. After the Belgian Revolution, the [[e:treaty-of-london-1839|Treaty of London]] of 1839 gave its French-speaking western half to [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]].
grand-duchy-of-luxembourg.r: The [[e:treaty-of-london-1867|Treaty of London]] of 1867 made [[s:county-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]] permanently neutral and its fortress was demolished. Personal union with the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]] ended in 1890, when [[e:adolphe-grand-duke-of-luxembourg|Adolphe of Nassau-Weilburg]] became grand duke. [[e:steel|Steel]], based on local iron ore, made the country prosperous. [[e:germany|Germany]] occupied it in both world wars, and [[e:charlotte-grand-duchess-of-luxembourg|Grand Duchess Charlotte]] led resistance from exile.
grand-duchy-of-luxembourg.e: After 1945 [[s:county-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]] abandoned neutrality, co-founding [[e:benelux|Benelux]], [[e:nato|NATO]] and the [[e:european-communities|European Communities]] and hosting European institutions. As [[e:steel|steel]] declined it became a banking and investment centre. It remains a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]]; Grand Duke [[e:guillaume-grand-duke-of-luxembourg|Guillaume]] succeeded his father Henri in 2025.

genoese-pera.t: The Genoese colony of Galata across the Golden Horn from Constantinople, a merchant republic whose trade outstripped the Byzantine capital itself.
genoese-pera.o: The [[e:treaty-of-nymphaeum-1261|Treaty of Nymphaeum]] of 1261 rewarded [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] for helping [[e:michael-viii-palaiologos|Michael VIII Palaiologos]], and in 1267 the emperor granted the Genoese the suburb of [[e:galata|Pera]], or Galata, on the north side of the [[e:golden-horn|Golden Horn]].
genoese-pera.r: [[e:galata|Pera]] was governed by a podesta sent from [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]], with its own councils and courts. It grew into the hub of Genoese trade with the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] colonies such as [[s:genoese-gazaria|Caffa]], dealing in grain, slaves, alum and [[e:silk|silk]], and by the 14th century its customs revenues far exceeded those of [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]]. The Genoese walled the town and in 1348 built the [[e:galata-tower|Tower of Christ]], now the Galata Tower, and fought the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] and [[e:venice|Venetians]] for control of the straits.
genoese-pera.e: During the siege of 1453 [[e:galata|Pera]] stayed officially neutral. After [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] fell it surrendered to [[e:mehmed-ii|Mehmed II]], who guaranteed its residents' property and religion but dismantled its walls; Galata remained a centre of the European community.

gilbert-and-ellice-islands.t: A British protectorate and colony uniting the Micronesian Gilbert and Polynesian Ellice islands, later divided into Kiribati and Tuvalu.
gilbert-and-ellice-islands.o: In 1892 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] declared [[e:protectorate|protectorates]] over the [[e:gilbert-islands|Gilbert Islands]], including the [[s:kingdom-of-abemama|Kingdom of Abemama]], and the [[e:ellice-islands|Ellice Islands]], to forestall other powers and regulate the labour trade. Phosphate-rich [[e:banaba|Banaba]] (Ocean Island) was annexed in 1900, and the protectorate was made a colony in 1916, later adding the Line and [[e:phoenix-islands|Phoenix Islands]].
gilbert-and-ellice-islands.r: A resident commissioner governed, from [[e:banaba|Banaba]] between 1908 and 1942 because of the phosphate mines, which enriched the British [[e:phosphate|Phosphate]] Commissioners while devastating Banaban land. Island councils and colonial regulations replaced older authority, and [[e:arthur-grimble|Arthur Grimble's]] memoirs described the colony's administration. [[e:japan|Japan]] occupied the [[e:humphrey-gilbert|Gilberts]] in 1941; the [[e:battle-of-tarawa|Battle of Tarawa]] in 1943 was among the bloodiest of the [[e:pacific-war|Pacific War]]. [[e:banabans|Banabans]] were resettled on [[e:rabi-island|Rabi]] in [[e:fiji|Fiji]] in 1945.
gilbert-and-ellice-islands.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] tested nuclear weapons at [[e:kiritimati|Christmas Island]] from 1957. Cultural differences led the Ellice Islanders to vote for separation in 1974; the split took effect in 1976. [[e:ellice-islands|Tuvalu]] became independent in 1978 and the [[e:humphrey-gilbert|Gilberts]], as [[e:kiribati|Kiribati]], in 1979.

goryeong-gaya.t: One of the six Gaya polities named in Korean legend, of uncertain location and known almost entirely from later tradition.
goryeong-gaya.o: [[e:goryeong|Goryeong]] Gaya appears in the 13th-century [[e:samguk-yusa|Samguk yusa]] as one of the six Gaya states founded in 42 CE. That text places it at Hamchang, near modern [[e:sangju|Sangju]] in [[e:north-gyeongsang-province|North Gyeongsang]], though some scholars doubt the identification.
goryeong-gaya.r: Known only from brief mentions in late sources, nothing reliable is recorded of its rulers or institutions. It should not be confused with [[s:daegaya|Daegaya]], whose capital was at the modern town of [[e:goryeong|Goryeong]].
goryeong-gaya.e: Like other Gaya polities it was absorbed by [[s:silla|Silla]], probably by the 6th century.

giri-kedaton.t: A line of Muslim priest-kings near Gresik in East Java, whose spiritual authority reached from Lombok to the Moluccas.
giri-kedaton.o: [[e:sunan-giri|Sunan Giri]], born Raden Paku and counted among the [[e:wali-songo|Wali Songo]], founded a religious school on the hills of Giri near the port of [[e:gresik|Gresik]] in the late 15th century. His descendants ruled as both religious teachers and princes, with the title Prabu Satmata or Sunan Giri.
giri-kedaton.r: Giri was a centre of Islamic learning that trained students from across the archipelago, including [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:zainal-abidin-of-ternate|Zainal Abidin of Ternate]]. Its leaders blessed the coronation of Javanese rulers and sent preachers to [[e:lombok|Lombok]], [[e:sulawesi|Sulawesi]] and the [[e:maluku-islands|Moluccas]]. [[e:sunan-prapen|Sunan Prapen]], in the 16th century, was its most influential ruler. Its wealth came from pilgrims and [[e:gresik|Gresik's]] trade.
giri-kedaton.e: [[e:sultan-agung|Sultan Agung of Mataram]] conquered Giri in 1636, using [[e:pangeran-pekik|Pangeran Pekik]] of [[s:duchy-of-surabaya|Surabaya]] so as not to fight the saints himself. Giri joined the [[e:trunajaya-rebellion|Trunajaya rebellion]] against [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram]] and was destroyed in 1680 by Mataram and [[e:dutch|Dutch]] forces. The tomb of [[e:sunan-giri|Sunan Giri]] remains a major pilgrimage site.

gadwal-samasthan.t: A Telugu samasthan between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, under the Nizams of Hyderabad, famed for its woven saris.
gadwal-samasthan.o: Gadwal was established around 1663 by [[e:pedda-soma-bhupal|Pedda Soma Bhupal]], a local chief who built the fort at Gadwal in the land between the [[e:krishna|Krishna]] and [[e:tungabhadra-river|Tungabhadra]]. His family held it under the [[s:golconda-sultanate|Qutb Shahis]], the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]] and then the [[e:nizam-of-hyderabad|Nizams]].
gadwal-samasthan.r: As a samasthan within [[s:hyderabad-state|Hyderabad State]], Gadwal paid tribute to the Nizam but was ruled internally by its Rajas and Ranis. The court patronised Telugu and [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] scholarship, and the town's weavers developed the [[e:cotton|cotton]]-and-[[e:silk|silk]] Gadwal sari.
gadwal-samasthan.e: With the integration of Hyderabad into [[e:india|India]] in 1948 and the abolition of samasthans, Gadwal ceased to exist. The town lies in [[e:jogulamba-gadwal-district|Jogulamba Gadwal district]] of [[e:telangana|Telangana]].

guler-state.t: An offshoot of the Katoch kingdom of Kangra whose small court at Haripur nurtured the painters Pandit Seu, Manaku and Nainsukh, founders of later Pahari painting.
guler-state.o: Tradition holds that around 1405 [[e:hari-chand-of-guler|Hari Chand]], heir to [[s:kangra-state|Kangra State]], fell into a well while hunting and was presumed dead; his brother took the throne, and on his rescue Hari Chand founded a new state with its capital at Haripur, in the Guler area.
guler-state.r: Guler was a small state, but its Rajas, especially [[e:govardhan-chand|Govardhan Chand]] in the mid-18th century, patronised a family of painters led by [[e:pandit-seu|Pandit Seu]] and his sons [[e:manaku|Manaku]] and [[e:nainsukh|Nainsukh]]. Their naturalistic style, known as Guler painting, shaped the later [[s:kangra-state|Kangra]] school. The state was often dominated by Kangra and by Mughal governors in the plains.
guler-state.e: [[e:ranjit-singh|Ranjit Singh]] annexed Guler to the [[s:sikh-empire|Sikh Empire]] in 1813, leaving the family a [[e:jagir|jagir]], which the British confirmed after 1846. The area is now in [[s:kangra-state|Kangra]] district, [[e:himachal-pradesh|Himachal Pradesh]].

gurgum.t: Gurgum, a Neo-Hittite kingdom centred on Maraş, whose kings left Luwian inscriptions and lion sculptures before Assyria annexed it.
gurgum.o: Gurgum arose after the Hittite collapse in the valley of the [[e:aksu|Aksu]] river around [[e:kahramanmaras|Marqas]], modern Kahramanmaraş, in south-eastern [[e:turkey|Turkey]]. A local dynasty ruled it from the 10th century BCE or earlier.
gurgum.r: Its kings, several called Halparuntiya, left Luwian hieroglyphic inscriptions on stelae and lion statues recording their family line and building works. Gurgum joined alliances with [[s:samal|Sam'al]] and [[s:bit-agusi|Arpad]] against the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] and paid tribute to it as circumstances required.
gurgum.e: King Tarhulara was murdered by his son Mutallu. In 711 BCE [[e:sargon-ii|Sargon II]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] deposed Mutallu and annexed Gurgum as the province of Marqasi.

grand-principality-of-transylvania.t: Habsburg crown land of Transylvania, where Hungarian, Saxon, Székely and Romanian communities contested rights until its union with Hungary in 1867.
grand-principality-of-transylvania.o: After the [[e:peace-of-szatmar|Peace of Szatmár]] in 1711 ended [[e:francis-ii-rakoczi|Francis II Rákóczi's]] revolt, [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] was governed directly by the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] as a separate land of the [[e:lands-of-the-crown-of-saint-stephen|Hungarian Crown]], under the [[e:leopoldine-diploma|Leopoldine Diploma]] of 1691. In 1765 [[e:maria-theresa|Maria Theresa]] raised it to the rank of grand principality, and the [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] ruler took the title of grand prince.
grand-principality-of-transylvania.r: A gubernium answering to [[e:vienna|Vienna]] ran the land, sitting at [[e:sibiu|Hermannstadt]] for much of the 18th century, with governors such as the [[e:saxons|Saxon]] [[e:samuel-von-brukenthal|Samuel von Brukenthal]]. The old system of three privileged nations persisted, leaving the Romanian majority without political rights, though the union of many [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] [[e:romanians|Romanians]] with [[e:rome|Rome]] around 1700 opened schools at [[e:blaj|Blaj]]. [[e:horea|Horea's]] peasant revolt of 1784 was bloodily suppressed.
grand-principality-of-transylvania.e: In 1848 Hungarian revolutionaries proclaimed union with [[e:hungary|Hungary]] while [[e:romanians|Romanians]] at [[e:blaj|Blaj]] demanded national rights, and civil war followed. After 1849 [[s:principality-of-transylvania|Transylvania]] was again a separate crown land, until the [[e:austro-hungarian-compromise-of-1867|Compromise of 1867]] merged it into the [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1526-1867|Kingdom of Hungary]] (1867-1918). It joined [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]] in 1918.
grand-principality-of-transylvania.re: Orthodox, Greek Catholic, Catholic and Protestant Christianity

guiyi-circuit.t: The self-governing Chinese regime at Dunhuang that threw off Tibetan rule in 848 and whose rulers sponsored many of the Mogao caves and their famous manuscripts.
guiyi-circuit.o: In 848, as the [[s:tibetan-empire|Tibetan Empire]] disintegrated, the local leader [[e:zhang-yichao|Zhang Yichao]] drove the Tibetan garrison out of [[e:dunhuang|Dunhuang]] (Shazhou) and soon of other [[e:gansu-corridor|Hexi Corridor]] towns. He sent envoys to the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] court, which in 851 recognised him as military governor of the Guiyi ('Return to Allegiance') Army.
guiyi-circuit.r: Though nominally a [[s:later-tang|Tang]] and later [[e:five-dynasties-and-ten-kingdoms-period|Five Dynasties]] province, it was a hereditary oasis state, first under the Zhang family and from 914 under the Cao family, who married into the Khotanese and [[e:uyghurs|Uyghur]] royal houses. Its rulers financed cave temples at [[e:mogao-caves|Mogao]], and its monasteries produced the [[e:dunhuang|Dunhuang]] [[e:manuscript|manuscripts]] in Chinese, Tibetan, Khotanese, Sogdian and Uyghur. Neighbours such as the [[s:ganzhou-uyghur-kingdom|Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom]] often threatened it.
guiyi-circuit.e: Cao rule weakened in the early 11th century, and around 1036 the [[s:western-xia|Western Xia]] took [[e:dunhuang|Dunhuang]]; the details of the final years are debated. The cave library, sealed around this time, was rediscovered in 1900.

grand-duchy-of-baden.t: South-western German grand duchy known for its liberal constitution, its revolutionaries of 1848-49 and its role as a model constitutional state.
grand-duchy-of-baden.o: Elector [[e:charles-frederick-grand-duke-of-baden|Charles Frederick]] of [[e:baden|Baden]] joined the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] in 1806 and became grand duke, gaining Austrian [[e:breisgau|Breisgau]], mediatised lands and the [[e:lake-constance|Lake Constance]] region. His long, narrow state stretched from [[e:mannheim|Mannheim]] to [[e:konstanz|Constance]] along the [[e:rhine|Rhine]].
grand-duchy-of-baden.r: The constitution of 1818 created one of the most liberal parliaments in [[e:germany|Germany]]. The [[e:baden|Baden]] revolutionaries of 1848, led by [[e:friedrich-hecker|Friedrich Hecker]] and [[e:gustav-struve|Gustav Struve]], were defeated, and in 1849 the army mutinied and the grand duke fled until Prussian troops restored him. Under [[e:frederick-i-grand-duke-of-baden|Frederick I]], from 1856, Baden became a liberal model state. Universities at [[e:heidelberg|Heidelberg]] and [[e:freiburg-im-breisgau|Freiburg]] and industry at [[e:mannheim|Mannheim]] and [[e:karlsruhe|Karlsruhe]] flourished.
grand-duchy-of-baden.e: [[e:baden|Baden]] sided with [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1866 but joined the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] in 1871. [[e:frederick-ii-grand-duke-of-baden|Grand Duke Frederick II]] abdicated in November 1918, and the state became the [[s:republic-of-baden|Republic of Baden]].

ghurid-sultanate.t: A dynasty from the mountains of Ghor in central Afghanistan that built the Minaret of Jam and laid the foundations of Muslim rule in northern India.
ghurid-sultanate.o: The Shansabani chiefs of [[e:ghor|Ghor]], an isolated mountain region, were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:ghaznavid-empire|Ghaznavids]] and [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]]. In 1150 [[e:ala-al-din-husayn|Ala al-Din Husayn]] sacked [[e:ghazni|Ghazni]], earning the name 'World Burner', and his nephews made Ghor an empire in the late 12th century.
ghurid-sultanate.r: The brothers [[e:ghiyath-al-din-muhammad|Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad]], ruling from [[e:firozkoh|Firozkoh]] and [[e:herat|Herat]], and [[e:muhammad-of-ghor|Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad of Ghor]], ruling from [[e:ghazni|Ghazni]], divided their conquests. Ghiyath al-Din built the [[e:minaret-of-jam|Minaret of Jam]] and the Herat mosque. Mu'izz al-Din defeated the [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] [[e:prithviraj-chauhan|Prithviraj Chauhan]] at [[e:second-battle-of-tarain|Tarain]] in 1192 and conquered northern [[e:india|India]], leaving Turkic slave commanders such as Qutb al-Din [[e:aybak|Aybak]] in charge.
ghurid-sultanate.e: After [[e:muhammad-of-ghor|Mu'izz al-Din]]'s murder in 1206 the empire fragmented. [[e:aybak|Aybak]] founded the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]], and the [[s:khwarazmian-empire|Khwarazmian Empire]] conquered [[e:ghor|Ghor]] and [[e:ghazni|Ghazni]] by 1215.

gela.t: Rhodian and Cretan colony on Sicily's south coast whose tyrants, Hippocrates and Gelon, built the first great Greek power on the island.
gela.o: Colonists from [[s:lindos|Lindos]] on [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]] and from [[e:crete|Crete]], led by Antiphemus and Entimus, founded Gela around 689 BCE on a long ridge by the Gela river, inland of a sandy coast. The colony pushed into the [[e:sicels|Sicel]] interior and in 580 BCE founded [[s:acragas|Acragas]] to the west.
gela.r: Gela reached its peak under the tyrants Cleander and [[e:hippocrates-of-gela|Hippocrates]], who around 495 BCE dominated much of eastern [[e:sicily|Sicily]], and under [[e:gelon|Gelon]], who seized [[s:syracuse|Syracuse]] in 485 BCE and moved half of Gela's people there. Its farmland produced grain and horses, and its terracotta workshops and coins with a man-headed bull were renowned. The playwright [[e:aeschylus|Aeschylus]] died there in 456 BCE.
gela.e: [[e:carthage|Carthage]] sacked Gela in 405 BCE. [[e:timoleon|Timoleon]] resettled it in the 330s BCE, but in 282 BCE [[e:phintias-of-acragas|Phintias]], tyrant of [[s:acragas|Acragas]], destroyed it and moved its people to his new city at [[e:licata|Licata]]. The site was refounded by Frederick II in 1233 as Terranova, renamed Gela in 1927.

gaetuli.t: Berber pastoral peoples of the Saharan fringe south of Numidia and Mauretania, feared by Rome as raiders and prized as cavalry.
gaetuli.o: The Gaetuli are known from Roman writers such as [[e:sallust|Sallust]] and [[e:strabo|Strabo]], who used the name for the nomadic and semi-nomadic [[e:berbers|Berber]] peoples living along the Saharan [[e:atlas-mountains|Atlas]], from southern [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Morocco]] to southern [[e:tunisia|Tunisia]]. They appear in the record from the 2nd century BCE.
gaetuli.r: They had no single government but lived in tribes under chiefs, herding horses, sheep and goats and moving with the seasons. They served as cavalry for [[e:jugurtha|Jugurtha]] and for [[e:julius-caesar|Julius Caesar]], and some received Roman citizenship. Gaetulian purple dye from the Atlantic coast was prized in [[e:rome|Rome]]. They paid tribute to the [[s:kingdom-of-mauretania|Kingdom of Mauretania]].
gaetuli.e: Around 6 CE they rebelled against [[e:juba-ii|Juba II]] and were defeated by [[e:cossus-cornelius-lentulus|Cossus Cornelius Lentulus]], who took the title Gaetulicus. In later centuries the name faded, and the peoples it described merged with other [[e:berbers|Berber]] groups of the desert edge.

great-moravia.t: The first major Slavic state in central Europe, where Cyril and Methodius created a Slavic liturgy and alphabet that shaped the Orthodox Slavic world.
great-moravia.o: Around 833 Prince [[e:mojmir-i|Mojmír I]] of the Moravians drove [[e:pribina|Pribina]] out of [[e:nitra|Nitra]] and united the [[e:slavs|Slavs]] north of the middle [[e:danube|Danube]], creating a state centred on the [[e:morava-river|Morava]] valley. Mojmír's successor [[e:rastislav-of-moravia|Rastislav]], installed with East Frankish help in 846, soon turned against [[s:east-francia|East Francia]] and built a strong independent principality.
great-moravia.r: Great [[e:moravia|Moravia's]] power rested on large fortified centres such as [[e:mikulcice|Mikulčice]], [[e:stare-mesto-uherske-hradiste-district|Staré Město]] and [[e:pohansko|Pohansko]], with stone churches and rich graves. In 863 [[e:rastislav-of-moravia|Rastislav]] invited the Byzantine brothers [[e:cyril-and-methodius|Cyril and Methodius]], who created the Glagolitic alphabet and Old Church Slavonic liturgy. Under [[e:svatopluk-i-of-moravia|Svatopluk]] I, the realm expanded into [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]], southern [[e:poland|Poland]] and [[e:pannonia|Pannonia]].
great-moravia.e: After [[e:svatopluk-i-of-moravia|Svatopluk]] died in 894 his sons quarrelled and [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] broke away. [[e:magyars|Magyar]] invasions destroyed Great [[s:margraviate-of-moravia|Moravia]] around 906 to 907; the last mention coincides with the [[e:battle-of-pressburg|Battle of Pressburg]] in 907. Its disciples carried the Slavic liturgy to [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]], while its lands passed to the [[s:duchy-of-bohemia|Duchy of Bohemia]] and [[e:hungary|Hungary]].

gelang-gelang.t: The brief revival of Kediri under Jayakatwang, who killed King Kertanegara of Singhasari in 1292 and was overthrown by Raden Wijaya and a Mongol army.
gelang-gelang.o: [[e:jayakatwang|Jayakatwang]], ruler of Gelang-gelang and a descendant of the kings of the [[s:kediri-kingdom|Kediri Kingdom]], was a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of [[e:kertanegara|Kertanegara of Singhasari]]. In 1292, while [[e:singhasari|Singhasari's]] army was away in [[e:sumatra|Sumatra]], he attacked, killed Kertanegara and restored the old royal seat at Daha. The register names his state after his former fief.
gelang-gelang.r: [[e:jayakatwang|Jayakatwang]] ruled for barely a year. He pardoned [[e:kertanegara|Kertanegara's]] son-in-law [[e:raden-wijaya|Raden Wijaya]], who on the advice of [[e:arya-wiraraja|Arya Wiraraja]] of [[s:kingdom-of-sumenep|Sumenep]] pretended submission and was given land at Tarik, where he founded [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit]].
gelang-gelang.e: In 1293 a Mongol fleet sent by [[e:kublai-khan|Kublai Khan]] to punish [[e:kertanegara|Kertanegara]] landed in [[e:java|Java]]. [[e:raden-wijaya|Raden Wijaya]] joined it, defeated [[e:jayakatwang|Jayakatwang]] at Daha and then turned on the [[e:mongols|Mongols]], driving them out. Jayakatwang died in captivity, and [[e:majapahit-empire|Majapahit]] became the main power in Java.

genoese-famagusta.t: Genoese-held enclave around the great port of Famagusta in Cyprus, seized from the Lusignan kings in 1373 and held for ninety years.
genoese-famagusta.o: At the coronation of King [[e:peter-ii-of-cyprus|Peter II of Cyprus]] in Famagusta in 1372, a dispute over precedence between Genoese and Venetian merchants led to riots in which Genoese were killed. [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] sent a fleet in 1373, invaded the [[s:kingdom-of-cyprus|Kingdom of Cyprus]] and occupied Famagusta, keeping the city as security for a huge indemnity.
genoese-famagusta.r: [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] governed Famagusta through a podesta and officials, and from 1447 through the [[e:bank-of-saint-george|Bank of Saint George]], which ran it as a business. The once-thriving port declined as [[e:genoa|Genoa]] restricted the trade of the rest of the island and [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] and Turkish pressure grew. Many inhabitants left and the economy shrank.
genoese-famagusta.e: King [[e:james-ii-of-cyprus|James II of Cyprus]], with [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] support, besieged Famagusta and recovered it in 1464, reuniting the island under the [[e:house-of-lusignan|Lusignans]]. Its Gothic cathedral of [[e:saint-nicholas|Saint Nicholas]] and walls remain.

goshen.t: A tiny Boer freebooter republic on the Tswana border, whose land grab provoked Britain to take over southern Bechuanaland.
goshen.o: In 1882 white volunteers who had fought for the [[e:barolong|Barolong]] chief Moshette against [[e:montshiwa|Montshiwa]] were rewarded with farms, and they proclaimed the Land Goshen with its headquarters at Rooigrond, near [[e:mahikeng|Mafikeng]]. Its administrator was [[e:gey-van-pittius|Gey van Pittius]].
goshen.r: Goshen had little more than a few hundred settlers, raiding [[e:montshiwa|Montshiwa's]] [[e:cattle|cattle]] and land. It sought union with the [[s:south-african-republic|South African Republic]], which proclaimed a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] in 1884; [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] objected because the territory lay on the 'missionaries' road' to the interior.
goshen.e: The [[e:warren-expedition|Warren Expedition]] of 1884-1885 dispersed the freebooters without a fight, and the land was incorporated into [[s:british-bechuanaland|British Bechuanaland]] in 1885. The affair helped secure [[e:britain|Britain's]] route to the north, later used by [[e:cecil-rhodes|Cecil Rhodes]].

gonanda-dynasty.t: The founding royal line of Kashmir in Kalhana's Rajatarangini, a largely legendary dynasty said to have ruled the valley for centuries before the Karkotas.
gonanda-dynasty.o: Almost everything known about the Gonandas comes from the [[e:rajatarangini|Rajatarangini]], the chronicle of [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] written by [[e:kalhana|Kalhana]] in the 12th century. He made the first king, Gonanda I, a contemporary of the [[e:mahabharata|Mahabharata]] war and listed dozens of successors in a chronology that modern historians consider largely unreliable. The early kings cannot be confirmed by inscriptions or coins.
gonanda-dynasty.r: [[e:kalhana|Kalhana]] presents [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] as a [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] kingdom in the [[e:jhelum|Jhelum]] valley whose kings founded towns, temples and Buddhist monasteries. He counts among them an [[e:ashoka|Ashoka]] credited with founding Srinagari, the older capital, and Meghavahana, praised for banning the slaughter of animals. His sequence is interrupted by Turushka kings, apparently the [[s:kushan-empire|Kushans]], and by the Hun ruler [[e:mihirakula|Mihirakula]], so some names may preserve real memories, but history and legend are thoroughly mixed.
gonanda-dynasty.e: According to [[e:kalhana|Kalhana]], the last Gonanda king, Baladitya, died without a son, and his son-in-law [[e:durlabhavardhana|Durlabhavardhana]] founded the [[s:karkota-dynasty|Karkota dynasty]] around 625. From the [[e:karkota-dynasty|Karkotas]] onwards the history of [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] rests on a much firmer chronology.

goryeo.t: The Korean dynasty that reunified the peninsula in the 10th century, gave Korea its Western name and produced celadon, the Tripitaka Koreana and early metal type.
goryeo.o: [[e:taejo-of-goryeo|Wang Geon]], a general of [[s:taebong|Taebong]] from a trading family of [[e:kaesong|Songak]], was raised to the throne in 918 and founded Goryeo, named after [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]]. [[s:silla|Silla]] surrendered in 935 and [[s:later-baekje|Later Baekje]] was conquered in 936, uniting the Later [[e:three-kingdoms-period|Three Kingdoms]], and [[s:balhae|Balhae]] refugees were welcomed.
goryeo.r: Kings ruled from [[e:kaesong|Kaegyong]] through a Chinese-style bureaucracy recruited partly by examinations, introduced by [[e:gwangjong-of-goryeo|Gwangjong]] in 958, while an aristocracy dominated office. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] was the state religion, and the court carved the [[e:tripitaka-koreana|Tripitaka Koreana]] woodblocks. Goryeo repelled the Khitan, winning at [[e:battle-of-gwiju|Gwiju]] in 1019. In 1170 military officers seized power, and from 1231 Mongol invasions made Goryeo a son-in-law [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the Yuan. Its potters perfected inlaid celadon, and the Buddhist text [[e:jikji|Jikji]] was printed with metal type in 1377.
goryeo.e: [[e:gongmin-of-goryeo|King Gongmin]] threw off Yuan control in the 1350s, but reform failed. In 1388 General [[e:taejo-of-joseon|Yi Seong-gye]] turned back an expedition against Ming and seized power, and in 1392 he deposed the last king and founded [[s:joseon|Joseon]].

greco-bactrian-kingdom.t: The easternmost Hellenistic kingdom, where Greek kings ruled Bactria's 'thousand cities' and struck some of the finest coins of the ancient world.
greco-bactrian-kingdom.o: [[e:bactria|Bactria]] was a [[e:satrapy|satrapy]] of the [[s:seleucid-empire|Seleucid Empire]] after [[e:alexander-the-great|Alexander the Great's]] conquest. Around 256 BCE its governor [[e:diodotus-i|Diodotus I]] broke away, and his son [[e:diodotus-ii|Diodotus II]] ruled as an independent king. [[e:euthydemus-i|Euthydemus I]] then seized the throne and withstood a two-year siege of [[e:balkh|Bactra]] by [[e:antiochus-iii-the-great|Antiochus III]], who recognised him as king around 206 BCE.
greco-bactrian-kingdom.r: Greek and Macedonian settlers formed the ruling class over a largely Iranian population, with cities such as [[e:ai-khanoum|Ai-Khanoum]] on the [[e:oxus|Amu Darya]] featuring a [[e:theatre|theatre]], [[e:gymnasium|gymnasium]] and palace in Greek style. Irrigated farming and trade supported the state. Under Demetrius I the kings crossed the [[e:hindu-kush|Hindu Kush]] into [[e:india|India]], founding the [[e:indo-greek-kingdom|Indo-Greek]] kingdoms, while [[e:eucratides-i|Eucratides I]] ruled a vast territory in the 2nd century BCE.
greco-bactrian-kingdom.e: After [[e:eucratides-i|Eucratides]] was murdered around 145 BCE, nomad invasions by the [[s:saka|Saka]] and the [[s:yuezhi|Yuezhi]] overran [[e:bactria|Bactria]], and [[e:ai-khanoum|Ai-Khanoum]] was abandoned. Greek rule continued south of the [[e:hindu-kush|Hindu Kush]] in the [[e:indo-greek-kingdom|Indo-Greek]] kingdoms until about 10 CE, and Greek script lived on in Kushan coinage.

garhwal-kingdom.t: The Himalayan kingdom of the Panwar dynasty, which united the 52 forts of Garhwal and ruled the pilgrim country of the upper Ganges until the Gurkha conquest.
garhwal-kingdom.o: Tradition holds that Kanak Pal founded the Panwar dynasty at Chandpur Garhi in 888. For centuries the region was divided among many small chiefs, each holding a garh (fort). In the 14th or 15th century Raja [[e:ajay-pal|Ajay Pal]] subdued them and united the country, which took its name [[e:garhwal|Garhwal]] from these forts.
garhwal-kingdom.r: [[e:ajay-pal|Ajay Pal]] moved the capital to Devalgarh and then to [[e:srinagar-uttarakhand|Srinagar]] on the [[e:alaknanda|Alaknanda]]. The kingdom controlled the routes to [[e:badrinath|Badrinath]] and [[e:kedarnath|Kedarnath]] and received pilgrims from across [[e:india|India]]. Its Rajas, who used the title Shah from the 16th century, fought with [[e:kumaon|Kumaon]] and the [[e:mughal-empire|Mughals]], and [[e:fateh-shah-of-garhwal|Fateh Shah]] opposed [[e:guru-gobind-singh|Guru Gobind Singh]] at [[e:battle-of-bhangani|Bhangani]] in 1688.
garhwal-kingdom.e: The [[s:gorkha-kingdom|Gorkha]] army of the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]] overran [[e:garhwal|Garhwal]] and killed Raja [[e:pradyumna-shah|Pradyumna Shah]] at Khurbura in 1804. After the [[e:anglo-nepalese-war|Anglo-Nepalese War]] the British kept the eastern half and in 1815 restored his son [[e:sudarshan-shah|Sudarshan Shah]] to the western part, which became [[s:tehri-garhwal-state|Tehri Garhwal State]].

governorate-of-livonia.t: Russian imperial province covering northern Latvia and southern Estonia, home to Riga and the University of Dorpat, where both Latvian and Estonian nationalism took shape.
governorate-of-livonia.o: [[e:russia|Russia]] took [[s:swedish-livonia|Swedish Livonia]] in the [[e:great-northern-war|Great Northern War]]; Riga fell in 1710, and the [[e:treaty-of-nystad|Treaty of Nystad]] in 1721 confirmed the conquest. The new province, at first called the Riga [[e:governorate|Governorate]], covered Latvian [[e:vidzeme|Vidzeme]], southern [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]] and, later, the island of Ösel.
governorate-of-livonia.r: The Livonian knighthood kept control of local government and the Lutheran church under the Baltic special order. [[e:serfdom|Serfdom]] was abolished in 1819. The [[e:university-of-tartu|University of Dorpat]], reopened in 1802, became a centre of [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic German]] and later Estonian learning, and Riga grew into one of the empire's main industrial cities and ports. Latvian and Estonian national movements flourished, and [[e:russification|Russification]] in the 1880s challenged German dominance.
governorate-of-livonia.e: In 1917 its northern part joined the [[s:autonomous-governorate-of-estonia|Autonomous Governorate of Estonia]]. German forces occupied the rest in 1917-1918, and the [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic Germans]] planned the [[s:united-baltic-duchy|United Baltic Duchy]]. After the war the territory was divided between the [[s:republic-of-latvia|Republic of Latvia]] and the [[s:republic-of-estonia|Republic of Estonia]].

gahadavala-dynasty.t: North India's last great Hindu kingdom on the Ganges before the Ghurid conquest, ruling Kannauj and the holy city of Varanasi.
gahadavala-dynasty.o: The Gahadavalas rose in the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]] valley in the late 11th century, filling the vacuum left by the collapse of Pratihara and Kalachuri power. [[e:chandradeva|Chandradeva]] seized [[e:kannauj|Kannauj]] around 1090 and also controlled [[e:varanasi|Varanasi]], [[e:ayodhya|Ayodhya]] and the [[e:ganges-yamuna-doab|Doab]], founding a line that soon dominated the middle Ganges plain.
gahadavala-dynasty.r: The kings issued hundreds of [[e:copper|copper]]-plate land grants to [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]], the main source for the dynasty, and styled themselves protectors of the sacred sites of [[s:kingdom-of-kashi|Kashi]]. [[e:govindachandra-of-the-gahadavala-dynasty|Govindachandra]], the most powerful ruler, fought the Palas and [[e:ghaznavid-empire|Ghaznavid]] raiders and patronised learning; his queen [[e:kumaradevi|Kumaradevi]] endowed a Buddhist monastery at [[e:sarnath|Sarnath]]. Revenue came from the fertile [[e:ganges-yamuna-doab|Doab]], and a special levy, the Turushkadanda, may have funded defence against Turkic incursions.
gahadavala-dynasty.e: [[e:jayachandra|Jayachandra]] was defeated and killed by [[e:muhammad-of-ghor|Muhammad of Ghor]] at the [[e:battle-of-chandawar|Battle of Chandawar]] in 1194, and [[e:kannauj|Kannauj]] and [[e:varanasi|Varanasi]] passed to the [[s:ghurid-sultanate|Ghurids]] and then the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]]. Later [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] clans, including the [[e:rathore|Rathores]], claimed descent from the dynasty.

grey-league.t: The largest of the Three Leagues of the Grisons, a federation of upper Rhine valley communes sworn under a maple tree at Truns in 1424.
grey-league.o: In 1395 the abbot of [[e:disentis-abbey|Disentis]] and local lords of the upper [[e:rhine|Rhine]] valley made an alliance for peace and mutual protection, and in 1424 it was renewed at [[e:trun|Truns]], under a maple tree, as a league that included the communes themselves. The name Grey League is traditionally explained by the grey homespun cloth worn by its people.
grey-league.r: The league joined communes of the [[e:surselva|Surselva]], Hinterrhein and [[e:mesolcina|Mesolcina]] valleys, each with its own courts and assembly, meeting at [[e:ilanz|Ilanz]]. It allied with the [[s:league-of-gods-house|League of God's House]] in 1406 and the [[s:league-of-the-ten-jurisdictions|League of the Ten Jurisdictions]] in 1471, forming the [[s:three-leagues|Three Leagues]], and in 1497 became an associate of the Swiss. Its communes divided between Catholic and Reformed.
grey-league.e: The [[s:three-leagues|Grisons]] became part of the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]] in 1799 and a Swiss canton in 1803. The league's name survives in [[e:graubunden|Graubünden]], the canton's German name.

gambulu.t: An Aramean tribal state in the marshes on the border of Babylonia and Elam, destroyed by Ashurbanipal for siding with the Elamite king Teumman.
gambulu.o: The Gambulu were one of the Aramean tribes that settled in southern [[e:babylonia|Babylonia]] in the early first millennium BCE. They lived in the marshes and canebrakes between the lower [[e:tigris|Tigris]] and the Elamite frontier, with their fortified centre at Sapibel (Shapi-Bel). They are named in Assyrian annals from the reign of Tiglath-Pileser III.
gambulu.r: The tribe was led by sheikhs who used the marshes as natural defences and were courted by both [[e:assyrian-empire|Assyria]] and the [[s:neo-elamite-kingdom|Neo-Elamite kingdom]]. Under [[e:esarhaddon|Esarhaddon]] the chief Bel-iqisha submitted to Assyria and was made a guardian of the frontier. His son Dunanu, however, supported [[e:teumman|Teumman]] of [[e:elam|Elam]].
gambulu.e: After [[e:teumman|Teumman's]] defeat at [[e:battle-of-ulai|Til-Tuba]] around 653 BCE, [[e:ashurbanipal|Ashurbanipal's]] army destroyed Sapibel. Dunanu was taken to [[e:nineveh|Nineveh]] and executed, scenes shown on palace reliefs, and Gambulu disappears as a political unit.

gangani-britain.t: People of the Llŷn peninsula in north-west Wales, known from a headland Ptolemy named after them, with namesakes in western Ireland.
gangani-britain.o: [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 names a Ganganorum Promontorium, the headland of the Gangani, on the coast of north-west [[e:wales|Wales]], generally identified with the tip of the [[e:llyn-peninsula|Llŷn]] peninsula. Ptolemy does not list the Gangani among the inland peoples, so they may have been a small coastal group or a subdivision of the [[s:ordovices|Ordovices]].
gangani-britain.r: Nothing is known of their rulers or society. [[e:llyn-peninsula|Llŷn]] was a land of hillforts such as [[e:trer-ceiri|Tre'r Ceiri]], a stone-walled settlement occupied into the Roman period, and of farming and fishing communities. The identical name in Ireland, borne by the [[s:gangani-ireland|Gangani (Ireland)]] on the [[e:river-shannon|Shannon]], has prompted theories of migration across the [[e:irish-sea|Irish Sea]] in either direction.
gangani-britain.e: The Gangani are not mentioned again. [[e:llyn-peninsula|Llŷn]] later saw Irish settlement in the post-Roman period and became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-gwynedd|Kingdom of Gwynedd]].

governorate-of-estonia.t: Russian imperial province of northern Estonia, governed for nearly two centuries by Baltic German nobles and the setting of the Estonian national awakening.
governorate-of-estonia.o: After [[e:peter-the-great|Peter the Great]] conquered the [[e:swedish-estonia|Swedish Duchy of Estonia]] (1561-1721) in the [[e:great-northern-war|Great Northern War]], the [[e:treaty-of-nystad|Treaty of Nystad]] in 1721 made it a province of the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]], with [[s:reval|Reval]] as its capital. Peter confirmed the privileges of the [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic German]] nobility, their Lutheran church and German as the language of administration.
governorate-of-estonia.r: Under this Baltic special order, the Estonian knighthood ran local government, courts and the land, while Estonian peasants were serfs. [[e:serfdom|Serfdom]] was abolished in 1816, though land remained with the nobles. In the late 19th century an Estonian national movement grew, and the [[e:russification|Russification]] policies of the 1880s replaced German with Russian in schools and courts. [[s:reval|Reval]] became an industrial port and naval base.
governorate-of-estonia.e: After the [[e:february-revolution|February Revolution]] of 1917 the [[s:russian-republic|Russian Provisional Government]] merged the governorate with the Estonian-speaking north of the [[s:governorate-of-livonia|Governorate of Livonia]] to form the [[s:autonomous-governorate-of-estonia|Autonomous Governorate of Estonia]], the forerunner of the [[s:republic-of-estonia|Republic of Estonia]].

great-horde.t: The last remnant of the Golden Horde on the lower Volga, whose khan Ahmad's retreat from the Ugra River in 1480 ended Mongol overlordship of Russia.
great-horde.o: By the mid-15th century the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] had shed the [[s:khanate-of-kazan|Khanate of Kazan]], the [[s:crimean-khanate|Crimean Khanate]] and other states. The rump around [[e:sarai|Sarai]], ruled by [[e:kuchuk-muhammad|Küchük Muhammad]] and his sons, became known as the Great Horde, claiming to be the senior [[e:jochids|Jochid]] state.
great-horde.r: Its khans still demanded tribute from [[e:moscow|Moscow]] and fought the [[s:crimean-khanate|Crimean Khanate]] for the [[e:golden-horde|Golden Horde's]] heritage, allying with Poland-[[e:lithuania|Lithuania]]. [[e:akhmat-khan|Akhmed Khan]], or Ahmad, was its strongest ruler. Its nomadic economy suffered as trade shifted and the [[e:volga|Volga]] cities declined.
great-horde.e: In 1480 Ahmad faced [[e:ivan-iii|Ivan III's]] army on the [[e:great-stand-on-the-ugra-river|Ugra River]] and withdrew without battle, ending Muscovy's tribute. He was killed in 1481 by [[e:ibak-khan|Ibak Khan]] of the [[s:tyumen-khanate|Tyumen Khanate]]. In 1502 the Crimean khan [[e:menli-i-giray|Meñli I Giray]] sacked [[e:sarai|Sarai]] and destroyed the horde.

government-of-national-salvation.t: Collaborationist Serbian government of General Milan Nedić, which administered German-occupied Serbia during the Second World War.
government-of-national-salvation.o: After the [[e:axis-powers|Axis]] conquest of the [[s:kingdom-of-yugoslavia|Kingdom of Yugoslavia]] in April 1941, a reduced [[s:serbia|Serbia]] was placed under a German military commander. A commissioner government led by [[e:milan-acimovic|Milan Aćimović]] proved unable to cope with the uprising of summer 1941, and on 29 August 1941 the Germans installed the former war minister General [[e:milan-nedic|Milan Nedić]] at the head of a Government of National Salvation.
government-of-national-salvation.r: The government ran the civil administration, police and a Serbian State Guard, but the German occupiers held real power and carried out mass reprisals, such as the [[e:kragujevac-massacre|Kragujevac massacre]] of October 1941. [[e:jews|Jews]] of [[s:serbia|Serbia]] were murdered in 1941 and 1942, with the help of local police. [[e:milan-nedic|Nedić]] promoted a conservative peasant ideology and sheltered refugees from the [[s:independent-state-of-croatia|Independent State of Croatia]].
government-of-national-salvation.e: As [[e:yugoslav-partisans|Partisans]] and the Soviet [[e:red-army|Red Army]] advanced, [[e:milan-nedic|Nedić]] fled in October 1944 and [[e:belgrade|Belgrade]] was liberated. He died in Yugoslav custody in 1946. The regime's record of collaboration remains debated in [[s:serbia|Serbia]].

german-south-west-africa.t: Germany's colony in Namibia, a settler territory where the colonial army committed genocide against the Herero and Nama.
german-south-west-africa.o: In 1883 the [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]] merchant [[e:adolf-luderitz|Adolf Lüderitz]] bought land at [[e:luderitz|Angra Pequena]], and on 24 April 1884 [[e:germany|Germany]] declared a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]]. Protection treaties with the [[s:herero-paramountcy|Herero Paramountcy]] and the [[s:rehoboth-basters|Rehoboth Basters]] followed, and [[e:curt-von-francois|Curt von François]] founded [[e:windhoek|Windhoek]] as the capital in 1890.
german-south-west-africa.r: Governor [[e:theodor-leutwein|Theodor Leutwein]] ruled through treaties with chiefs while settlers took land and [[e:cattle|cattle]]. The [[e:herero-people|Herero]] rising of 1904 and the [[e:nama-people|Nama]] war under [[e:hendrik-witbooi|Hendrik Witbooi]] were crushed by General [[e:lothar-von-trotha|Lothar von Trotha]]; tens of thousands died in the desert and in [[e:concentration-camp|concentration camps]] such as [[e:shark-island-concentration-camp|Shark Island]]. Diamonds found near [[e:luderitz|Lüderitz]] in 1908 made the colony profitable.
german-south-west-africa.e: South African forces invaded during the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], and the German garrison surrendered at Khorab in July 1915. The territory became [[s:south-west-africa|South West Africa]]. [[e:germany|Germany]] formally acknowledged the [[e:genocide|genocide]] in 2021.
