garha-kingdom.t: The largest of the Gond kingdoms of central India, ruled from Garha and Mandla, famous for Rani Durgavati's stand against the Mughals.
garha-kingdom.o: [[e:gond-people|Gond]] rulers established a kingdom around Garha, near modern [[e:jabalpur|Jabalpur]], perhaps in the 14th century; its early history comes from later genealogies. [[e:sangram-shah|Sangram Shah]], in the early 16th century, expanded it to dozens of forts across the [[e:narmada-river|Narmada]] valley, making Garha-[[e:katanga|Katanga]] one of the largest states of central [[e:india|India]].
garha-kingdom.r: The kings ruled a mixed population of [[e:gond-people|Gond]] and [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] farmers and forest peoples, and adopted [[e:rajputs|Rajput]] customs and alliances; [[e:dalpat-shah|Dalpat Shah]] married Durgavati, a Chandela princess. The kingdom was known for its herds of elephants and its forests. After Dalpat's death, Durgavati ruled as regent and built tanks and towns.
garha-kingdom.e: The Mughal general Asaf Khan invaded in 1564, and Durgavati died in battle near [[e:narai|Narai]]. The kingdom survived as a Mughal [[e:vassal|vassal]] from [[e:mandla|Mandla]], losing territory steadily. The [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] took control in the 18th century, ending [[e:gond-people|Gond]] rule in the 1780s, and the region later passed to the British.

governorate-of-courland.t: Russian imperial province formed from the Duchy of Courland in 1795, ruled by its Baltic German knighthood until the First World War.
governorate-of-courland.o: After the [[e:third-partition-of-poland|Third Partition of Poland]] in 1795, the nobility of the [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia|Duchy of Courland and Semigallia]] submitted to [[e:catherine-the-great|Catherine the Great]], and the duchy, with the [[s:district-of-pilten|District of Pilten]], became the [[e:governorate|Governorate]] of [[e:courland|Courland]], with its capital at [[e:jelgava|Mitau]] (Jelgava).
governorate-of-courland.r: The [[e:courland|Courland]] knighthood kept control of local government, courts and the Lutheran church under the Baltic special order, and German remained the language of administration until the [[e:russification|Russification]] of the 1880s. [[e:serfdom|Serfdom]] was abolished in 1817, but the land stayed largely with the nobles. Latvian peasants increasingly bought farms, and [[e:liepaja|Libau]] (Liepāja) and [[e:ventspils|Windau]] grew as ports. The 1905 revolution saw many manor houses burned.
governorate-of-courland.e: German armies occupied [[e:courland|Courland]] in 1915, and it was administered by [[s:ober-ost|Ober Ost]]. In 1918 the [[e:baltic-germans|Baltic Germans]] proclaimed the [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia|Duchy of Courland and Semigallia]] (1918), but after [[e:germany|Germany's]] defeat the territory became part of the [[s:republic-of-latvia|Republic of Latvia]], with a small southern strip going to [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]].

governorate-of-the-rio-de-la-plata.t: The first Spanish governorate of the River Plate basin, which founded Buenos Aires and Asunción and opened the interior of southern South America.
governorate-of-the-rio-de-la-plata.o: In 1534 [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] granted [[e:pedro-de-mendoza|Pedro de Mendoza]] a governorate south of [[e:francisco-pizarro|Pizarro]]'s lands. Mendoza founded [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] in 1536, but hunger and attacks forced its abandonment in 1541. [[e:juan-de-salazar|Juan de Salazar]] founded [[e:asuncion|Asunción]] in 1537, upriver on the [[s:republic-of-paraguay|Paraguay]] river, and it became the capital of the governorate.
governorate-of-the-rio-de-la-plata.r: From [[e:asuncion|Asunción]], governors such as [[e:domingo-martinez-de-irala|Domingo Martínez de Irala]] and [[e:alvar-nunez-cabeza-de-vaca|Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca]] ruled a frontier colony built on alliances with the [[e:guarani-people|Guaraní]], many of whom were bound in [[e:encomienda|encomiendas]], and on mixed marriages that produced a large mestizo population. Expeditions sought a route to the [[e:silver|silver]] of [[e:peru|Peru]]. [[e:juan-de-garay|Juan de Garay]] founded [[e:santa-fe-argentina|Santa Fe]] in 1573 and refounded [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] in 1580. [[e:hernandarias|Hernandarias]], the first [[e:criollo-people|Creole]] governor, promoted [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] missions.
governorate-of-the-rio-de-la-plata.e: In 1617 the crown split the vast governorate into the [[s:governorate-of-paraguay|Governorate of Paraguay]], based at [[e:asuncion|Asunción]], and the [[s:governorate-of-buenos-aires|Governorate of Buenos Aires]]. Both later joined the [[s:viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata]] created in 1776, and Asunción is remembered as the 'mother of cities' for the towns founded from it.

gaza.t: Gaza, the southernmost Philistine city and the gateway between Egypt and Asia, a hub of the incense trade that resisted Alexander.
gaza.o: Gaza was the main Egyptian administrative base in [[e:canaan|Canaan]] during the [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]]. In the 12th century BCE [[s:philistine-pentapolis|Philistines]] settled there, and it became one of the cities of the Philistine Pentapolis, controlling the coastal road to [[e:egypt|Egypt]].
gaza.r: Its kings grew rich as the terminus of [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] from [[e:arabia|Arabia]] carrying frankincense and [[e:myrrh|myrrh]]. The [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]] sets the death of [[e:samson|Samson]] in its temple of [[e:dagan|Dagon]]. In 734 BCE King Hanunu fled to [[e:egypt|Egypt]] before Tiglath-Pileser III of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]], who made Gaza a trading post.
gaza.e: Under the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]] Gaza was a flourishing frontier city. In 332 BCE its commander [[e:batis|Batis]] held out against Alexander of the [[s:macedonian-empire|Macedonian Empire]] for two months; the city was stormed and its people killed or enslaved.

gurjaras-of-nandipuri.t: A Gurjara dynasty of southern Gujarat around Bharuch that fought Arab raiders in the 8th century.
gurjaras-of-nandipuri.o: A Gurjara family established itself in the late 6th century in the [[e:lata-region|Lata]] region of southern [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], around [[e:bharuch|Bharuch]] and Nandipuri, probably near modern Nandod. Its founder was Dadda I, and the line is known entirely from [[e:copper|copper]]-plate land grants.
gurjaras-of-nandipuri.r: The kings ruled a small but wealthy territory around the port of [[e:bharuch|Bharuch]], usually as feudatories of the [[s:kalachuris-of-mahishmati|Kalachuris of Mahishmati]] and then of the [[s:chalukyas-of-badami|Chalukyas of Badami]]. [[e:dadda-ii|Dadda II]] is credited with protecting the [[e:maitraka-dynasty|Maitraka]] king of [[e:valabhi|Valabhi]] against [[e:harsha|Harsha]]. The dynasty patronised [[e:brahmins|Brahmins]] and Sun worship, according to its grants.
gurjaras-of-nandipuri.e: The last known king, [[e:jayabhata-iv|Jayabhata IV]], fought Arab raids from [[e:sindh|Sindh]] in the 730s. The dynasty ends around 738, probably overwhelmed by the Arab incursions and by the [[e:chalukya-dynasty|Chalukyas]], and [[e:lata-region|Lata]] passed later to the [[s:rashtrakuta-dynasty|Rashtrakuta dynasty]].

grenland.t: Petty kingdom at the mouth of the Skien river in southern Norway, one of the coastal realms brought under Harald Fairhair.
grenland.o: Grenland, around the lower [[e:skienselva|Skienselva]] and the coast of modern [[e:telemark|Telemark]], appears in the sagas as one of the small kingdoms of south-eastern [[e:norway|Norway]]. Its early history is obscure and known only from scattered references in later Icelandic writings.
grenland.r: The district looked to the sea and the [[e:skagerrak|Skagerrak]], and its people farmed, fished and traded. Inland [[e:telemark|Telemark]] supplied iron and whetstones that were exported widely in the [[e:viking-age|Viking Age]]. No reliable record of its kings or institutions survives.
grenland.e: Grenland passed into the realm of the [[s:vestfold|Vestfold]] kings and of [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]] in the late 9th century and became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]]. The town of [[e:skien|Skien]] grew there in the [[e:middle-ages|Middle Ages]].

gangga-negara.t: A half-legendary Hindu-Buddhist kingdom in the Beruas and Dinding area of Perak, remembered as one of the oldest polities of the Malay Peninsula.
gangga-negara.o: Gangga Negara is known mainly from Malay tradition, especially the [[e:hikayat-merong-mahawangsa|Hikayat Merong Mahawangsa]], and from scattered archaeological finds around [[e:beruas|Beruas]] in [[s:perak-sultanate|Perak]]. Its name, [[e:sanskrit|Sanskrit]] for 'city on the [[e:ganges-plain|Ganges]]', points to the Indian cultural influence that reached the peninsula's west coast in the early centuries CE. No inscription confirms a founding date.
gangga-negara.r: Finds at [[e:beruas|Beruas]] and nearby sites, including Buddhist statues, [[e:bead|beads]] and Chinese ceramics, suggest a riverine trading settlement exporting [[e:tin|tin]] and forest products. Little is known of its government beyond what later legends say.
gangga-negara.e: Tradition holds that the kingdom was destroyed during the [[e:chola-invasion-of-srivijaya|Chola raids]] led by [[e:rajendra-chola-i|Rajendra Chola]] around 1025. The later Malay state of [[e:beruas|Beruas]], which flourished before the [[s:perak-sultanate|Perak Sultanate]], is often linked with its memory.

garrauli-state.t: A small Bundelkhand state created in 1812 to settle a Bundela chief who had long resisted the British.
garrauli-state.o: [[e:gopal-singh-of-garrauli|Gopal Singh]], a [[e:bundela|Bundela]] leader, fought the British in [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] for several years after 1803. In 1812 he submitted and received Garrauli and nearby villages by sanad as a hereditary holding.
garrauli-state.r: Garrauli was a minor, non-salute state of the [[e:bundelkhand-agency|Bundelkhand Agency]] ruled by a [[e:diwan|Diwan]]. Little else is recorded of its internal history.
garrauli-state.e: After independence Garrauli was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] with the other [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] states and absorbed by 1950; it lies in [[s:chhatarpur-state|Chhatarpur]] district of [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]].

griqualand-east.t: The territory where Adam Kok III's Griqua resettled after their trek over the Drakensberg, with its capital at Kokstad.
griqualand-east.o: After selling their land at [[s:philippolis-griqua-state|Philippolis]] to the [[s:orange-free-state|Orange Free State]] in 1861, [[e:adam-kok-iii|Adam Kok III]] and some 2,000 [[e:griqua|Griqua]] trekked across the [[e:drakensberg|Drakensberg]] with wagons and [[e:cattle|cattle]], arriving in 1863 in Nomansland, a thinly settled area between the [[s:mpondo-kingdom|Mpondo Kingdom]] and [[s:natal-colony|Natal]] that the Cape government had offered them.
griqualand-east.r: The [[e:griqua|Griqua]] set up a [[e:volksraad|Volksraad]] under Kok and issued land titles to settlers. They founded [[e:kokstad|Kokstad]] in 1869 below Mount Currie. Many settlers, however, sold their farms to whites, and debt and land loss weakened the community.
griqualand-east.e: The [[s:cape-colony|Cape Colony]] took over administration in 1874 and annexed the territory formally in 1879, after Kok's death in 1875 and a short [[e:griqua|Griqua]] rising in 1878. [[e:kokstad|Kokstad]] remains a centre of Griqua identity.

gangpur-state.t: A princely state in the far north-west of Odisha whose former territory now holds the Rourkela steel plant.
gangpur-state.o: Tradition dates the ruling family to around 1500, but little is reliably known of its founding.
gangpur-state.r: Gangpur was a large, forested state with a mainly Adivasi population, including [[e:kurukh-people|Oraon]], [[e:munda-people|Munda]] and [[e:kharia-people|Kharia peoples]]. It was tributary to [[s:sambalpur-state|Sambalpur]] and the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and was transferred from the [[e:chota-nagpur-plateau|Chota Nagpur]] states to the [[e:orissa-tributary-states|Orissa Tributary States]] in 1905. Its capital was [[e:sundargarh|Sundargarh]].
gangpur-state.e: Gangpur merged into [[e:odisha|Orissa]] on 1 January 1948 and became part of [[e:sundargarh|Sundargarh]] district, where the [[e:rourkela|Rourkela]] [[e:steel|steel]] plant was built in the 1950s.

goree.t: Small island off Dakar, held by Dutch, French and British in turn, which became a symbol of the Atlantic slave trade.
goree.o: The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] occupied the island in the 1620s and named it Goede Reede, 'good harbour'. Its position off the [[e:cap-vert|Cap-Vert]] peninsula made it a sheltered port for ships trading on the coast of [[e:senegal|Senegal]]. [[e:france|France]] captured Goree in 1677, and it became a base for the [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]] company.
goree.r: Goree was a trading town where slaves, gum and hides passed through, and where a [[e:criollo-people|Creole]] society formed around the signares, African and mixed-race women traders who married European men. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] occupied it several times during wars. In 1872 it became one of the [[e:four-communes|Four Communes of Senegal]], whose inhabitants gained French citizenship rights.
goree.e: As [[e:dakar-senegal|Dakar]] grew on the mainland, Goree lost its commercial role, and it was merged administratively with Dakar. The island's House of Slaves, built in the 1770s, is a memorial site, and Goree became a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]] in 1978.

gondal-state.t: A Jadeja Rajput state of Kathiawar made famous by Maharaja Bhagvatsinhji, a reformer who abolished taxes and made girls' schooling compulsory.
gondal-state.o: Gondal was founded in 1634 by Kumbhoji I, a member of the [[e:jadeja|Jadeja]] house of [[s:rajkot-state|Rajkot]], who received the area as his share. His successor Kumbhoji II expanded the state in the 18th century.
gondal-state.r: The Thakore Sahibs ruled a prosperous [[e:cotton|cotton]]-growing territory. [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]] [[e:bhagvatsinhji|Bhagvatsinhji]], who reigned from 1888 to 1944 and trained as a doctor at [[e:edinburgh|Edinburgh]], built railways and schools, made education compulsory for girls, abolished many taxes and sponsored the [[e:bhagavadgomandal|Bhagavadgomandal]] Gujarati encyclopedia. It was an eleven-gun salute state.
gondal-state.e: Gondal merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960. The town retains its palaces and a reputation as a model state.

cr.a: Dr. Andreas Birken at German Wikipedia

gwalior-state.t: The Maratha kingdom of the Scindias, whose ruler Mahadji Scindia controlled the Mughal emperor and which became one of the five 21-gun princely states.
gwalior-state.o: [[e:ranoji-scindia|Ranoji Scindia]], a commander under [[e:peshwa|Peshwa]] [[e:baji-rao-i|Baji Rao I]], received a share of [[e:malwa|Malwa]] around 1731, ruling from [[e:ujjain|Ujjain]]. After the [[e:maratha-empire|Maratha]] defeat at [[e:third-battle-of-panipat|Panipat]] in 1761 his son [[e:mahadji-scindia|Mahadji Scindia]] rebuilt the family's power with a European-trained army and from 1771 dominated the Mughal emperor in [[e:delhi|Delhi]].
gwalior-state.r: [[e:daulat-rao-scindia|Daulat Rao Scindia]] lost the [[e:second-anglo-maratha-war|Second Anglo-Maratha War]] in 1803 and moved his military camp, Lashkar, to Gwalior. Defeat at [[e:battle-of-maharajpur|Maharajpur]] in 1843 brought British control over the army. In 1857 [[e:jayajirao-scindia|Jayajirao]] stayed loyal, though his troops joined the rebels and the [[e:lakshmibai|Rani of Jhansi]] briefly took Gwalior fort. [[e:madho-rao-scindia|Madho Rao]] I built railways and industry, and the [[e:jai-vilas-palace|Jai Vilas Palace]] symbolised the dynasty's wealth.
gwalior-state.e: [[e:jivajirao-scindia|Jivajirao Scindia]] acceded to [[e:india|India]] and became [[e:rajpramukh|Rajpramukh]] of [[s:madhya-bharat|Madhya Bharat]] in 1948, with Gwalior as its winter capital. The state joined [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]] in 1956; the family remained prominent in Indian politics.

gombe-emirate.t: An eastern emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate in north-east Nigeria, founded by Buba Yero on the frontier with Bornu and the Jukun.
gombe-emirate.o: Gombe was founded by [[e:buba-yero|Buba Yero]], a [[e:fula|Fulani]] scholar and warrior who had studied under [[e:usman-dan-fodio|Usman dan Fodio]] and received a flag from him to wage [[e:jihad|jihad]] in the [[e:gongola-river|Gongola]] valley. He began campaigning in 1804, among the first commanders to take the field, and built an [[e:emirate|emirate]] out of conquests over local peoples on the borders of the [[s:kanem-bornu-empire|Kanem-Bornu Empire]] and the [[e:jukun-people|Jukun]] lands.
gombe-emirate.r: [[e:buba-yero|Buba Yero]] ruled until 1841 and pushed his raids far to the south and east, at times clashing with neighbouring [[e:emirate|emirates]]. Like other emirates, Gombe was ruled by an emir with [[e:fula|Fulani]] office-holders, paid tribute to [[e:sokoto-caliphate|Sokoto]] and depended on farming, [[e:cattle|cattle]] and the raiding of non-Muslim communities for slaves. The capital moved several times, including to Gombe Abba.
gombe-emirate.e: British forces occupied the [[e:emirate|emirate]] in 1902, and it became a division of the [[s:protectorate-of-northern-nigeria|Protectorate of Northern Nigeria]]. The emir remains a traditional ruler, and the modern city of Gombe, founded under colonial rule, is now a state capital.

cr.a: United States Depart of State, US Embassy to Nigeria

gambia-colony-and-protectorate.t: Britain's smallest African colony, a narrow strip along the Gambia river with its capital at Bathurst, which became independent as The Gambia in 1965.
gambia-colony-and-protectorate.o: In 1816 Captain Alexander Grant founded [[e:banjul|Bathurst]] on St Mary's Island at the mouth of the [[e:the-gambia|Gambia]] river, to suppress the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]] and secure British trade after the loss of [[s:goree|Goree]]. From 1821 the settlement was governed from [[e:sierra-leone|Sierra Leone]] as part of [[s:british-west-africa|British West Africa]], becoming a separate colony in 1843.
gambia-colony-and-protectorate.r: [[e:the-gambia|The Gambia]] was again placed under [[e:sierra-leone|Sierra Leone]] in 1866 and became separate for good in 1888. An Anglo-French agreement of 1889 fixed its borders as a strip a few kilometres wide on either side of the river, enclosed by [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]], and a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] over the interior followed in 1894. [[e:groundnut|Groundnuts]] were the main export, and most people were Muslim [[e:mandinka|Mandinka]], [[e:fula|Fula]] and [[e:wolof|Wolof]].
gambia-colony-and-protectorate.e: Constitutional reforms in the 1950s and early 1960s brought [[e:dawda-jawara|Dawda Jawara]] and his [[e:peoples-progressive-party-the-gambia|People's Progressive Party]] to power. [[e:the-gambia|The Gambia]] became independent on 18 February 1965, and [[e:banjul|Bathurst]] was renamed Banjul in 1973.

gold-coast-colony.t: The British colony on the coast of modern Ghana, which grew from a string of forts into the first sub-Saharan African colony to win independence, as Ghana in 1957.
gold-coast-colony.o: In 1821 the British crown took over the forts of the [[e:company-of-merchants-trading-to-africa|Company of Merchants]] on the [[e:gold-coast|Gold Coast]] and placed them under [[e:charles-maccarthy|Charles MacCarthy]] in [[e:sierra-leone|Sierra Leone]]. He was killed fighting the [[s:ashanti-empire|Ashanti Empire]] in 1824. [[e:george-maclean|George Maclean]], president of the merchant council from 1830, made peace with [[e:ashanti-empire|Ashanti]] in 1831 and extended British jurisdiction among the [[e:fante|Fante]], formalised in the Bond of 1844.
gold-coast-colony.r: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] bought the Danish forts in 1850 and the [[s:dutch-gold-coast|Dutch Gold Coast]] in 1872, and after defeating [[e:ashanti-empire|Ashanti]] in 1874 declared a crown colony, with its capital at [[e:accra|Accra]] from 1877. The colony's economy rested on gold, [[e:timber|timber]] and above all cocoa, of which it became the largest exporter in the world. Governor [[e:gordon-guggisberg|Gordon Guggisberg]] built Takoradi harbour and [[e:achimota-school|Achimota School]] in the 1920s.
gold-coast-colony.e: Riots in 1948 and the campaign of [[e:kwame-nkrumah|Kwame Nkrumah's]] [[e:convention-peoples-party|Convention People's Party]] led to self-government. On 6 March 1957 the colony, with the [[s:ashanti-colony|Ashanti Colony]], the Northern Territories and [[s:british-togoland|British Togoland]], became independent as [[e:ghana|Ghana]].

cr.a: No machine-readable author provided. Yaddah assumed (based on copyright claims).

gabon-french-colony.t: French rule over the Gabon estuary and its hinterland, from coastal treaty posts in the 1840s to an autonomous republic in 1958.
gabon-french-colony.o: French naval officers signed treaties with [[e:mpongwe|Mpongwe]] rulers of the Gabon estuary, including [[e:denis-rapontchombo|King Denis]] Rapontchombo in 1839 and King Louis in 1842, and built a fort in 1843 to support anti-slave-trade patrols. [[e:libreville|Libreville]] was founded in 1849 by Africans freed from a captured slave ship. [[e:pierre-savorgnan-de-brazza|Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza's]] expeditions from the 1870s pushed claims inland.
gabon-french-colony.r: Gabon was long administered with the [[s:french-congo|French Congo]] and from 1910 as part of [[s:french-equatorial-africa|French Equatorial Africa]]. Concession companies, [[e:timber|timber]] cutting, especially of okoumé, and forced labour shaped the economy, while Catholic and Protestant missions spread schooling. [[e:albert-schweitzer|Albert Schweitzer]] ran his hospital at [[e:lambarene|Lambaréné]] from 1913.
gabon-french-colony.e: In 1958 Gabon became an autonomous republic within the [[e:french-community|French Community]] and gained full independence on 17 August 1960 under [[e:leon-mba|Léon M'ba]], keeping close economic and military ties with [[e:france|France]] and [[e:libreville|Libreville]] as its capital.

gcaleka-xhosa-kingdom.t: The senior Xhosa kingdom east of the Kei, whose rulers Hintsa and Sarhili faced British expansion and the catastrophe of the cattle-killing.
gcaleka-xhosa-kingdom.o: When the united [[s:xhosa-kingdom|Xhosa Kingdom]] divided around 1775, the Great House under Gcaleka kept the senior paramountcy and the lands east of the Kei river, while the [[s:rharhabe-xhosa-kingdom|Rharhabe Xhosa Kingdom]] held the west. Gcaleka's successors continued to be recognised as paramount over all [[e:xhosa-people|Xhosa]].
gcaleka-xhosa-kingdom.r: The paramount ruled his own chiefdom directly and held ritual seniority over others, governing with councillors. [[e:hintsa-kakhawuta|Hintsa]] was drawn into the Sixth Frontier War and was shot while held by British forces in 1835. Under [[e:sarhili|Sarhili]], the Gcaleka followed the prophecies of [[e:nongqawuse|Nongqawuse]] in 1856–57, killing their [[e:cattle|cattle]] in hope of deliverance, which led to mass famine.
gcaleka-xhosa-kingdom.e: After the Ninth Frontier War of 1877–78, [[e:sarhili|Sarhili]] was driven out and Gcalekaland came under Cape control, being formally annexed by 1885. The [[e:xhosa-people|Xhosa]] royal house continues, and the [[e:cattle|cattle]]-killing remains a defining memory in South African history.

great-sioux-nation.t: The Oceti Sakowin, or Seven Council Fires, of the Dakota, Nakota and Lakota peoples, who became the leading power of the northern Plains in the 19th century.
great-sioux-nation.o: The seven divisions of the Oceti Sakowin, the four [[e:dakota-people|Dakota peoples]], the [[e:yankton-sioux|Yankton]], the [[e:yanktonai|Yanktonai]] and the [[e:lakota-people|Lakota]] or Teton, originally lived around the upper [[e:mississippi-river|Mississippi]] in what is now [[e:minnesota|Minnesota]]. Pressed by the [[e:ojibwe|Ojibwe]] and drawn by the bison, many moved west in the 18th century, acquired horses, and by around 1776 the Lakota had reached the [[e:black-hills|Black Hills]].
great-sioux-nation.r: The divisions were connected by kinship, language and ceremony rather than a single government; each band, or tiyospaye, had its own leaders, and the [[e:lakota-people|Lakota]] were themselves divided into seven groups. Mounted bison hunting supplied food, hides and trade goods, and ceremonies such as the [[e:sun-dance|Sun Dance]] renewed communal bonds. In the 1860s Red Cloud's War forced the [[s:united-states|United States]] to accept the Fort Laramie Treaty of 1868, creating a [[e:great-sioux-reservation|Great Sioux Reservation]] that included the [[e:black-hills|Black Hills]].
great-sioux-nation.e: After gold was found in the [[e:black-hills|Black Hills]] in 1874, the [[e:great-sioux-war-of-1876|Great Sioux War]] followed; [[e:lakota-people|Lakota]] and [[e:cheyenne|Cheyenne]] under [[e:sitting-bull|Sitting Bull]] and [[e:crazy-horse|Crazy Horse]] defeated [[e:george-armstrong-custer|Custer]] at the [[e:battle-of-the-little-bighorn|Little Bighorn]] in 1876. In 1877 Congress seized the Black Hills, and the Lakota were confined to shrinking reservations.

cr.a: David F. Barry, Photographer, Bismarck, Dakota Territory

ga-kingdom.t: Kingdom of the Ga people around present-day Accra, which controlled coastal trade until conquered by Akwamu.
ga-kingdom.o: Ga-speaking communities settled the [[e:accra|Accra]] plains by the 15th century, and a kingdom formed with its capital at [[e:ayawaso|Ayawaso]], inland from the coast, which Europeans called Great Accra. The coastal town of Small Accra became a market for Portuguese, [[e:dutch|Dutch]], English, Danish and Swedish traders.
ga-kingdom.r: The Ga king, the Mantse, ruled with priests of the Ga gods and town quarters. The kingdom controlled trade between the coast and the inland forest, supplying gold and slaves and buying cloth and metal goods. European companies built forts at [[e:accra|Accra]] in the 17th century: the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] [[e:ussher-fort|Fort Crevecoeur]], the English [[e:james-fort|James Fort]] and the Danish [[e:osu-castle|Christiansborg]].
ga-kingdom.e: The rising [[s:akwamu|Akwamu]] state attacked the Ga, destroyed [[e:ayawaso|Ayawaso]] in 1677 and completed its conquest by 1681. The Ga regrouped in the coastal towns, which grew into the city of [[e:accra|Accra]], capital of independent [[e:ghana|Ghana]].

grand-duchy-of-lithuania.t: Once the largest state in Europe, a pagan Baltic power that grew to rule most of Belarus and Ukraine and joined Poland in the Commonwealth.
grand-duchy-of-lithuania.o: In the early 13th century Lithuanian chiefs united against attacks by German crusaders and their neighbours, and in 1236 a Lithuanian army destroyed the [[s:livonian-brothers-of-the-sword|Livonian Brothers of the Sword]] at [[e:battle-of-saule|Saule]]. [[e:mindaugas|Mindaugas]] unified the tribes and was crowned king in 1253, briefly creating the [[s:kingdom-of-lithuania|Kingdom of Lithuania]], before the grand ducal state took its lasting form.
grand-duchy-of-lithuania.r: [[e:gediminas|Gediminas]], who ruled from about 1316 to 1341, made [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]] his capital and expanded into Rus', and his sons [[e:algirdas|Algirdas]] and [[e:kestutis|Kestutis]] took [[e:kyiv|Kiev]] and much of the [[e:dnieper|Dnieper]] basin. [[s:republic-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] stayed pagan until 1387, when [[e:w-adys-aw-ii-jagie-o|Jogaila]], baptised in [[e:krakow|Krakow]] the year before, began its conversion. Ruthenian was the chancery language, the [[e:statutes-of-lithuania|Lithuanian Statutes]] codified law, and [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]], Catholics, [[e:jews|Jews]] and [[e:tatars|Tatars]] lived side by side.
grand-duchy-of-lithuania.e: [[e:vytautas-the-great|Vytautas]] helped defeat the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Knights]] at [[e:battle-of-grunwald|Grunwald]] in 1410. Long tied to [[e:poland|Poland]] by personal unions, the grand duchy joined it in the [[s:polish-lithuanian-commonwealth|Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth]] by the [[e:union-of-lublin|Union of Lublin]] in 1569, keeping its own army, treasury and law. The [[e:third-partition-of-poland|Third Partition]] of 1795 gave its lands to the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]].
grand-duchy-of-lithuania.re: Baltic paganism, later Catholic and Orthodox Christianity

germiyanids.t: A powerful beylik of western Anatolia centred on Kutahya, important patrons of early Anatolian Turkish literature.
germiyanids.o: The Germiyan were a tribal group settled by the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]] near [[s:melid|Malatya]] and moved to the [[e:kutahya|Kutahya]] region in the later 13th century to guard the frontier. As Seljuk authority waned around 1300, their leaders ruled Kutahya as an independent [[e:beylik|beylik]], for a time the strongest in western [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]].
germiyanids.r: Yakub I received tribute from several neighbours, including Byzantine [[e:alasehir|Philadelphia]], and the [[e:beylik|beylik]] later absorbed the Sahib Ataid and Inancid lands. [[e:suleyman-shah-of-germiyan|Suleyman Shah]] married his daughter to the future [[e:bayezid-i|Bayezid I]], giving [[e:kutahya|Kutahya]] as part of her dowry around 1381. The court sponsored poets writing in Turkish, among them [[e:ahmedi|Ahmedi]] and Sheykhoglu Mustafa, and the alum and other mines of the region brought wealth.
germiyanids.e: [[e:bayezid-i|Bayezid I]] took the rest of the [[e:beylik|beylik]] in 1390, but [[e:timur|Timur]] restored [[e:yakub-ii-of-germiyan|Yakub II]] in 1402. Yakub II bequeathed his lands to [[e:murad-ii|Murad II]], and they passed to the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] on his death in 1429.

geumgwan-gaya.t: The leading early state of the Gaya confederacy at modern Gimhae, a port kingdom whose iron trade linked Korea, Chinese commanderies and Japan.
geumgwan-gaya.o: Geumgwan Gaya grew out of Guya-guk, a [[s:byeonhan|Byeonhan]] statelet at the mouth of the [[e:nakdong-river|Nakdong]] river. Its founding legend tells of [[e:suro-of-geumgwan-gaya|King Suro]] hatching from a golden egg in 42 CE and marrying [[e:heo-hwang-ok|Heo Hwang-ok]], a princess said to have sailed from a distant land called Ayuta.
geumgwan-gaya.r: Kings at [[e:gimhae|Gimhae]] controlled [[e:iron-smelting|iron production]] and a harbour where traders from [[e:lelang-commandery|Lelang]], [[e:daifang-commandery|Daifang]] and Wa called. The royal cemetery at [[e:daeseong-dong-tumuli|Daeseong-dong]] contains iron armour, horse gear and weapons, plus Japanese-style objects. Until about 400 it led the Gaya states, but a [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] campaign that year to aid [[s:silla|Silla]] broke its strength.
geumgwan-gaya.e: Weakened and squeezed by [[s:silla|Silla]], King [[e:guhyeong-of-geumgwan-gaya|Guhyeong]] surrendered to [[e:beopheung-of-silla|King Beopheung]] of Silla in 532 and was given rank and land. His great-grandson [[e:kim-yu-sin|Kim Yu-sin]] became the general who helped Silla unify [[e:korea|Korea]].

galatia.t: Galatia, the land of three Celtic tribes who crossed into Anatolia in 278 BCE and kept their own language and laws for centuries.
galatia.o: In 278 BCE [[e:nicomedes-i-of-bithynia|Nicomedes I]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-bithynia|Kingdom of Bithynia]] invited bands of Celtic warriors across the [[s:bosporan-kingdom|Bosporus]] as [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]]. After years of raiding western [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]], they were defeated by Antiochus I and [[e:attalus-i|Attalus I]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-pergamon|Kingdom of Pergamon]] and settled on the central plateau around [[e:ankara|Ancyra]].
galatia.r: Three tribes, the [[e:tolistobogii|Tolistobogii]], [[s:volcae-tectosages|Tectosages]] and [[e:trocmi|Trocmi]], each split into four parts under tetrarchs, met in a council of 300 at a sacred grove called [[e:drynemeton|Drynemeton]]. Galatians served as [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]] across the Hellenistic world. The statues of the [[e:dying-gaul|Dying Gaul]] commemorate [[e:pergamon|Pergamon's]] victories over them.
galatia.e: In the 1st century BCE [[e:deiotarus|Deiotarus]], [[e:rome|Rome's]] ally, made himself king of all Galatia. After the death of the last king, [[e:amyntas-of-galatia|Amyntas]], in 25 BCE, Augustus made Galatia a Roman province; Paul later wrote to its Christian communities.

gaza-empire.t: The Nguni conquest state of southern Mozambique founded by Soshangane, the last great African power to resist Portugal in the region.
gaza-empire.o: [[e:soshangane|Soshangane]], a commander of [[e:zwide|Zwide's]] [[s:ndwandwe-kingdom|Ndwandwe Kingdom]], fled north after the [[e:ndwandwe|Ndwandwe]] defeat by the [[e:zulu-kingdom|Zulu]] and by about 1824 had settled in southern [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Mozambique]]. He conquered [[e:tsonga-people|Tsonga]] and Chopi communities and defeated Portuguese posts at [[e:delagoa-bay|Delagoa Bay]] and [[e:inhambane|Inhambane]], building a kingdom that reached the [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]] and the eastern [[e:zimbabwe|Zimbabwe]] highlands.
gaza-empire.r: The [[e:nguni|Nguni]] elite ruled through age regiments on the [[e:zulu-kingdom|Zulu]] model, taking tribute in [[e:cattle|cattle]] and young men from conquered peoples, who became known as Shangaan. A long succession war after [[e:soshangane|Soshangane's]] death in 1858 brought his son [[e:mzila|Mzila]] to power. Later rulers profited from sending men to work on the [[e:kimberley|Kimberley]] and [[e:witwatersrand|Witwatersrand]] mines.
gaza-empire.e: [[e:ngungunhane|Ngungunhane]] moved the capital to Mandlakazi in 1889 and tried to play [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] against Portugal. Portuguese forces defeated his army at Coolela in 1895 and captured him at Chaimite; he died in exile in the [[e:azores|Azores]], and the land became part of [[s:portuguese-mozambique|Portuguese Mozambique]].

gadir.t: The great Phoenician city of Cádiz, gateway to the Atlantic, home of a famous temple of Melqart and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Europe.
gadir.o: Gadir was founded by settlers from [[s:tyre|Tyre]] on islands off the Atlantic coast near the mouth of the [[e:guadalete|Guadalete]]. Ancient writers dated its foundation to around 1100 BCE, but archaeology places it in the 9th to 8th centuries BCE. Its position beyond the [[e:strait-of-gibraltar|Strait of Gibraltar]] gave access to Tartessian [[e:silver|silver]] and Atlantic [[e:tin|tin]].
gadir.r: Gadir was governed by its own elite under institutions modelled on [[s:tyre|Tyre]], and its temple of [[e:melqart|Melqart]], later identified with Hercules, drew pilgrims from across the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]]; [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] visited before marching on [[e:italy|Italy]] in 218 BCE. Fish salting, purple dye and long-distance trade made it rich, and it came to lead the Phoenician towns of the south under Carthaginian hegemony.
gadir.e: In 206 BCE, after the Carthaginian defeat at [[e:battle-of-ilipa|Ilipa]], Gadir went over to [[e:rome|Rome]] under a treaty of alliance. Its citizens received Roman citizenship under [[e:julius-caesar|Julius Caesar]], and Gades became one of the wealthiest cities of [[s:hispania-baetica|Hispania Baetica]].

governorate-of-buenos-aires.t: The Spanish governorate around the River Plate estuary whose port, long restricted by Spain, thrived on smuggling and grew into a viceregal capital.
governorate-of-buenos-aires.o: In 1617 the [[s:governorate-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|Governorate of the Río de la Plata]] was divided, and the southern part became the [[e:governorate|Governorate]] of [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]], with its capital at Buenos Aires, refounded by [[e:juan-de-garay|Juan de Garay]] in 1580. It included the towns of [[e:santa-fe-argentina|Santa Fe]], [[e:corrientes|Corrientes]] and later [[e:montevideo|Montevideo]].
governorate-of-buenos-aires.r: [[e:spain|Spain]] restricted trade through [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] to protect the official route through [[e:lima|Lima]] and [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]], but the port flourished on smuggling of [[e:silver|silver]] from [[e:potosi|Potosí]] in exchange for European goods and enslaved Africans. [[e:cattle|Cattle]] hides were the main export. Rivalry with Portugal over [[s:colonia-del-sacramento|Colonia del Sacramento]] dominated its politics, and Governor [[e:bruno-mauricio-de-zabala|Bruno Mauricio de Zabala]] founded [[e:montevideo|Montevideo]] in 1724 to block Portuguese expansion.
governorate-of-buenos-aires.e: In 1776 [[e:charles-iii-of-spain|Charles III]] made [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]] the capital of the new [[s:viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata]], which absorbed the governorate. The port's growing importance laid the foundations for [[e:argentina|Argentina's]] later dominance in the region.

greater-lebanon.t: The French-created state that enlarged Mount Lebanon with Beirut, the coast and the Beqaa, giving Lebanon its modern borders.
greater-lebanon.o: On 1 September 1920 General [[e:henri-gouraud|Henri Gouraud]] proclaimed the State of Greater [[s:lebanese-republic|Lebanon]] in [[s:beirut|Beirut]]. Responding to the wishes of the Maronite Patriarch [[e:elias-peter-hoayek|Elias Hoayek]] and others, [[e:france|France]] added [[e:beirut|Beirut]], [[s:county-of-tripoli|Tripoli]], [[s:sidon|Sidon]], [[s:tyre|Tyre]] and the [[e:beqaa-valley|Beqaa Valley]] to the former [[s:mount-lebanon-mutasarrifate|Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate]].
greater-lebanon.r: The state was administered by French governors under the high commissioner, with an elected representative council from 1922 organised on confessional lines. The enlargement made it economically viable but brought in large [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] and Shia populations, many of whom wanted union with [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]]. [[s:beirut|Beirut]] became the seat of the [[s:french-mandate-for-syria-and-the-lebanon|French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon]].
greater-lebanon.e: In May 1926 a constitution was adopted that turned the state into the [[s:lebanese-republic|Lebanese Republic]], with [[e:charles-debbas|Charles Debbas]] as its first president.
greater-lebanon.re: Maronite Christianity, Sunni and Shia Islam, Druze

ganzhou-uyghur-kingdom.t: A Uyghur khaganate in the Hexi Corridor, founded by refugees from the fallen steppe empire, that controlled a key stretch of the Silk Road for over a century.
ganzhou-uyghur-kingdom.o: When the [[s:uyghur-khaganate|Uyghur Khaganate]] in [[s:mongolia|Mongolia]] was destroyed by the [[e:yenisei-kyrgyz|Kyrgyz]] in 840, [[e:uyghurs|Uyghur]] groups fled south and west. One group settled among the oases of the [[e:gansu-corridor|Hexi Corridor]] and by the 890s had made [[e:zhangye|Ganzhou]] (modern Zhangye) the seat of its own [[e:khagan|khagan]].
ganzhou-uyghur-kingdom.r: The [[e:khagan|khagans]] ruled [[e:uyghurs|Uyghur]] herders alongside Chinese, Tibetan and other townspeople, profiting from the horse and jade trade between [[e:central-asia|Central Asia]] and [[e:china|China]]. They sent tribute missions to the [[e:five-dynasties-and-ten-kingdoms-period|Five Dynasties]] courts and the [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]], intermarried with the Cao rulers of the [[s:guiyi-circuit|Guiyi Circuit]] at [[e:dunhuang|Dunhuang]] and sometimes fought them. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] largely replaced the [[e:manichaeism|Manichaeism]] of the old khaganate.
ganzhou-uyghur-kingdom.e: Rising Tangut power closed in, and in 1028 [[e:li-yuanhao|Li Yuanhao]], later founder of [[s:western-xia|Western Xia]], captured [[e:zhangye|Ganzhou]]. [[e:uyghurs|Uyghur]] remnants survived in the region; the [[e:yugurs|Yugur]] (Yellow Uyghur) people of [[e:gansu|Gansu]] are commonly regarded as their descendants.

garifuna-of-saint-vincent.t: The Black Caribs of Saint Vincent, a people of mixed African and Kalinago descent who defended their island against Britain and were deported in 1797.
garifuna-of-saint-vincent.o: From the 17th century Africans who escaped shipwrecks or [[e:slavery|slavery]] on nearby islands reached [[e:saint-vincent-island|Saint Vincent]] and mixed with the [[e:kalinago|Kalinago]]. By around 1700 these [[e:garifuna|Black Caribs]], the Garinagu, formed a distinct people controlling much of the island's windward side, separate from the Yellow Caribs. Europeans agreed the island was neutral and left largely to its native inhabitants.
garifuna-of-saint-vincent.r: The [[e:garifuna|Garifuna]] lived in villages led by chiefs, farming [[e:cassava|cassava]], fishing and trading with French settlers, from whom some took Catholic practices. Their language was [[e:arawakan-languages|Arawakan]] with Carib and later French and English loans, and their religion centred on ancestors. After [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] gained the island in 1763 and pressed for land, they fought the [[e:first-carib-war|First Carib War]] of 1772 to 1773 and won a treaty securing part of the north.
garifuna-of-saint-vincent.e: Allied with the French during the [[e:second-carib-war|Second Carib War]] of 1795 to 1796, the [[e:garifuna|Garifuna]] lost their paramount chief [[e:joseph-chatoyer|Joseph Chatoyer]] and surrendered. In 1797 about 2,000 survivors were shipped from [[e:balliceaux|Balliceaux]] to [[e:roatan|Roatán]], from where they spread along the Central American coast. Chatoyer is now [[e:saint-vincent-island|Saint Vincent]]'s national hero.

governorate-of-tucuman.t: The Spanish governorate of northwestern Argentina, a chain of towns linking the River Plate to the silver mines of Upper Peru.
governorate-of-tucuman.o: Spanish settlers from [[e:peru|Peru]] and [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] founded [[e:santiago-del-estero|Santiago del Estero]] in 1553, the oldest surviving city in [[s:argentine-republic|Argentina]]. In 1563 [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II]] created the [[e:governorate|Governorate]] of Tucumán, Juríes and [[e:diaguita|Diaguitas]], separating it from Chile and placing it under the [[e:audiencia|Audiencia]] of [[e:upper-peru|Charcas]], with [[s:spanish-jamaica|Santiago]] del Estero as capital.
governorate-of-tucuman.r: Governors founded a series of towns, including [[e:san-miguel-de-tucuman|San Miguel de Tucumán]] in 1565, [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]] in 1573, [[e:salta|Salta]] in 1582 and [[e:san-salvador-de-jujuy|San Salvador de Jujuy]] in 1593. The economy supplied mules, [[e:cattle|cattle]], textiles and foodstuffs to [[e:potosi|Potosí]]. The [[e:diaguita|Diaguita]] and Calchaquí peoples resisted in the [[e:calchaqui-wars|Calchaquí Wars]] until the 1660s. The [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] founded the [[e:national-university-of-cordoba|University of Córdoba]] in 1613, the oldest in [[s:argentine-republic|Argentina]], and ran estancias in the region.
governorate-of-tucuman.e: Tucumán became part of the [[s:viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata]] in 1776. In 1782 the intendancy reform divided it into the intendancies of [[e:salta|Salta]] del Tucumán and [[e:cordoba|Córdoba]] del Tucumán, which later became the provinces of northwestern [[s:argentine-republic|Argentina]].

governorate-of-new-toledo.t: The Spanish governorate granted to Diego de Almagro south of Pizarro's lands, whose disputed border over Cusco sparked the civil wars of the conquerors.
governorate-of-new-toledo.o: In 1534 [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] granted [[e:diego-de-almagro|Diego de Almagro]], [[e:francisco-pizarro|Francisco Pizarro's]] partner in the conquest of [[e:peru|Peru]], a governorate of 200 leagues south of the [[s:governorate-of-new-castile|Governorate of New Castile]]. In 1535 Almagro led a large expedition south into [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]], crossing the [[s:andecavi|Andes]] with Spanish soldiers and thousands of indigenous auxiliaries, but found no rich lands.
governorate-of-new-toledo.r: New [[e:toledo|Toledo]] was more a claim than an administered territory. Its northern boundary was vague, and [[e:diego-de-almagro|Almagro]] insisted that [[e:cusco|Cusco]] lay within it. Returning from [[s:republic-of-chile|Chile]] in 1537, he seized Cusco from [[e:hernando-pizarro|Hernando]] and [[e:gonzalo-pizarro|Gonzalo Pizarro]] during the rebellion of [[e:manco-inca|Manco Inca]]. War between the two factions followed.
governorate-of-new-toledo.e: [[e:diego-de-almagro|Almagro]] was defeated at the [[e:battle-of-las-salinas|Battle of Las Salinas]] in 1538 and executed. His son, [[e:diego-de-almagro-the-younger|Diego de Almagro the Younger]], had [[e:francisco-pizarro|Pizarro]] murdered in 1541 but was defeated at [[e:battle-of-chupas|Chupas]] in 1542 and executed. That year the [[e:new-laws|New Laws]] merged both [[e:governorate|governorates]] into the [[s:viceroyalty-of-peru|Viceroyalty of Peru]].

grand-principality-of-serbia.t: Medieval Serbian state of Raška, where Stefan Nemanja united the Serbian lands and founded the dynasty that ruled Serbia for two centuries.
grand-principality-of-serbia.o: As [[s:duklja|Duklja]] declined in the late 11th century, Raška in the inland highlands gained independence under [[e:grand-zupan|Grand Župan]] [[e:vukan-of-raska|Vukan]], who from about 1091 raided Byzantine territory. His successors of the [[e:vukanovic-dynasty|Vukanović]] line ruled from [[e:ras|Ras]], often as Byzantine or Hungarian clients.
grand-principality-of-serbia.r: The grand župan ruled with regional lords (župans) and an assembly of nobles. [[e:stefan-nemanja|Stefan Nemanja]] (1166–1196) defeated his brothers, annexed [[s:duklja|Duklja]], [[s:travunia|Travunia]] and [[s:zachlumia|Zachlumia]] around 1186, and founded [[e:studenica-monastery|Studenica]] monastery. His youngest son, [[e:saint-sava|Rastko]], became the monk [[e:sava|Sava]] and helped establish Serbian [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] monasticism at [[e:hilandar|Hilandar]] on [[s:monastic-community-of-mount-athos|Mount Athos]]. Byzantine and Hungarian pressure shaped its politics.
grand-principality-of-serbia.e: [[e:stefan-nemanja|Nemanja]] abdicated in 1196 in favour of his son Stefan, who received a royal crown from [[e:pope-honorius-iii|Pope Honorius III]] in 1217. The state became the [[s:kingdom-of-serbia-medieval|Kingdom of Serbia (medieval)]], ruled by the [[e:nemanjic-dynasty|Nemanjić dynasty]].

grand-principality-of-tver.t: Moscow's great rival for leadership of north-eastern Russia, whose princes held the throne of Vladimir before Moscow annexed Tver in 1485.
grand-principality-of-tver.o: Tver, on the upper [[e:volga|Volga]], received its first prince around 1247, when [[e:yaroslav-of-tver|Yaroslav Yaroslavich]], a younger brother of [[e:alexander-nevsky|Alexander Nevsky]], made it his seat. Yaroslav became grand prince of Vladimir in 1264, and Tver quickly grew into one of the strongest towns of the [[s:vladimir-suzdal|Vladimir-Suzdal]] lands.
grand-principality-of-tver.r: Tver controlled [[e:volga|Volga]] trade and built early stone churches and fortifications. [[e:mikhail-of-tver|Mikhail Yaroslavich]] became grand prince of Vladimir in 1305 but was executed at the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] in 1318 after a struggle with [[e:moscow|Moscow]]. In 1327 a revolt in Tver killed the Mongol envoy [[e:chol-khan|Cholkhan]], and [[e:ivan-i-of-moscow|Ivan Kalita of Moscow]] joined the [[e:tatars|Tatars]] in crushing it. The merchant [[e:afanasy-nikitin|Afanasy Nikitin]] set out from Tver for [[e:india|India]] in the 1460s.
grand-principality-of-tver.e: Under [[e:boris-of-tver|Boris Alexandrovich]] Tver revived in the 15th century, but it was surrounded by [[e:moscow|Moscow's]] territory. When its last prince, [[e:mikhail-borisovich-of-tver|Mikhail Borisovich]], sought Lithuanian help, [[e:ivan-iii|Ivan III]] besieged the city and annexed it to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]] in 1485.

grenada.t: Spice island independent since 1974, scene of a socialist revolution in 1979 and a US invasion in 1983.
grenada.o: The [[s:colony-of-grenada|Colony of Grenada]] became independent on 7 February 1974 under [[e:eric-gairy|Eric Gairy]], amid strikes and protests against his rule and his feared [[e:mongoose-gang|Mongoose Gang]]. It remained a [[e:commonwealth-of-nations|Commonwealth]] realm with the British monarch as head of state.
grenada.r: On 13 March 1979 the New Jewel Movement led by [[e:maurice-bishop|Maurice Bishop]] overthrew [[e:eric-gairy|Gairy]] and formed the [[e:peoples-revolutionary-government-grenada|People's Revolutionary Government]], the first revolution in the English-speaking [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]]. It expanded literacy, health and cooperatives, allied with [[e:cuba|Cuba]], which helped build the [[e:maurice-bishop-international-airport|Point Salines]] airport, and postponed elections. A rival faction under [[e:bernard-coard|Bernard Coard]] placed [[e:bishop|Bishop]] under arrest, and on 19 October 1983 Bishop and several ministers were executed.
grenada.e: On 25 October 1983 the [[s:united-states|United States]] and [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] allies invaded, removing the military council. Elections in 1984 restored parliamentary rule. [[e:keith-mitchell|Keith Mitchell]] served as prime minister for many years, [[e:hurricane-ivan|Hurricane Ivan]] wrecked the island in 2004, and [[e:dickon-mitchell|Dickon Mitchell]] took office in 2022.

generalitat-of-catalonia-1931-1939.t: Catalonia's autonomous government under the Second Republic, restored after two centuries and abolished after Franco's victory.
generalitat-of-catalonia-1931-1939.o: On 14 April 1931 [[e:francesc-macia|Francesc Macià]] of the Republican Left of [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]] proclaimed a [[s:catalan-republic-1641|Catalan Republic]] in [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]]. After negotiations with [[e:madrid|Madrid]] it became an autonomous government that took the medieval name of the Generalitat, and the [[e:statute-of-autonomy-of-catalonia-1932|Statute of Autonomy]] was approved in 1932.
generalitat-of-catalonia-1931-1939.r: The Generalitat had its own parliament and powers over education, culture, public order and [[e:civil-law|civil law]], and promoted the Catalan language. [[e:lluis-companys|Lluís Companys]] succeeded [[e:francesc-macia|Macià]] in 1933. In October 1934 Companys proclaimed a Catalan State within a federal republic, leading to his arrest and the statute's suspension until 1936. During the civil war it ran much of the Republican war effort in [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]].
generalitat-of-catalonia-1931-1939.e: Nationalist forces took [[e:barcelona|Barcelona]] in January 1939, and [[e:francisco-franco|Franco]] abolished the autonomy. [[e:lluis-companys|Companys]] was handed over by the [[e:gestapo|Gestapo]] and executed in 1940. The Generalitat survived in exile and was restored in 1977.

guam.t: The largest island of the Marianas, a Spanish colony for two centuries and an American territory since 1898, now a key US military base in the Pacific.
guam.o: The [[e:chamorro-people|Chamorro people]] settled Guam some 3,500 years ago. [[e:ferdinand-magellan|Magellan]] reached it in 1521, and [[e:spain|Spain]] colonised it from 1668, when the [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] [[e:diego-luis-de-san-vitores|Diego Luis de San Vitores]] founded a mission; wars and disease drastically reduced the Chamorro. In 1898, during the [[e:spanish-american-war|Spanish-American War]], the cruiser [[e:uss-charleston-c-2|USS Charleston]] captured the island, and Spain ceded it to the [[s:united-states|United States]].
guam.r: The [[e:united-states-navy|US Navy]] governed Guam as a naval station, while the rest of the [[e:mariana-islands|Marianas]] went to [[e:germany|Germany]] and then [[e:japan|Japan]]. Japan occupied Guam from December 1941 until American forces retook it in July 1944, an ordeal still commemorated on Liberation Day. The [[e:guam-organic-act-of-1950|Organic Act]] of 1950 made Guamanians US citizens and created a civilian government, though they cannot vote for president.
guam.e: Guam elected its first governor, [[e:carlos-camacho|Carlos Camacho]], in 1970. It remains an unincorporated territory of the [[s:united-states|United States]], dependent on military bases such as [[e:andersen-air-force-base|Andersen Air Force Base]] and on tourism, with continuing debate over its political status.

genoese-gazaria.t: Genoa's string of trading colonies on the Crimean coast, centred on Caffa, a hub of the Black Sea slave, grain and silk trades.
genoese-gazaria.o: After the restoration of the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]] in 1261 gave [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] access to the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]], Genoese merchants obtained the right to settle at [[e:feodosia|Caffa]], modern [[s:theodosia|Feodosia]], from the khan of the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] around 1266. Over the next century they added [[e:sudak|Soldaia]], now Sudak, in 1365 and [[e:balaklava|Cembalo]], now Balaklava.
genoese-gazaria.r: [[e:feodosia|Caffa]] was governed by a consul sent from [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] and supervised by the Office of Gazaria there. Its merchants traded grain, fish, [[e:fur-trade|furs]] and especially slaves, many sold to [[e:mamluk-sultanate|Mamluk Egypt]], as well as [[e:silk|silk]] and [[e:spice-trade|spices]] from the [[e:silk-road|Silk Road]]. Relations with the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] were tense: during a siege by [[e:jani-beg|Jani Beg]] in 1346 plague broke out, and ships from Caffa may have helped carry it to [[e:europe|Europe]].
genoese-gazaria.e: After 1453 [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]] handed the colonies to the [[e:bank-of-saint-george|Bank of San Giorgio]], as the [[s:ottoman-empire|Ottoman Empire]] controlled the straits. In 1475 an Ottoman fleet under [[e:gedik-ahmed-pasha|Gedik Ahmed Pasha]] took [[e:feodosia|Caffa]] and the other colonies, ending Italian rule in the [[e:crimea|Crimea]].

government-of-the-grand-national-assembl.t: The Ankara government of Mustafa Kemal, which won the Turkish War of Independence and replaced the Ottoman Empire with the Turkish Republic.
government-of-the-grand-national-assembl.o: After the [[e:allies|Allies]] formally occupied [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in March 1920, nationalist deputies and delegates met in [[e:ankara|Ankara]] and on 23 April 1920 opened the [[e:grand-national-assembly-of-turkey|Grand National Assembly]], which claimed [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] in the name of the nation. [[e:mustafa-kemal-ataturk|Mustafa Kemal]] was elected its president.
government-of-the-grand-national-assembl.r: The assembly governed directly through ministers it elected and adopted a constitution in 1921 vesting [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] in the nation. It rejected the [[e:treaty-of-sevres|Treaty of Sevres]], signed treaties with [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] at [[e:moscow|Moscow]] and [[e:kars|Kars]], and secured French withdrawal by the [[e:treaty-of-ankara-1921|Treaty of Ankara]]. Its army stopped the [[e:greeks|Greeks]] at [[e:battle-of-sakarya|Sakarya]] in 1921 and drove them out in 1922 under [[e:mustafa-kemal-ataturk|Mustafa Kemal]] and [[e:ismet-inonu|Ismet]].
government-of-the-grand-national-assembl.e: The assembly abolished the Ottoman sultanate in November 1922, won recognition in the [[e:treaty-of-lausanne|Treaty of Lausanne]] of July 1923, and proclaimed the [[s:republic-of-turkey|Republic of Turkey]] on 29 October 1923.

grand-principality-of-nizhny-novgorod-su.t: A powerful Volga principality that briefly rivalled Moscow and commissioned the Laurentian Codex of the Primary Chronicle.
grand-principality-of-nizhny-novgorod-su.o: [[e:nizhny-novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]] was founded in 1221 at the meeting of the [[e:oka-river|Oka]] and the [[e:volga|Volga]] as a frontier fortress against [[s:volga-bulgaria|Volga Bulgaria]]. In 1341 the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]] granted it to [[e:konstantin-vasilyevich-of-suzdal|Konstantin Vasilyevich of Suzdal]], who moved his capital there and created a new grand principality.
grand-principality-of-nizhny-novgorod-su.r: The principality grew rich on [[e:volga|Volga]] trade with the Horde and the East. [[e:dmitry-of-suzdal|Dmitry Konstantinovich]] held the grand-princely title of Vladimir from 1360 to 1363 before giving way to [[e:dmitry-donskoy|Dmitry Donskoy]], who married his daughter [[e:eudokia-dmitriyevna|Evdokia]]. In 1377 the monk Lavrenty copied the oldest surviving [[e:manuscript|manuscript]] of the [[e:primary-chronicle|Primary Chronicle]] for him.
grand-principality-of-nizhny-novgorod-su.e: Raids by [[e:tatars|Tatar]] [[e:emir|emirs]] and quarrels among Dmitry's brothers weakened the state. In 1392 [[e:vasily-i-of-moscow|Vasily I of Moscow]] bought the right to [[e:nizhny-novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]] from Khan [[e:tokhtamysh|Tokhtamysh]] and annexed it to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]], though the [[e:suzdal|Suzdal]] princes struggled to regain it for decades.

grand-duchy-of-hesse.t: Hesse-Darmstadt as a grand duchy, a constitutional state on both banks of the Rhine and home of the Darmstadt Artists' Colony.
grand-duchy-of-hesse.o: [[e:louis-i-grand-duke-of-hesse|Landgrave Louis X]] of Hesse-[[e:darmstadt|Darmstadt]] joined the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] in 1806 and took the title Grand Duke Louis I, adding mediatised territories to the [[s:duchy-of-westphalia|Duchy of Westphalia]], which he had gained in 1803. In 1816 he exchanged [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]] for [[e:rhenish-hesse|Rhenish Hesse]] with [[e:mainz|Mainz]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-worms|Worms]] on the left bank.
grand-duchy-of-hesse.r: A constitution of 1820 established a two-chamber parliament. The state combined Lutheran [[e:upper-hesse|Upper Hesse]] and [[e:starkenburg|Starkenburg]] with Catholic [[e:rhenish-hesse|Rhenish Hesse]], and [[e:mainz|Mainz]] was a federal fortress. The family married into royal houses: Princess [[e:alexandra-feodorovna-alix-of-hesse|Alix]] became Empress Alexandra of [[e:russia|Russia]]. [[e:ernest-louis-grand-duke-of-hesse|Grand Duke Ernest Louis]] founded the [[e:darmstadt-artists-colony|Darmstadt Artists' Colony]] on the [[e:mathildenhohe|Mathildenhöhe]] in 1899, a centre of [[e:art-nouveau|Jugendstil]].
grand-duchy-of-hesse.e: [[e:hesse|Hesse]] sided with [[e:austria|Austria]] in 1866 and lost Hesse-Homburg and some districts to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], but survived and joined the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]]. [[e:ernest-louis-grand-duke-of-hesse|Ernest Louis]] was deposed in November 1918, and the state became the [[s:peoples-state-of-hesse|People's State of Hesse]].

gallaecia.t: The late Roman province of north-western Iberia, created by Diocletian and soon to become the home of the Suebic kingdom.
gallaecia.o: Gallaecia was formed around 293 by [[e:diocletian|Diocletian's]] reform, which split [[s:hispania-tarraconensis|Hispania Tarraconensis]] into smaller provinces. It covered the lands of the [[s:callaeci|Callaeci]] and [[s:astures|Astures]], from the [[e:douro|Douro]] to the [[e:bay-of-biscay|Bay of Biscay]], with [[e:bracara-augusta|Bracara Augusta]] (Braga) as its capital.
gallaecia.r: A governor ran the province under the [[s:diocese-of-hispania|Diocese of Hispania]]. Its economy was rural, based on farming, herding and the remains of the gold-mining industry around [[e:asturica-augusta|Asturica Augusta]]. Towns such as [[e:lucus-augusti|Lucus Augusti]] (Lugo), with its surviving walls, were fortified in the late 3rd century. [[e:christianity|Christianity]] spread, and the ascetic movement of [[e:priscillian|Priscillian]], executed in 385, found strong support here.
gallaecia.e: In 409 [[s:suebi|Suebi]] and [[e:vandals|Hasding Vandals]] entered Gallaecia, and the Suebi made it the centre of their kingdom. Roman rule faded, as recorded by [[e:hydatius|Hydatius]], [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[e:aquae-flaviae|Aquae Flaviae]], and the name lived on in the medieval [[s:kingdom-of-galicia|Kingdom of Galicia]].

ghaznavid-empire.t: A Turkic dynasty from Ghazni whose sultan Mahmud raided deep into India and whose court fostered Persian literature, including Ferdowsi's Shahnameh.
ghaznavid-empire.o: [[e:sabuktigin|Sabuktigin]], a Turkic slave soldier in the service of the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanid Empire]], became governor of [[e:ghazni|Ghazni]] in 977. His son Mahmud took power in 998, seized [[e:khorasan|Khurasan]] in 999 and threw off [[e:samanid-empire|Samanid]] authority, gaining recognition from the Abbasid [[e:caliphate|caliph]].
ghaznavid-empire.r: [[e:mahmud-of-ghazni|Mahmud of Ghazni]] launched some seventeen raids into [[e:india|India]] between 1001 and 1026, defeating the [[s:hindu-shahis|Hindu Shahis]] and sacking [[e:somnath-temple|Somnath]], which brought vast wealth to [[e:ghazni|Ghazni]]. The empire relied on a standing army of slave soldiers and [[e:war-elephant|war elephants]], while Persian administration and culture flourished: the poet Ferdowsi completed the [[e:shahnameh|Shahnameh]], and al-Biruni wrote his study of India under Ghaznavid patronage.
ghaznavid-empire.e: The [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]] defeated [[e:masud-i-of-ghazni|Mas'ud I]] at [[e:battle-of-dandanaqan|Dandanaqan]] in 1040, taking [[e:khorasan|Khurasan]]. The Ghaznavids continued in eastern [[s:islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-present|Afghanistan]] and the [[e:punjab|Punjab]], ruling from [[e:lahore|Lahore]] after the [[s:ghurid-sultanate|Ghurid Sultanate]] sacked [[e:ghazni|Ghazni]] in 1150, until the Ghurids took Lahore in 1186.

guarco.t: A coastal lordship of the Cañete valley that resisted the Incas for years, with its stronghold at Cerro Azul by the Pacific.
guarco.o: The lordship of Guarco, or Huarco, emerged in the lower [[e:canete-river|Cañete]] valley south of [[e:lima|Lima]] around 1100. It developed around fishing villages and irrigation, with a fortified centre at [[e:cerro-azul-peru|Cerro Azul]], a headland on the Pacific coast, and the fortress of Ungará.
guarco.r: Guarco was ruled by local lords who controlled farmland and fishing. Excavations at [[e:cerro-azul-peru|Cerro Azul]] have shown large compounds used to store dried fish, especially anchovies and sardines, which were traded inland for farm goods. Society seems to have been organised around elite families who controlled food stores and labour.
guarco.e: According to the chronicler [[e:pedro-cieza-de-leon|Pedro Cieza de León]], Guarco resisted the [[e:inca-empire|Incas]] for several years in the time of [[e:tupac-inca-yupanqui|Túpac Inca Yupanqui]]. After its fall around 1470 the Incas built the fortress and administrative centre of [[e:incawasi|Incawasi]] in the [[e:canete-river|Cañete]] valley. The region came under Spanish rule in the 1530s.

ganja-khanate.t: A khanate centred on the city of Ganja whose last khan, Javad Khan, died defending it against the Russian storm of 1804.
ganja-khanate.o: After [[e:nader-shah|Nader Shah's]] death in 1747, Shahverdi Khan of the Ziyadoghlu branch of the [[e:qajar-dynasty|Qajar]] tribe, whose family had long governed [[e:ganja-azerbaijan|Ganja]] and [[e:karabakh|Karabakh]] for the [[e:safavid-empire|Safavids]], made Ganja an independent khanate. It covered the fertile plain between the [[e:kura-river|Kura]] and the Lesser [[e:caucasus|Caucasus]].
ganja-khanate.r: The khans ruled a town of craftsmen and merchants and surrounding villages producing grain, [[e:silk|silk]] and fruit. Pressed by the [[s:karabakh-khanate|Karabakh Khanate]] and [[s:georgia|Georgia]], the khanate paid tribute to [[e:erekle-ii|Erekle II]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti|Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti]] for decades. [[e:javad-khan|Javad Khan]], who ruled from 1786, rebuilt its strength and sided with [[s:qajar-iran|Qajar Iran]] against [[e:georgia|Georgia]] and [[e:russia|Russia]].
ganja-khanate.e: In January 1804 Russian troops under [[e:pavel-tsitsianov|Pavel Tsitsianov]] stormed [[e:ganja-azerbaijan|Ganja]], and [[e:javad-khan|Javad Khan]] was killed with his son. The [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]] annexed the khanate and renamed the city Elizavetpol; it regained the name Ganja in the 20th century.

ganden-phodrang.t: The government of the Dalai Lamas, founded in 1642, which ruled Tibet from Lhasa and the Potala Palace for three centuries.
ganden-phodrang.o: In 1642 [[e:gushi-khan|Güshi Khan]] of the [[s:khoshut-khanate|Khoshut Khanate]] defeated the [[s:tsangpa-dynasty|Tsangpa dynasty]] and conferred authority over [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] on the [[e:5th-dalai-lama|Fifth Dalai Lama]], Ngawang Lobsang Gyatso. The government took its name from the [[e:dalai-lama|Dalai Lama's]] residence at [[e:drepung-monastery|Drepung]] monastery and soon moved to the [[e:potala-palace|Potala Palace]], built in [[e:lhasa|Lhasa]] from 1645.
ganden-phodrang.r: [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] was governed by the [[e:dalai-lama|Dalai Lamas]] or their regents with a council of ministers (the [[e:kashag|Kashag]], formalised in 1751) and a dual service of monk and lay officials. The [[e:gelug|Gelug]] school dominated, and monasteries held vast estates. After intervening against the [[e:dzungars|Dzungars]] in 1720, the [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]] stationed ambans in [[e:lhasa|Lhasa]] and introduced the [[e:golden-urn|Golden Urn]] in 1793, though their real authority fluctuated.
ganden-phodrang.e: The British expedition under [[e:francis-younghusband|Younghusband]] reached [[e:lhasa|Lhasa]] in 1904, and [[e:qing-empire|Qing]] troops occupied it in 1910, driving the [[e:thubten-gyatso|Thirteenth Dalai Lama]] into exile in [[e:india|India]]. After the Qing fell, [[e:tibetans|Tibetans]] expelled the Chinese garrison in 1912, and the same government continued as [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] (1912-1951).

gotland.t: Self-governing farmers' republic on the Baltic island of Gotland, rich from trade, which kept its own law and assembly until a Danish conquest in 1361.
gotland.o: Gotland's position in the middle of the Baltic made it a trading hub from the [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. Its picture stones and more than 700 [[e:viking-age|Viking Age]] [[e:silver|silver]] hoards, including the [[e:spillings-hoard|Spillings hoard]], show immense wealth from trade with Rus', the Islamic world and [[e:western-europe|Western Europe]]. The [[e:gutasaga|Gutasaga]] records an agreement under which the islanders paid a yearly tribute to the king of the [[e:svear|Svear]] in return for protection.
gotland.r: Free farmers governed themselves through the [[e:gutnalthing|Gutnalthing]], the island's general assembly, which met at [[e:romani-people|Roma]], and wrote down their own law, the [[e:gutalag|Gutalag]]. Every farmer was also a trader, and Gotlanders held privileges in Novgorod and across the Baltic. In the 12th and 13th centuries the island was covered with stone churches, and [[s:visby|Visby]] grew into a German-dominated Hanseatic town.
gotland.e: Tension between rural Gotlanders and [[s:visby|Visby]] led to civil war in 1288. In 1361 [[e:valdemar-iv-of-denmark|Valdemar IV of Denmark]] invaded, massacring the farmers' army outside Visby. Gotland then passed among [[e:denmark|Denmark]], [[e:piracy|pirates]] and the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]], and became Swedish in 1645 by the [[e:treaty-of-bromsebro-1645|Treaty of Brömsebro]].

galuh-kingdom.t: A Sundanese kingdom in the eastern Priangan of West Java, the twin and rival of the Sunda Kingdom until their union in 1482.
galuh-kingdom.o: According to Sundanese tradition, chiefly the 16th-century [[e:carita-parahyangan|Carita Parahyangan]], Galuh emerged around 669 when the lands of [[s:tarumanagara|Tarumanagara]] divided along the [[e:citarum-river|Citarum River]], Galuh taking the east and the [[s:sunda-kingdom|Sunda Kingdom]] the west. Its legendary founder Wretikandayun is said to have ruled from near [[e:ciamis|Ciamis]].
galuh-kingdom.r: Galuh was an inland [[e:rice|rice]]-growing realm with [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] and indigenous Sundanese religious traditions. Its best-attested period is the 14th and 15th centuries, when kings ruled from Kawali. The [[e:astana-gede|Astana Gede]] inscriptions there record [[e:niskala-wastu-kancana|Prabu Raja Wastu]], identified with Niskala Wastu Kancana, fortifying the town and urging his successors to rule justly.
galuh-kingdom.e: In 1482 [[e:sri-baduga-maharaja|Jayadewata]], known as Sri Baduga [[e:maharaja|Maharaja]], inherited both thrones and moved the united court to [[s:sunda-kingdom|Pakuan Pajajaran]], merging Galuh into the Sunda Kingdom. Galuh later came under [[e:cirebon|Cirebon]] and [[s:mataram-sultanate|Mataram]], and its name survives in [[e:ciamis|Ciamis]] regional identity.

gangani-ireland.t: People of western Ireland recorded by Ptolemy near the Shannon estuary, sharing their name with the Gangani of north-west Wales.
gangani-ireland.o: [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150 places the [[s:gangani-britain|Gangani]] on the west coast of Ireland, south of the [[s:auteini|Auteini]] and north of the [[s:velabri|Velabri]], usually located in [[e:county-clare|County Clare]] or around the mouth of the [[e:river-shannon|Shannon]]. The same name is given to a headland in [[e:wales|Wales]], home of the Gangani ([[s:united-kingdom|Britain]]), on the [[e:llyn-peninsula|Llŷn]] peninsula.
gangani-ireland.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers or customs. The shared name on both sides of the [[e:irish-sea|Irish Sea]] has been taken as evidence of migration, of an Irish group settled in [[e:wales|Wales]], or simply of a common Celtic word, perhaps connected with Irish legends of the Gamanrad, but none of these ideas can be proven.
gangani-ireland.e: The [[s:gangani-britain|Gangani]] of Ireland do not appear in later sources. Their region later formed part of the [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Kingdom of Munster]] and the lands of peoples such as the [[s:ui-fidgenti|Ui Fidgenti]].

grand-principality-of-ryazan.t: A frontier principality on the Oka, first to fall to the Mongols in 1237 and the last major Russian land absorbed by Moscow.
grand-principality-of-ryazan.o: [[e:ryazan|Ryazan]] on the middle [[e:oka-river|Oka]] belonged to the Chernigov dynasty and was ruled together with [[e:murom|Murom]]. Around 1129 the two lands separated, and Ryazan became a principality of its own under descendants of [[e:yaroslav-sviatoslavich|Yaroslav Sviatoslavich]], bordering the steppe and the forest lands of the [[e:mordvins|Mordvins]].
grand-principality-of-ryazan.r: Its princes were frequently at war with [[s:vladimir-suzdal|Vladimir-Suzdal]] and later the [[s:grand-duchy-of-moscow|Grand Duchy of Moscow]], while facing steppe raids from the south. In December 1237 [[e:batu-khan|Batu]]'s [[e:mongols|Mongols]] destroyed the old city and killed Prince [[e:yuri-igorevich-of-ryazan|Yuri Igorevich]], an event later told in the tale of [[e:evpaty-kolovrat|Evpaty Kolovrat]]. The capital moved to [[e:ryazan|Pereyaslavl-Ryazansky]], the modern city of Ryazan.
grand-principality-of-ryazan.e: [[e:oleg-ii-of-ryazan|Oleg Ivanovich]], who ruled for most of 1350 to 1402, stood up to [[e:dmitry-donskoy|Dmitry Donskoy]] and kept out of the Battle of Kulikovo. Afterwards [[e:moscow|Moscow's]] influence grew steadily, and in 1521 [[e:vasily-iii-of-moscow|Vasily III]] arrested [[e:ivan-ivanovich-of-ryazan|Ivan Ivanovich]], the last grand prince, and annexed [[e:ryazan|Ryazan]].

guge.t: A kingdom of western Tibet founded by descendants of the Tibetan emperors, whose kings sparked the revival of Buddhism in Tibet and whose ruined capital Tsaparang still stands.
guge.o: After the [[s:tibetan-empire|Tibetan Empire]] collapsed, [[e:kyide-nyimagon|Kyide Nyimagon]], a descendant of its royal line, settled in western [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] in the 10th century. His territories were divided among his sons, and one line ruled Guge and [[e:purang|Purang]] in the upper [[e:sutlej-river|Sutlej]] valley, later with its capital at [[e:tsaparang|Tsaparang]].
guge.r: The kings [[e:yeshe-o|Yeshe-Ö]] and [[e:jangchub-o|Jangchub-Ö]] were great patrons of [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]]. They founded [[e:tholing-monastery|Tholing]] monastery in 996, sent the translator [[e:rinchen-zangpo|Rinchen Zangpo]] to [[e:kashmir|Kashmir]] and invited the Indian teacher [[e:atisha|Atisha]], who arrived in 1042, beginning the later diffusion of Buddhism in [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]]. Guge grew rich on gold, wool and the trade across the [[e:himalayas|Himalaya]], and its temples hold outstanding murals.
guge.e: In 1624 the [[e:jesuits|Jesuit]] [[e:antonio-de-andrade|António de Andrade]] founded a mission at [[e:tsaparang|Tsaparang]] with royal favour, angering the monastic establishment. In 1630 the [[s:kingdom-of-ladakh|Kingdom of Ladakh]] invaded with local support and ended the dynasty. Western [[s:tibet-1912-1951|Tibet]] passed to the [[s:ganden-phodrang|Ganden Phodrang]] in the 1680s.

gibraltar.t: A British territory on the rock at the entrance to the Mediterranean, held since 1704 and still claimed by Spain.
gibraltar.o: An Anglo-[[e:dutch|Dutch]] fleet under Admiral [[e:george-rooke|George Rooke]] captured Gibraltar in 1704 during the [[e:war-of-the-spanish-succession|War of the Spanish Succession]], nominally for the [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] claimant Charles. [[e:spain|Spain]] ceded the town and fortress to [[s:kingdom-of-great-britain|Great Britain]] in perpetuity by Article X of the [[e:treaty-of-utrecht|Treaty of Utrecht]] in 1713.
gibraltar.r: Gibraltar became a fortress and naval base guarding the Strait, surviving the Great Siege of 1779-1783 and serving as a key base in the Napoleonic and World Wars. Its mixed population of Genoese, Spanish, Maltese, Jewish and British origin developed a distinct identity and the [[e:llanito|Llanito]] speech. It became a [[e:crown-colony|Crown colony]] in 1830.
gibraltar.e: [[e:spain|Spain]] pressed its claim at the UN; Gibraltarians voted to stay British in 1967, and Spain closed the land border from 1969 to 1985. In 2002 they rejected shared [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]]. Today it is a self-governing [[e:british-overseas-territories|British Overseas Territory]], with its border regime negotiated after [[e:brexit|Brexit]].
