ghassanids.t: Christian Arab kings who guarded Byzantium's desert frontier for over a century and patronised the Miaphysite church in Syria.
ghassanids.o: The [[s:ghassanid-kingdom|Ghassanids]] were part of the Azd, a tribal group that migrated north from [[e:south-arabia|South Arabia]]. Entering Roman territory in the late 5th century, they defeated the [[s:salihids|Salihids]] and around 502 made a treaty with the emperor [[e:anastasius-i-dicorus|Anastasius]] that made them the empire's chief Arab allies in [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] and [[e:arabia|Arabia]].
ghassanids.r: Justinian made [[e:al-harith-ibn-jabala|al-Harith ibn Jabala]] supreme phylarch and king over all [[e:rome|Rome's]] Arab allies around 529 to counter the [[s:lakhmid-kingdom|Lakhmids]], [[e:persia|Persia's]] clients; he killed the Lakhmid king al-[[e:al-mundhir-iii|Mundhir III]] in battle in 554. The [[s:ghassanid-kingdom|Ghassanids]] moved between camps such as [[e:jabiyah|Jabiyah]] in the [[e:golan-heights|Golan]], built churches and towers, and fervently supported Miaphysite [[e:christianity|Christianity]], obtaining the consecration of [[e:jacob-baradaeus|Jacob Baradaeus]] as [[e:bishop|bishop]]. Their court attracted Arabic poets such as [[e:al-nabigha-al-dhubyani|al-Nabigha]] and [[e:hassan-ibn-thabit|Hassan ibn Thabit]].
ghassanids.e: In 581 the emperor Maurice arrested [[e:al-mundhir-ibn-al-harith|al-Mundhir ibn al-Harith]] and exiled him to [[e:sicily|Sicily]], and the confederation fragmented. Partly revived under [[e:heraclius|Heraclius]], the [[s:ghassanid-kingdom|Ghassanids]] fought for [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] at [[e:battle-of-the-yarmuk|Yarmuk]] in 636; afterwards some accepted [[e:islam|Islam]] and others, led by [[e:jabala-ibn-al-ayham|Jabala ibn al-Ayham]], withdrew into [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]].

gajapati-kingdom.t: The Suryavamsi kingdom of Odisha whose Gajapati kings, devotees of Jagannath at Puri, briefly ruled from the Ganges to the Kaveri.
gajapati-kingdom.o: In 1434 [[e:kapilendra-deva|Kapilendra Deva]], a minister and general of the last [[e:eastern-ganga-dynasty|Eastern Ganga]] king, seized the throne at [[e:cuttack|Cuttack]] and founded the Suryavamsi dynasty. He took the title Gajapati, lord of elephants, and launched campaigns that pushed the kingdom's frontiers south along the eastern coast and north into [[e:bengal|Bengal]].
gajapati-kingdom.r: [[e:kapilendra-deva|Kapilendra Deva]] conquered coastal [[e:andhra-region|Andhra]] from the [[s:reddi-kingdom|Reddi Kingdom]] and raided as far as the Kaveri, defeating the [[s:bahmani-sultanate|Bahmani Sultanate]] and the [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]]. The kings ruled as servants of [[e:jagannath|Jagannath]] of Puri, whose temple was the centre of state ritual. [[e:prataparudra-deva|Prataparudra Deva]] hosted the saint [[e:chaitanya-mahaprabhu|Chaitanya]], and [[e:odia-language|Odia]] literature flourished with [[e:sarala-das|Sarala Das's]] [[e:mahabharata|Mahabharata]].
gajapati-kingdom.e: [[e:krishnadevaraya|Krishnadevaraya]] of [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara]] took the southern provinces from [[e:prataparudra-deva|Prataparudra]], and the [[s:golconda-sultanate|Golconda Sultanate]] pressed from the south-west. In 1541 the minister [[e:govinda-vidyadhara|Govinda Vidyadhara]] killed the last Suryavamsi heirs and founded the [[s:bhoi-dynasty|Bhoi dynasty]].

ghodasar-state.t: A small chiefship of central Gujarat, one of the minor hereditary estates that survived under British protection.
ghodasar-state.o: Ghodasar was a small estate in the plains of central [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], held by a local chiefly family from around 1600. Little is recorded of its founding.
ghodasar-state.r: Its Thakor ruled a few villages and paid tribute to the overlords of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], the Mughal governors and later the [[e:gaekwads|Gaekwads of Baroda]], before coming under British supervision. Standard references give few details of its rulers.
ghodasar-state.e: Ghodasar was merged into [[s:bombay-presidency|Bombay Province]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960.

genoese-amasra.t: A Genoese trading colony on the Black Sea coast of Anatolia, protected by walls that still carry Genoese coats of arms.
genoese-amasra.o: After the [[e:treaty-of-nymphaeum-1261|Treaty of Nymphaeum]] of 1261 opened the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] to [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]], Genoese merchants established themselves at [[e:amasra|Amasra]] (Samastri), an old Byzantine port on a pair of headlands, which became one of their stations on the coast between [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] and [[s:genoese-gazaria|Caffa]].
genoese-amasra.r: [[e:amasra|Amasra]] was governed by Genoese consuls subordinate to the colonial authorities at [[e:galata|Pera]] and [[s:genoese-gazaria|Caffa]]. Its population was largely Greek, with [[e:latin|Latin]] merchants and soldiers. The town traded in [[e:timber|timber]], grain and slaves and served as a harbour of refuge. The Genoese strengthened its castle, and their inscriptions and arms survive in the walls.
genoese-amasra.e: In 1460 [[e:mehmed-ii|Mehmed II]] appeared before [[e:amasra|Amasra]] and the Genoese surrendered without a fight. Much of the population was moved to [[e:istanbul|Istanbul]].

gath.t: Gath, the largest Philistine city in the 10th and 9th centuries BCE, home of Goliath in the Bible, destroyed by Aram-Damascus.
gath.o: Gath, at Tell es-Safi in the Judaean foothills, was a Canaanite town before Philistine settlers arrived in the 12th century BCE. It became one of the five cities of the [[s:philistine-pentapolis|Philistine Pentapolis]], guarding the [[e:valley-of-elah|valley of Elah]] between the coastal plain and [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Judah]].
gath.r: By the 10th century BCE Gath was the leading Philistine city, covering some 50 hectares. The [[e:hebrew-bible|Bible]] tells of its king Achish sheltering [[e:david|David]] and of the giant [[e:goliath|Goliath]]; an inscription found at the site contains two names resembling Goliath. Its temples show a mix of [[e:aegean|Aegean]] and local traditions.
gath.e: Around 830 BCE [[e:hazael|Hazael]] of [[s:aram-damascus|Aram-Damascus]] besieged and destroyed Gath; the siege trench he dug has been excavated. The city never recovered its leading role.

government-of-national-unity.t: Arrow Cross regime of Ferenc Szálasi, installed by Germany in October 1944, which brought terror to Budapest in the final months of the war.
government-of-national-unity.o: On 15 October 1944 Regent [[e:miklos-horthy|Miklós Horthy]] announced that the [[s:kingdom-of-hungary-1920-1946|Kingdom of Hungary]] (1920-1946) was seeking an armistice with the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]]. [[e:germany|Germany]] kidnapped his son and forced Horthy to abdicate in favour of [[e:ferenc-szalasi|Ferenc Szálasi]], leader of the fascist [[e:arrow-cross-party|Arrow Cross Party]], who formed a Government of National Unity and took the title Leader of the Nation.
government-of-national-unity.r: The regime continued the war on [[e:germany|Germany's]] side, mobilising every remaining resource. [[e:arrow-cross-party|Arrow Cross]] militias murdered thousands of [[e:budapest|Budapest]] [[e:jews|Jews]], many shot into the [[e:danube|Danube]], and tens of thousands were sent on death marches towards [[e:austria|Austria]], while diplomats such as [[e:raoul-wallenberg|Raoul Wallenberg]] issued protective papers. A rival provisional government was formed at [[e:debrecen|Debrecen]] under Soviet protection in December 1944.
government-of-national-unity.e: The Soviet siege of [[e:budapest|Budapest]] ended in February 1945, and [[e:ferenc-szalasi|Szálasi]]'s government retreated west before collapsing in April 1945. Szálasi was captured by American troops, handed over to [[e:hungary|Hungary]], and tried and executed in Budapest in 1946.

georgia.t: The independent republic of Georgia on the Black Sea, heir of ancient Kartli and Colchis, whose path since 1991 has been shaped by conflict with Russia and Western ambitions.
georgia.o: Georgia declared independence from the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] on 9 April 1991, two years after the [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]] massacre, restoring the legacy of the [[s:democratic-republic-of-georgia|Democratic Republic of Georgia]]. [[e:zviad-gamsakhurdia|Zviad Gamsakhurdia]] became president, but he was ousted in a civil war in the winter of 1991-1992, and [[e:eduard-shevardnadze|Eduard Shevardnadze]] returned to lead the country.
georgia.r: Wars in [[e:south-ossetia|South Ossetia]] and [[s:principality-of-abkhazia|Abkhazia]] in 1991-1993 left both regions outside [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi's]] control. The 2003 [[e:rose-revolution|Rose Revolution]] brought [[e:mikheil-saakashvili|Mikheil Saakashvili]] to power, who fought corruption and sought [[e:nato|NATO]] and EU membership. The 2008 war with [[e:russia|Russia]] ended with [[e:moscow|Moscow]] recognising both breakaway regions. Georgia's economy rests on transit, agriculture, wine and tourism.
georgia.e: The Georgian Dream party, founded by [[e:bidzina-ivanishvili|Bidzina Ivanishvili]], has governed since 2012. Georgia gained EU candidate status in 2023, but disputes over democracy and relations with [[e:russia|Russia]] brought mass protests in 2024.

grand-duchy-of-wurzburg.t: Napoleonic grand duchy formed from the secularised bishopric of Würzburg for Ferdinand of Tuscany, a Habsburg in Napoleon's camp.
grand-duchy-of-wurzburg.o: The [[s:prince-bishopric-of-wurzburg|Prince-Bishopric of Würzburg]] was secularised in 1803 and given to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. Under the [[e:peace-of-pressburg-1805|Peace of Pressburg]] in 1805, Bavaria handed it to [[e:ferdinand-iii-grand-duke-of-tuscany|Ferdinand III]], former [[e:grand-duke-of-tuscany|Grand Duke of Tuscany]], in exchange for [[e:salzburg|Salzburg]], and it became the Electorate of [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]]. Joining the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] in 1806, it was renamed a grand duchy.
grand-duchy-of-wurzburg.r: Ferdinand, a brother of Emperor [[e:francis-i|Francis I]], governed from the great baroque [[e:wurzburg-residence|Würzburg Residenz]], keeping a cultured court and a largely Catholic administration. The state was obliged to supply troops for [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] campaigns, including the invasion of [[e:russia|Russia]] in 1812. Wine growing on the Main was central to its economy.
grand-duchy-of-wurzburg.e: In 1814 Ferdinand recovered [[s:grand-duchy-of-tuscany|Tuscany]], and [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]] was returned to the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]], becoming part of the province of [[e:lower-franconia|Lower Franconia]]. Ferdinand's line, the Habsburg-Tuscany branch, ruled in [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]] until 1859.

getae.t: Thracian people of the lower Danube, followers of the god Zalmoxis, whose king Dromichaetes captured Lysimachus and whose lands formed the core of Dacia.
getae.o: [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] names the Getae among [[e:thracians|Thracians]] living south and north of the lower [[e:danube|Danube]] when [[e:darius-i|Darius I]] marched against the [[e:scythians|Scythians]] around 514 BCE; they alone resisted before being subdued. Their territory covered the Danube plain in modern [[s:bulgaria|Bulgaria]] and [[s:kingdom-of-romania|Romania]].
getae.r: Getic chiefs and kings ruled from fortified centres; the royal city of Helis is often identified with [[e:thracian-tomb-of-sveshtari|Sveshtari]], where a decorated tomb survives. [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] says the Getae believed in immortality through the god [[e:zalmoxis|Zalmoxis]]. Grain, horses and trade with Greek [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] cities such as [[s:histria|Histria]] shaped the economy. Around 292 BCE King [[e:dromichaetes|Dromichaetes]] defeated and captured [[e:lysimachus|Lysimachus]], then released him.
getae.e: Celtic incursions and pressure from [[e:kingdom-of-macedon|Macedon]] and [[e:rome|Rome]] fragmented Getic power. About 82 BCE [[e:burebista|Burebista]] united the Getae and [[e:dacians|Dacians]] into the [[s:kingdom-of-dacia|Kingdom of Dacia]]; Roman writers afterwards used Getae and Dacians almost interchangeably.

golden-ambrosian-republic.t: A short-lived Milanese republic proclaimed when the Visconti line ended in 1447, which fell to its own general Francesco Sforza.
golden-ambrosian-republic.o: When Duke [[e:filippo-maria-visconti|Filippo Maria Visconti]] died without a male heir in August 1447, a group of [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milanese]] nobles and lawyers proclaimed a republic named after the city's patron saint [[e:ambrose|Ambrose]]. Many subject cities of the Duchy of [[e:milan|Milan]] seized the chance to break away.
golden-ambrosian-republic.r: The republic was led by elected captains and defenders of liberty, but split between nobles and popular leaders. Threatened by the [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]], it hired [[e:francesco-sforza|Francesco Sforza]], husband of the late duke's illegitimate daughter [[e:bianca-maria-visconti|Bianca Maria]], who defeated the [[e:venice|Venetians]] at [[e:battle-of-caravaggio|Caravaggio]] in 1448. [[e:house-of-sforza|Sforza]] then made a separate peace with Venice and turned against [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]].
golden-ambrosian-republic.e: [[e:house-of-sforza|Sforza]] besieged the city, and in February 1450, with [[s:duchy-of-milan|Milan]] starving, the citizens opened the gates. He was acclaimed duke, restoring the Duchy of [[e:milan|Milan]] under the Sforza dynasty.

grand-duchy-of-posen.t: A Prussian province with limited Polish self-rule, created at the Congress of Vienna and stripped of its autonomy after the revolution of 1848.
grand-duchy-of-posen.o: At the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] in 1815 the western part of the [[s:duchy-of-warsaw|Duchy of Warsaw]], centred on [[e:poznan|Poznan]], was returned to the [[s:kingdom-of-prussia|Kingdom of Prussia]]. To reconcile its mainly Polish population, it was given the title of grand duchy and a promise of respect for Polish language and institutions.
grand-duchy-of-posen.r: The king of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] ruled through a Polish governor, Prince [[e:antoni-radziwill|Antoni Radziwill]], and the Polish language was used in schools and courts. After the [[e:november-uprising|November Uprising]] of 1830 in [[s:congress-poland|Congress Poland]], the provincial president [[e:eduard-flottwell|Eduard Flottwell]] began a policy of [[e:germanisation|Germanisation]]. Polish landowners and clergy led a lively cultural and economic life, including the [[e:bazar-poznan|Bazar]] in [[e:poznan|Poznan]].
grand-duchy-of-posen.e: In 1848 [[e:ludwik-mieroslawski|Ludwik Mieroslawski]] led a Polish uprising in the grand duchy, which Prussian troops crushed. Its special status was abolished, and it became the ordinary [[e:province-of-posen|Province of Posen]]. In 1919 most of it passed to the [[s:second-polish-republic|Second Polish Republic]].

german-samoa.t: Germany's Samoan colony on Upolu and Savaiʻi, governed by Wilhelm Solf through Samoan institutions until New Zealand occupied it in 1914.
german-samoa.o: [[e:germany|Germany]] had dominated [[e:samoan-islands|Samoa]]'s plantation economy since the 1850s through the firm [[e:j-c-godeffroy-and-sohn|Godeffroy]] and its successor, the [[e:deutsche-handels-und-plantagen-gesellschaft|DHPG]]. When the [[e:tripartite-convention-1899|Tripartite Convention of 1899]] partitioned the [[s:kingdom-of-samoa|Kingdom of Samoa]], Germany received the western islands of [[e:upolu|Upolu]] and [[e:savaii|Savaiʻi]], and the colony was proclaimed at [[e:apia|Apia]] on 1 March 1900.
german-samoa.r: Governor [[e:wilhelm-solf|Wilhelm Solf]], from 1900 to 1911, ruled indirectly through Samoan chiefs and protected Samoan land from further sale, while abolishing the contested kingship; [[e:mataafa-iosefo|Mataʻafa Iosefo]] was recognised as paramount chief. Coconut and cocoa plantations used labourers from [[e:china|China]] and the Melanesian islands. In 1909 the orator chief [[e:lauaki-namulauulu-mamoe|Lauaki Namulauʻulu Mamoe]] led the [[e:mau-movement|Mau]] a Pule protest and was exiled to [[e:saipan|Saipan]].
german-samoa.e: At the outbreak of the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]], a [[s:new-zealand|New Zealand]] force landed at [[e:apia|Apia]] on 29 August 1914 and took the colony without resistance. It was then governed as the [[s:territory-of-western-samoa|Territory of Western Samoa]].

grand-duchy-of-moscow.t: Muscovy, the small appanage that gathered the Russian lands, threw off Tatar rule and became the core of the Russian state.
grand-duchy-of-moscow.o: [[e:moscow|Moscow]], first mentioned in 1147, became the seat of its own prince around 1263, when [[e:alexander-nevsky|Alexander Nevsky's]] youngest son Daniel received it. Daniel and his sons enlarged the territory, and in 1325 the head of the Russian church moved to Moscow. In 1331 [[e:ivan-i-of-moscow|Ivan I Kalita]] became the sole grand prince of Vladimir, collecting tribute for the [[s:golden-horde|Golden Horde]].
grand-duchy-of-moscow.r: The grand princes built power by buying, conquering and inheriting neighbouring lands, aided by the church and loyal boyars. [[e:dmitry-donskoy|Dmitry Donskoy]] defeated the [[e:tatars|Tatars]] at [[e:battle-of-kulikovo|Kulikovo]] in 1380. [[e:ivan-iii|Ivan III]] annexed the [[s:novgorod-republic|Novgorod Republic]] and Tver, ended Horde overlordship at the [[e:great-stand-on-the-ugra-river|Ugra]] river in 1480, rebuilt the [[e:moscow-kremlin|Kremlin]] with Italian architects and issued a law code in 1497.
grand-duchy-of-moscow.e: [[e:vasily-iii-of-moscow|Vasily III]] completed the absorption of [[e:pskov|Pskov]] and [[s:grand-principality-of-ryazan|Ryazan]]. In 1547 his son [[e:ivan-iv-of-russia|Ivan IV]] was crowned tsar, and the grand duchy became the [[s:tsardom-of-russia|Tsardom of Russia]], the direct ancestor of the [[s:russian-empire|Russian Empire]].

gingee-nayaks.t: Telugu Nayaka governors of Vijayanagara who ruled northern Tamil country from the near-impregnable fortress of Gingee.
gingee-nayaks.o: The [[s:vijayanagara-empire|Vijayanagara Empire]] appointed [[e:nayaka|Nayaka]] governors to administer its Tamil provinces in the early 16th century. Around 1509 one line, traditionally founded by Tubaki Krishnappa Nayaka, was installed at [[e:gingee|Gingee]] (Senji), controlling the land between the [[e:palar-river|Palar]] and [[e:kollidam-river|Kollidam]] rivers, including the coast around [[e:pondicherry|Pondicherry]].
gingee-nayaks.r: The [[e:gingee|Gingee]] [[e:nayaka|Nayaks]] strengthened the hill fortress, linking three hills with walls to create one of the strongest forts in south [[e:india|India]]. Like the other Nayakas, they collected revenue through local military chiefs and patronised temples such as [[e:tiruvannamalai|Tiruvannamalai]]. After Vijayanagara's defeat in 1565 they acted increasingly independently, allowing the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] to set up a post at Tegnapatnam.
gingee-nayaks.e: Wars with the [[s:madurai-nayak-dynasty|Madurai Nayak dynasty]] and the [[s:thanjavur-nayak-kingdom|Thanjavur Nayak kingdom]] weakened them, and the [[s:bijapur-sultanate|Bijapur Sultanate]] captured [[e:gingee|Gingee]] in 1649. The fort later passed to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]] and the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]].

greuthungi.t: The eastern Goths of the Ukrainian steppe, whose realm under Ermanaric was shattered by the Huns and set off the great migrations.
greuthungi.o: [[e:goths|Goths]] moving south-east from the [[e:vistula|Vistula]] reached the lands north of the [[e:black-sea|Black Sea]] in the 3rd century, the land [[e:jordanes|Jordanes]] called Oium. By the late 3rd century the Greuthungi, the 'steppe people', had emerged east of the [[e:dniester|Dniester]], separate from the [[s:tervingi|Tervingi]] to their west, and are linked to the [[e:chernyakhov-culture|Chernyakhov culture]].
greuthungi.r: [[e:ammianus-marcellinus|Ammianus Marcellinus]] describes the Greuthungi as ruled by kings, and their king [[e:ermanaric|Ermanaric]] was remembered as a mighty warrior whose dominion took in many peoples. Their society combined farming villages with a warrior aristocracy that raided and traded with the Roman world. Most remained pagan, though Gothic [[e:christianity|Christianity]] was spreading.
greuthungi.e: When the [[e:huns|Huns]] attacked around 375, [[e:ermanaric|Ermanaric]] took his own life and his successor Vithimiris fell in battle. Many Greuthungi submitted to the Huns, while others under [[e:alatheus|Alatheus]] and [[e:saphrax|Saphrax]] crossed the [[e:danube|Danube]] in 376 and helped crush the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] at [[e:edirne|Adrianople]] in 378. Their descendants formed part of the later [[e:ostrogoths|Ostrogoths]].

goguryeo.t: The largest of Korea's Three Kingdoms, a warlike northern power that ruled much of Manchuria and the northern peninsula and repelled massive Sui and Tang invasions.
goguryeo.o: According to tradition [[e:dongmyeong-of-goguryeo|Jumong]], a prince from [[s:buyeo|Buyeo]], founded Goguryeo in 37 BCE at [[e:jolbon|Jolbon]] in the middle [[e:yalu-river|Yalu]] valley. The kingdom grew from a federation of five clans in mountainous terrain, moved its capital to [[e:gungnae|Gungnae]] (modern [[e:ji-an-jilin|Ji'an]]) and by the 4th century had taken the Chinese [[e:commandery|commanderies]] of [[e:lelang-commandery|Lelang]] and [[e:daifang-commandery|Daifang]].
goguryeo.r: Kings ruled through a warrior aristocracy and a system of mountain fortresses. [[e:sosurim-of-goguryeo|Sosurim]] adopted [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] and set up a Confucian academy in 372. [[e:gwanggaeto-the-great|Gwanggaeto the Great]] expanded in all directions, recorded on his stele of 414, and [[e:jangsu-of-goguryeo|Jangsu]] moved the capital to [[e:pyongyang|Pyongyang]] in 427. Painted tombs show hunters, dancers and armoured cavalry. Goguryeo defeated [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] at the [[e:battle-of-salsu|Salsu]] river in 612 and held Ansi fortress against [[s:later-tang|Tang]] in 645.
goguryeo.e: Succession quarrels after the dictator [[e:yeon-gaesomun|Yeon Gaesomun]] died let a [[s:silla|Silla]] and [[s:later-tang|Tang]] alliance take [[e:pyongyang|Pyongyang]] in 668. Its people later contributed to [[s:balhae|Balhae]], [[s:lesser-goguryeo|Lesser Goguryeo]] and [[s:goryeo|Goryeo]], whose name derives from Goguryeo.

gujarat-sultanate.t: A rich maritime sultanate of western India that built Ahmedabad and fought the Portuguese for control of the Arabian Sea.
gujarat-sultanate.o: [[e:muzaffar-shah-i|Zafar Khan]], governor of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] for the [[e:tughlaq-dynasty|Tughluqs]], declared independence in 1407 as Muzaffar Shah after [[e:timur|Timur's]] sack of Delhi left the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] powerless. His grandson [[e:ahmad-shah-i-of-gujarat|Ahmad Shah I]] founded [[e:ahmedabad|Ahmedabad]] in 1411 on the Sabarmati river and made it the capital of the [[s:muzaffarid-dynasty|Muzaffarid dynasty]].
gujarat-sultanate.r: [[e:gujarat|Gujarat's]] ports, including [[e:khambhat|Cambay]], [[e:surat|Surat]] and Diu, were hubs of the [[e:indian-ocean-trade|Indian Ocean trade]] in textiles, [[e:indigo|indigo]] and [[e:spice-trade|spices]]. [[e:mahmud-begada|Mahmud Begada]], the greatest sultan, captured [[e:champaner|Champaner]] and [[s:junagadh-state|Junagadh]], and his fleet with the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]] fought the Portuguese at [[e:chaul|Chaul]] and Diu. [[e:ahmedabad|Ahmedabad's]] mosques, with their carved stone screens such as [[e:sidi-saiyyed-mosque|Sidi Saiyyed]], blend Islamic and local [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] and Jain craftsmanship.
gujarat-sultanate.e: [[e:bahadur-shah-of-gujarat|Bahadur Shah]] ceded [[e:vasai|Bassein]] and allowed a fort at Diu to the Portuguese and was killed by them in 1537. Weak successors and noble factions followed, and [[e:akbar|Akbar]] of the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]] conquered [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1572 to 1573.

gran-colombia.t: Bolívar's great republic uniting Venezuela, New Granada, Quito and Panama, which won independence for northern South America but broke apart in 1830.
gran-colombia.o: In December 1819, after [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]]'s victory at [[e:battle-of-boyaca|Boyacá]], the [[e:congress-of-angostura|Congress of Angostura]] proclaimed the [[s:republic-of-colombia|Republic of Colombia]], uniting [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]] and [[e:new-granada|New Granada]]. The [[e:congress-of-cucuta|Congress of Cúcuta]] adopted a centralist constitution in 1821, with Bolívar as president and [[e:francisco-de-paula-santander|Francisco de Paula Santander]] as vice-president. [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]] joined in 1821, and [[e:quito|Quito]] and [[e:guayaquil|Guayaquil]] in 1822.
gran-colombia.r: [[e:francisco-de-paula-santander|Santander]] governed from [[e:bogota|Bogotá]] while [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]] campaigned in [[e:peru|Peru]] and [[s:royal-audiencia-of-charcas|Upper Peru]]. The republic abolished the Indian tribute and passed a free-womb law in 1821. Regional resentment grew, especially in [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]], where [[e:jose-antonio-paez|José Antonio Páez]] led the [[e:la-cosiata|Cosiata]] revolt in 1826. After the failure of the [[e:convention-of-ocana|Convention of Ocaña]] in 1828, Bolívar assumed dictatorial powers and survived an assassination attempt that September.
gran-colombia.e: [[s:venezuela|Venezuela]] under [[e:jose-antonio-paez|Páez]] seceded in 1830, followed by [[s:republic-of-ecuador|Ecuador]] under [[e:juan-jose-flores|Juan José Flores]]. [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]] resigned and died at [[e:santa-marta|Santa Marta]] in December 1830. In 1831 the remainder became the [[s:republic-of-new-granada|Republic of New Granada]].

gerrha.t: A legendary trading city of eastern Arabia, described by Greek writers as the richest place in the world for its incense and spice trade.
gerrha.o: Gerrha is known mainly from Greek and Roman writers, who say it was founded by Chaldean exiles from [[e:babylon|Babylon]] on the [[e:persian-gulf|Gulf]] coast of eastern [[e:arabia|Arabia]]. It flourished from around the 4th century BCE. Its site has never been identified with certainty; [[e:thaj|Thaj]], [[e:hofuf|Hofuf]] and the coast near [[e:uqair|Uqair]] have all been proposed.
gerrha.r: The Gerrhaeans carried frankincense and other goods from south [[e:arabia|Arabia]] across the desert and shipped Indian wares up the [[e:persian-gulf|Gulf]] to [[e:babylonia|Babylonia]]. [[e:agatharchides|Agatharchides]] and [[e:strabo|Strabo]] describe houses decorated with gold, [[e:silver|silver]] and [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]]. In 205 BCE the [[e:seleucid-empire|Seleucid]] king [[e:antiochus-iii-the-great|Antiochus III]] sailed to Gerrha and accepted a tribute of silver, frankincense and [[e:myrrh|myrrh]] in return for leaving it free. Local coins with [[e:aramaic|Aramaic]] legends were struck in the region.
gerrha.e: Gerrha fades from the sources around the 1st century CE as Roman [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] trade and the Nabataean and Palmyrene routes took over. Its precise location remains one of the open questions of Arabian archaeology.

galindians.t: The southernmost Baltic people of Prussia, living among the Masurian lakes and named by Ptolemy, whose land was almost empty by the time the Teutonic Knights arrived.
galindians.o: Ptolemy listed the Galindai in the 2nd century, and they are usually located in the lake country of southern [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], roughly modern [[e:masuria|Masuria]] in [[e:poland|Poland]]. Like their neighbours the [[s:sudovians|Sudovians]] and other Prussian groups, they lived in scattered clans around fortified hilltops, without any known central authority.
galindians.r: Almost nothing is recorded of their institutions. They farmed, fished and hunted in a land of forest and lakes, and shared the pagan religion and West Baltic speech of the [[e:old-prussians|Prussians]]. The Teutonic chronicler [[e:peter-of-dusburg|Peter of Dusburg]] claimed that Galindia had been depopulated by wars and famine long before his time.
galindians.e: By the late 13th century the area formed part of the great wilderness that the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]] absorbed during its conquest of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], completed in 1283. Survivors were merged into the Prussian population, and the region was later resettled by German and Polish (Masurian) colonists.

gezer.t: Gezer, a Canaanite city on the road from Egypt to Jerusalem, captured by pharaohs and, by biblical tradition, given to Solomon as a dowry.
gezer.o: Gezer lay on a hill at the edge of the Judaean foothills, overlooking the coastal road. In the [[e:middle-bronze-age|Middle Bronze Age]] it was fortified with massive walls and gates, and a row of tall standing stones marked a cultic high place that still stands.
gezer.r: In the [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]] local kings ruled as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]]. [[e:thutmose-iii|Thutmose III]] lists Gezer among his conquests, its kings Milkilu and Yapahu wrote [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]], and the [[e:merneptah-stele|Merneptah Stele]] boasts that Gezer was seized. The Gezer calendar, an early [[e:hebrew|Hebrew]] inscription, was found there.
gezer.e: Gezer kept its independence after the end of Egyptian rule until a [[e:pharaoh|pharaoh]] burned it, according to 1 Kings, and gave it to [[e:solomon|Solomon]] of the [[s:united-kingdom-of-israel|United Kingdom of Israel]]. Its later Israelite gate is often linked to that era.

ghassanid-kingdom.t: Christian Arab allies of Byzantium who guarded the desert frontier of Syria and patronised Miaphysite Christianity until the Islamic conquests.
ghassanid-kingdom.o: The [[s:ghassanids|Ghassanids]] were an Arab tribe said to have migrated from south [[e:arabia|Arabia]] to the Syrian desert margins, traditionally in the 3rd century. Around 500 they became Roman federates, and in 529 the emperor Justinian made [[e:al-harith-ibn-jabala|al-Harith ibn Jabala]] supreme phylarch of the [[e:arabs|Arabs]], giving the family authority over the allied tribes of the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire's]] eastern frontier.
ghassanid-kingdom.r: Ghassanid rulers led mobile cavalry against the [[s:lakhmid-kingdom|Lakhmid Kingdom]], ally of the [[s:sasanian-empire|Sasanian Empire]], and policed the desert routes. They were committed Miaphysite Christians and protected that church against imperial pressure, sponsoring [[e:bishop|bishops]] and monasteries. Their camp at [[e:jabiyah|Jabiyah]] in the [[e:golan-heights|Golan]] and sites such as [[e:rusafa|Rusafa]] served as courts, and poets such as [[e:al-nabigha-al-dhubyani|al-Nabigha]] praised them.
ghassanid-kingdom.e: In 582 [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]] arrested [[e:al-mundhir-ibn-al-harith|al-Mundhir ibn al-Harith]] and the federation broke up into rival chiefs. Revived partly against the [[e:persians|Persians]], Ghassanid forces fought for [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantium]] at [[e:battle-of-the-yarmuk|Yarmuk]] in 636 against the [[s:rashidun-caliphate|Rashidun Caliphate]]. Their last king, [[e:jabala-ibn-al-ayham|Jabala ibn al-Ayham]], briefly converted to [[e:islam|Islam]], then withdrew to Byzantine [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]].

gaochang-kingdom.t: A Chinese-ruled oasis kingdom in the Turpan basin that flourished on Silk Road trade and sponsored the pilgrim Xuanzang, before the Tang annexed it in 640.
gaochang-kingdom.o: [[e:gaochang|Gaochang]] grew from a Han military colony in the [[e:turfan|Turpan]] basin into the seat of a commandery under [[s:former-liang|Former Liang]] and its successors. After the [[s:rouran-khaganate|Rouran Khaganate]] destroyed the [[s:northern-liang|Northern Liang]] remnant there in 460, it installed [[e:kan-bozhou|Kan Bozhou]] as King of Gaochang. After several short-lived dynasties, the Qu family took the throne around 500 and held it until 640.
gaochang-kingdom.r: [[e:gaochang|Gaochang's]] rulers governed a largely Chinese population with Chinese-style offices, Confucian schooling and Chinese law, while paying tribute to the [[s:rouran-khaganate|Rouran]] and later the Turks. Documents from the [[e:astana-cemetery|Astana cemetery]] record contracts, taxes and caravans trading [[e:silk|silk]], horses and slaves. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] flourished: in 630 King [[e:qu-wentai|Qu Wentai]] welcomed [[e:xuanzang|Xuanzang]] and funded his journey to [[e:india|India]].
gaochang-kingdom.e: [[e:qu-wentai|Qu Wentai]] allied with the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turkic Khaganate]] and blocked trade to [[e:china|China]]. In 640 the [[s:tang-dynasty|Tang Dynasty]] sent [[e:hou-junji|Hou Junji]], Qu Wentai died as the army approached, and his son surrendered. [[e:gaochang|Gaochang]] became the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] prefecture of Xizhou.

griqualand-west.t: The Griqua community of Griquatown under the Waterboer family, whose land claims became the legal key to the Kimberley diamond fields.
griqualand-west.o: [[e:griqua|Griqua]], people of mixed [[e:khoekhoe|Khoekhoe]] and settler descent from the Cape, had gathered at the [[e:london-missionary-society|London Missionary Society]] station of [[e:griquatown|Klaarwater]] north of the [[e:orange-river|Orange River]]. In 1813 the missionary [[e:john-campbell-missionary|John Campbell]] helped them adopt a written constitution and renamed the place Griquatown, under the leaders [[e:adam-kok-ii|Adam Kok II]] and Barend Barends.
griqualand-west.r: The community was governed by elected kapteins and a council, with mission influence strong in law, schooling and church life. After [[e:adam-kok-ii|Adam Kok II]] moved away, [[e:andries-waterboer|Andries Waterboer]], kaptein from 1820, made a treaty with the Cape in 1834 that brought a small subsidy and guns. The [[e:griqua|Griqua]] lived by herding, hunting and trading, and spoke [[e:cape-dutch|Cape Dutch]].
griqualand-west.e: When diamonds were found in the late 1860s, [[e:nicolaas-waterboer|Nicolaas Waterboer's]] claim to the diggings was upheld by the [[e:keate-award|Keate Award]], and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] annexed the territory in 1871, creating the [[s:griqualand-west-colony|Griqualand West Colony]] around [[e:kimberley|Kimberley]].

gorkha-kingdom.t: A small hill kingdom of central Nepal whose king Prithvi Narayan Shah conquered the Kathmandu Valley and created modern Nepal.
gorkha-kingdom.o: In 1559 [[e:drabya-shah|Drabya Shah]], a younger son of the ruler of the [[s:kingdom-of-lamjung|Kingdom of Lamjung]], seized the hilltop village of Gorkha and founded a new principality among the [[e:chaubise-rajya|Chaubise Rajya]] of central [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Nepal]]. His descendants, the Shah dynasty, slowly enlarged the kingdom and [[e:ram-shah|Ram Shah]] became known for codes of justice.
gorkha-kingdom.r: Gorkha was a poor but well-organised state whose kings relied on a militarised peasantry of [[e:khas-people|Khas]], [[e:magar-people|Magar]] and [[e:gurung|Gurung]] soldiers. [[e:prithvi-narayan-shah|Prithvi Narayan Shah]], who took the throne in 1743, blockaded the [[e:kathmandu-valley|Kathmandu Valley's]] trade, took the [[s:kingdom-of-makwanpur|Kingdom of Makwanpur]] in 1762 and [[e:kirtipur|Kirtipur]] in 1767, and armed his soldiers with [[e:musket|muskets]].
gorkha-kingdom.e: In 1768 [[e:prithvi-narayan-shah|Prithvi Narayan Shah]] captured [[e:kathmandu|Kathmandu]], followed by [[e:lalitpur-nepal|Patan]] and [[e:bhaktapur|Bhaktapur]], and moved his capital there, creating the [[s:kingdom-of-nepal|Kingdom of Nepal]]. Gorkha remained the dynasty's ancestral seat, and its name was given to the [[e:gurkhas|Gurkha]] soldiers.

guangzhouwan.t: A small French leased territory on the coast of Guangdong, administered as part of French Indochina for nearly half a century.
guangzhouwan.o: During the scramble for concessions in [[e:china|China]], [[e:france|France]] occupied the bay of Guangzhouwan on the [[e:leizhou-peninsula|Leizhou]] peninsula in 1898, and a convention of 1899 granted it a ninety-nine-year lease. France wanted a coaling station and a counterweight to [[s:hong-kong-british|British Hong Kong]].
guangzhouwan.r: The territory was attached to [[s:french-indochina|French Indochina]], governed by an administrator under the governor-general in [[e:hanoi|Hanoi]], with its seat at [[e:zhanjiang|Fort-Bayard]] (modern Zhanjiang). It never became the great port [[e:france|France]] hoped for, and its economy rested on local trade, a free port, opium and smuggling. Local Chinese notables kept much influence over daily life.
guangzhouwan.e: [[e:japan|Japan]] occupied the territory in 1943 with the acquiescence of [[s:vichy-france|Vichy France]]. In August 1945 the French provisional government agreed to return it, and it passed to the [[s:nationalist-government|Nationalist government]] in the following months, becoming the city of [[e:zhanjiang|Zhanjiang]].

gojoseon.t: The first Korean kingdom known from written sources, centred on the Liaodong and northern Korean region until its conquest by Han China in 108 BCE.
gojoseon.o: Korean tradition credits its founding to the mythical [[e:dangun|Dangun]] in 2333 BCE, but the historical state appears in Chinese sources from about the 7th century BCE as a power of the [[e:liao-dynasty|Liao]] river basin and northwestern [[e:korea|Korea]], linked to the [[e:liaoning|Liaoning]] bronze dagger culture. Its centre later shifted to the [[e:taedong-river|Taedong]] river near modern [[e:pyongyang|Pyongyang]].
gojoseon.r: Early rulers took the title of king by the 4th century BCE and clashed with the Chinese state of Yan. Around 194 BCE the refugee Wiman ousted [[e:jun-of-gojoseon|King Jun]] and founded a dynasty that prospered as a middleman between [[e:han-dynasty|Han China]] and the southern Korean polities. A short law code of eight articles, three of which survive, punished murder, injury and theft.
gojoseon.e: [[e:ugeo-of-gojoseon|King Ugeo's]] control of trade and refusal to submit provoked [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu of Han]], whose armies besieged [[e:wanggeom-seong|Wanggeom-seong]]; the city fell in 108 BCE after Ugeo's assassination. Han set up four [[e:commandery|commanderies]], including [[e:lelang-commandery|Lelang]], and later Korean states looked back to Gojoseon as the founding Korean polity.

gadhka-state.t: A minor chiefship of central Kathiawar, one of the small estates near Rajkot.
gadhka-state.o: Gadhka was a small estate in central [[e:kathiawar|Kathiawar]] held by a local chiefly family from around 1700. Its founding is known mainly from local tradition.
gadhka-state.r: The ruler held a few villages and, after 1807, came under British supervision in the [[e:kathiawar-agency|Kathiawar Agency]]. Few further details are recorded.
gadhka-state.e: Gadhka merged into the [[s:saurashtra-state|United State of Saurashtra]] in 1948 and became part of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]] in 1960, in [[s:rajkot-state|Rajkot]] district.

gortyn.t: Powerful city of the Mesara in southern Crete, famous for the Gortyn Code, the longest surviving early Greek law inscription.
gortyn.o: Gortyn grew in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]] on the Lethaios river at the western edge of the [[e:mesara-plain|Mesara]] plain, near the older Minoan centre of [[s:phaistos|Phaistos]]. By the 7th century BCE it was a Dorian city and, with [[s:knossos|Knossos]], one of the two strongest powers on [[e:crete|Crete]].
gortyn.r: The [[e:gortyn-code|Gortyn Code]], inscribed c. 450 BCE on a wall later built into the Roman odeion, sets out laws on marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption and the status of slaves and serfs. Gortyn was ruled by [[e:kosmoi|kosmoi]] magistrates and had men's messes. In the [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]] it fought [[s:knossos|Knossos]] and destroyed [[s:phaistos|Phaistos]] c. 150 BCE.
gortyn.e: After the Roman conquest of 69 to 67 BCE, Gortyn, which had cooperated with [[e:rome|Rome]], became the capital of the province of [[s:roman-cyrenaica|Crete and Cyrenaica]]. It flourished under the Empire and the early [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]].

gallic-empire.t: Breakaway Roman state in Gaul, Britain and for a time Hispania, set up by Postumus in 260 when the empire seemed unable to defend its frontiers.
gallic-empire.o: In 260, after the emperor [[e:valerian|Valerian]] was captured by the [[e:persians|Persians]] and Germanic invaders broke across the [[e:rhine|Rhine]], the governor [[e:postumus|Postumus]] was proclaimed emperor by his troops. He besieged [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] and killed [[e:gallienus|Gallienus]]' son [[e:saloninus|Saloninus]] there and won the loyalty of [[e:gaul|Gaul]], [[e:germania|Germania]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:hispania|Hispania]].
gallic-empire.r: The Gallic emperors kept Roman institutions, with their own consuls, praetorian guard and mints at [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] and [[e:trier|Trier]]. They did not march on [[e:rome|Rome]] but concentrated on defending the [[e:rhine|Rhine]]. [[e:postumus|Postumus]] was murdered by his troops in 269, followed by [[e:marius-emperor|Marius]], [[e:victorinus|Victorinus]] and [[e:tetricus-i|Tetricus I]].
gallic-empire.e: [[e:hispania|Hispania]] returned to the central empire early, and [[e:victorinus|Victorinus]] was murdered in 271. In 274 Aurelian defeated [[e:tetricus-i|Tetricus]] near [[e:chalons-en-champagne|Châlons]], where Tetricus seems to have abandoned his army. He was paraded in Aurelian's triumph and then given an office in [[e:italy|Italy]], and the provinces rejoined the [[s:roman-empire|Roman Empire]].

graaff-reinet-republic.t: The first Boer republic, proclaimed by frontier farmers who drove out the Dutch East India Company's magistrate in 1795.
graaff-reinet-republic.o: [[e:graaff-reinet|Graaff-Reinet]], the eastern frontier district of the [[s:dutch-cape-colony|Dutch Cape Colony]], was in turmoil over the Company's handling of conflict with the [[e:xhosa-people|Xhosa]] and the [[e:san-people|San]]. In February 1795 the [[e:burghers|burghers]] expelled the landdrost [[e:honoratus-maynier|Honoratus Maynier]] and declared their independence, led by [[e:adriaan-van-jaarsveld|Adriaan van Jaarsveld]] and [[e:marthinus-prinsloo|Marthinus Prinsloo]].
graaff-reinet-republic.r: The rebels formed an assembly of national representatives, adopted the language of the [[e:french-revolution|French Revolution]] and demanded freedom to deal with Africans on their own terms, including enslaving captured [[e:san-people|San]]. They refused to recognise the Company's officials and, later, the authority of the British.
graaff-reinet-republic.e: After [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] took the Cape in 1795, it cut off supplies of ammunition, and the [[e:graaff-reinet|Graaff-Reinet]] [[e:burghers|burghers]] submitted in 1796. Further revolts broke out in 1799 and 1801, and the episode is often seen as a forerunner of the later [[e:boers|Boer]] republics.

governorate-of-paraguay.t: The Spanish province centred on Asunción, best known for the Jesuit missions among the Guaraní and for the Comunero revolts against royal authority.
governorate-of-paraguay.o: In 1617 the crown divided the [[s:governorate-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|Governorate of the Río de la Plata]] in two. The northern part, with its capital at [[e:asuncion|Asunción]], became the [[e:governorate|Governorate]] of [[s:republic-of-paraguay|Paraguay]], also known as Guayrá, covering the lands along the [[e:paraguay|Paraguay]] and upper [[e:parana-river|Paraná]] rivers.
governorate-of-paraguay.r: [[s:republic-of-paraguay|Paraguay]] was a poor, largely mestizo and [[e:guarani-people|Guaraní]]-speaking province. The [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] built a network of reductions among the Guaraní, which the bandeirantes of [[e:sao-paulo|São Paulo]] raided in the 1620s and 1630s, forcing the missions south. [[e:yerba-mate|Yerba mate]] was the chief export. Settlers resented the Jesuits' control of indigenous labour, and the [[e:revolt-of-the-comuneros-paraguay|Comunero revolts]] of 1721 to 1735, led at first by [[e:jose-de-antequera-y-castro|José de Antequera]], challenged the [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]]'s authority.
governorate-of-paraguay.e: [[s:republic-of-paraguay|Paraguay]] joined the [[s:viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata]] in 1776 and became an intendancy in 1782. In 1811 it rejected the authority of [[e:buenos-aires|Buenos Aires]], defeated [[e:manuel-belgrano|Manuel Belgrano's]] army, and in May overthrew the governor, becoming the independent Republic of [[e:paraguay|Paraguay]].

grand-duchy-of-finland.t: Autonomous Finland within the Russian Empire, where Finnish national identity, institutions and the first female suffrage in Europe took shape.
grand-duchy-of-finland.o: [[e:russia|Russia]] conquered [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]] from [[e:sweden|Sweden]] in the [[e:finnish-war|Finnish War]] of 1808-1809. At the [[e:diet-of-porvoo|Diet of Porvoo]] in 1809 [[e:alexander-i-of-russia|Alexander I]] promised to respect [[e:finland|Finland's]] laws, Lutheran religion and estates, and Finland became a grand duchy with the tsar as grand duke. The Treaty of Fredrikshamn confirmed the transfer, and in 1812 the capital moved from [[e:turku|Turku]] to Helsinki.
grand-duchy-of-finland.r: [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]] kept its Swedish-era laws and had its own Senate, civil service, army for a time and, from 1860, its own currency, the markka. [[e:alexander-ii-of-russia|Alexander II]] convened the Diet regularly and allowed Finnish to become an official language. [[e:elias-lonnrot|Elias Lönnrot's]] [[e:kalevala|Kalevala]], published in 1835, inspired the national movement. In 1906 a unicameral parliament was created, elected by universal suffrage including women, the first in [[e:europe|Europe]].
grand-duchy-of-finland.e: From 1899 [[e:russification|Russification]] threatened Finnish autonomy, and Governor-General [[e:nikolai-bobrikov|Bobrikov]] was assassinated in 1904. After the [[e:russian-revolution|Russian Revolution]], the Finnish parliament declared independence on 6 December 1917, and [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] recognised it, creating the [[s:republic-of-finland|Republic of Finland]].

grand-duchy-of-tuscany.t: The Medici and then Habsburg-Lorraine state of Tuscany, patron of Galileo and a pioneer of Enlightenment reform, including abolition of the death penalty.
grand-duchy-of-tuscany.o: In 1569 [[e:pope-pius-v|Pope Pius V]] raised [[e:cosimo-i-de-medici|Cosimo I de' Medici]], ruler of the [[s:duchy-of-florence|Duchy of Florence]] and conqueror of [[s:republic-of-siena|Siena]], to the rank of [[e:grand-duke-of-tuscany|Grand Duke of Tuscany]], a title confirmed by the emperor in 1576.
grand-duchy-of-tuscany.r: The Medici grand dukes ran a centralised state from [[s:duchy-of-florence|Florence]]. [[e:ferdinando-i-de-medici|Ferdinando I]] made [[e:livorno|Livorno]] a free port open to [[e:jews|Jews]] and foreign merchants, and [[e:cosimo-ii-de-medici|Cosimo II]] made [[e:galileo-galilei|Galileo]] court mathematician. The Medici line ended in 1737; the last heiress, [[e:anna-maria-luisa-de-medici|Anna Maria Luisa]], left the family's art collections to [[e:florence|Florence]]. [[e:francis-i-holy-roman-emperor|Francis Stephen of Lorraine]] succeeded, and his son [[e:leopold-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Peter Leopold]] reformed law and trade, abolishing torture and the death penalty in 1786.
grand-duchy-of-tuscany.e: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] turned Tuscany into the [[s:kingdom-of-etruria|Kingdom of Etruria]] in 1801 and annexed it to [[e:france|France]] in 1807. Restored in 1814, the [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Lorraine]] dynasty left when [[e:leopold-ii-grand-duke-of-tuscany|Leopold II]] fled in 1859, and Tuscany voted to join the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]] in 1860.

gowa-sultanate.t: The Makassar kingdom that built a great free port in South Sulawesi and fought the Dutch East India Company until the Treaty of Bongaya in 1667.
gowa-sultanate.o: Gowa was one of several Makassar chiefdoms in southwest [[e:sulawesi|Sulawesi]]. In the early 16th century King [[e:tumaparisi-kallonna|Tumapa'risi' Kallonna]] joined it with neighbouring [[s:tallo-kingdom|Tallo]] in a twin kingdom and began conquering nearby states. The fortified port of [[e:somba-opu|Somba Opu]] became its capital.
gowa-sultanate.r: Makassar grew into one of the busiest ports in [[e:southeast-asia|Southeast Asia]], open to Malay, Portuguese, English and Danish traders and a key outlet for Moluccan [[e:spice-trade|spices]] outside [[e:dutch|Dutch]] control. In 1605 [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:alauddin-khalji|Alauddin]] and his [[s:tallo-kingdom|Tallo]] chancellor [[e:karaeng-matoaya|Karaeng Matoaya]] adopted [[e:islam|Islam]], and Gowa forced it on the [[e:bugis|Bugis]] states. Court scholars kept detailed chronicles and diaries.
gowa-sultanate.e: The [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]] under [[e:cornelis-speelman|Cornelis Speelman]], allied with [[e:arung-palakka|Arung Palakka of Bone]], defeated [[e:sultan-hasanuddin|Sultan Hasanuddin]], and the [[e:treaty-of-bongaya|Treaty of Bongaya]] of 1667 ended Gowa's power; [[e:somba-opu|Somba Opu]] fell in 1669. The sultanate survived as a lesser state until the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] conquest of 1906.

gaurihar-state.t: A small chiefship of the Bundelkhand Agency, confirmed by British sanad in 1807.
gaurihar-state.o: Gaurihar was one of the small [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] holdings confirmed by British sanads in 1807, after the British established supremacy in the region following the wars with the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]].
gaurihar-state.r: It was a minor, non-salute state of a few dozen villages. Little else of its history is recorded.
gaurihar-state.e: After independence Gaurihar was merged into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]] with the other [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] states and absorbed by 1950; it lies in [[s:chhatarpur-state|Chhatarpur]] district of [[e:madhya-pradesh|Madhya Pradesh]].

georgian-ssr.t: Soviet Georgia from 1921 to 1991, homeland of Stalin and Beria, known for its wine, resorts and strong national sentiment within the USSR.
georgian-ssr.o: In February 1921 the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] invaded the [[s:democratic-republic-of-georgia|Democratic Republic of Georgia]] and took [[e:tbilisi|Tiflis]], and the Georgian SSR was proclaimed. It joined the [[s:transcaucasian-sfsr|Transcaucasian SFSR]] in 1922 and became a full union republic in 1936, renaming its capital Tbilisi. A national uprising in August 1924 was crushed with thousands of executions.
georgian-ssr.r: [[s:georgia|Georgia]] was governed by its [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Communist Party]] within the Soviet system, with [[e:joseph-stalin|Stalin]] and [[e:lavrentiy-beria|Beria]] rising from its ranks. Collectivisation and purges hit hard, but the republic prospered from [[e:tea|tea]], citrus, wine and tourism. National feeling surfaced in the 1956 [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]] protests and the 1978 defence of Georgian as official language. [[e:eduard-shevardnadze|Eduard Shevardnadze]] led the party from 1972 to 1985.
georgian-ssr.e: On 9 April 1989 Soviet troops killed peaceful protesters in [[e:tbilisi|Tbilisi]], fuelling the independence movement. [[e:zviad-gamsakhurdia|Zviad Gamsakhurdia's]] nationalists won elections in 1990, and [[s:georgia|Georgia]] declared independence on 9 April 1991, becoming the Republic of [[e:georgia|Georgia]].

gurjara-pratihara.t: The great Rajput dynasty of Kannauj that held back Arab expansion into India and ruled most of the north in the 9th century.
gurjara-pratihara.o: The dynasty rose in [[e:malwa|Malwa]] and [[e:rajasthan|Rajasthan]] in the 8th century. [[e:nagabhata-i|Nagabhata I]] is credited with repelling Arab armies advancing from [[e:sindh|Sindh]] around 738. [[e:vatsaraja|Vatsaraja]] extended its power, and [[e:nagabhata-ii|Nagabhata II]] took [[e:kannauj|Kannauj]] around 816 from the [[s:ayudha-dynasty|Ayudha dynasty]], making it the capital.
gurjara-pratihara.r: For two centuries the Pratiharas competed with the [[s:pala-empire|Pala Empire]] and the [[s:rashtrakuta-dynasty|Rashtrakuta dynasty]] for control of [[e:kannauj|Kannauj]], a contest called the tripartite struggle. [[e:mihira-bhoja|Mihira Bhoja]], who ruled from 836 to 885, governed an empire from [[e:punjab|Punjab]] to [[e:bengal|Bengal's]] borders, and Arab travellers praised the security of his realm and his cavalry. [[e:mahendrapala-i|Mahendrapala I]] patronised the poet [[e:rajashekhara|Rajashekhara]]. The kings were [[e:vaishnavism|Vaishnavas]] and [[e:shaivism|Shaivas]].
gurjara-pratihara.e: The Rashtrakuta [[e:indra-iii|Indra III]] sacked [[e:kannauj|Kannauj]] around 916, and feudatories such as the [[s:chandela-dynasty|Chandela dynasty]] and the [[s:paramara-dynasty|Paramara dynasty]] broke away. [[e:mahmud-of-ghazni|Mahmud of Ghazni]] took Kannauj in 1018, and the dynasty faded away by 1036.

german-new-guinea.t: Germany's main Pacific colony, covering northeast New Guinea, the Bismarck Archipelago and much of Micronesia, until Australia and Japan seized it in 1914.
german-new-guinea.o: In 1884 [[e:germany|Germany]] proclaimed a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] over northeastern [[e:new-guinea|New Guinea]], named Kaiser-Wilhelmsland, and the [[e:bismarck-archipelago|Bismarck Archipelago]]. The territory was run by the chartered New [[e:guinea|Guinea]] Company until 1899, when the Reich took over. That year Germany bought the [[e:caroline-islands|Caroline]], [[e:palau|Palau]] and [[e:northern-mariana-islands|Northern Mariana Islands]] from [[e:spain|Spain]], and the [[s:marshall-islands-protectorate|Marshall Islands Protectorate]], including [[s:territory-of-nauru|Nauru]], was merged in 1906.
german-new-guinea.r: Administration moved from [[e:finschhafen|Finschhafen]] to [[e:madang|Friedrich-Wilhelmshafen]] (Madang), then [[e:kokopo|Herbertshöhe]], and to [[e:rabaul|Rabaul]] in 1910. Copra plantations depended on recruited labour, often coerced, and phosphate was mined on [[s:territory-of-nauru|Nauru]] and [[e:angaur|Angaur]]. Governor [[e:albert-hahl|Albert Hahl]], from 1902 to 1914, extended control through appointed village headmen called luluai and a head tax. Lutheran and Catholic missions were active, and scientists studied the region's peoples.
german-new-guinea.e: In September 1914 an Australian force captured [[e:rabaul|Rabaul]] after fighting at [[e:battle-of-bita-paka|Bita Paka]], while [[e:japan|Japan]] seized the Micronesian islands. After the war the lands became the [[s:territory-of-new-guinea|Territory of New Guinea]], the [[s:south-seas-mandate|South Seas Mandate]] and the [[s:territory-of-nauru|Territory of Nauru]].
german-new-guinea.la: German, Tok Pisin, Papuan and Austronesian languages

gongsun-yan.t: A semi-independent regime in Liaodong that held the north-east for three generations and stretched into Korea, until Sima Yi destroyed it in 238.
gongsun-yan.o: In 189, as the [[s:han-dynasty|Han Dynasty]] disintegrated, [[e:gongsun-du|Gongsun Du]] was appointed governor of [[e:liaodong|Liaodong]] and quickly made himself its independent master, ruling from [[e:liaoyang|Xiangping]] (Liaoyang). He expanded against [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] and the [[s:wuhuan|Wuhuan]] and controlled the Han [[e:commandery|commanderies]] in northern [[e:korea|Korea]].
gongsun-yan.r: His son [[e:gongsun-kang|Gongsun Kang]] created [[e:daifang-commandery|Daifang Commandery]] south of [[e:lelang-commandery|Lelang]] around 204 and in 207 sent [[e:cao-cao|Cao Cao]] the heads of the fugitive Yuan brothers, buying recognition. The regime controlled trade routes to [[e:korea|Korea]] and [[e:japan|Japan]]. [[e:gongsun-yuan|Gongsun Yuan]], who seized power in 228, courted [[s:eastern-wu|Eastern Wu]], then killed its envoys to please [[s:cao-wei|Cao Wei]], and in 237 proclaimed himself King of Yan.
gongsun-yan.e: In 238 [[s:cao-wei|Cao Wei]] sent [[e:sima-yi|Sima Yi]], who besieged [[e:liaoyang|Xiangping]], captured and executed [[e:gongsun-yuan|Gongsun Yuan]] and massacred thousands of men. Wei took over [[e:lelang-commandery|Lelang]] and [[e:daifang-commandery|Daifang]], opening direct contact with the [[e:wa-japan|Wa of Japan]].

great-xi.t: The short reign of the rebel Zhang Xianzhong in Sichuan, notorious in Chinese history for mass killings during the collapse of the Ming.
great-xi.o: [[e:zhang-xianzhong|Zhang Xianzhong]], a former soldier from [[e:shaanxi|Shaanxi]], led one of the great peasant armies that roamed northern and central [[e:china|China]] from the 1630s. In 1644, as [[e:li-zicheng|Li Zicheng]] took [[e:beijing|Beijing]], Zhang invaded [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]], captured [[e:chengdu|Chengdu]] and proclaimed himself king of Great Xi.
great-xi.r: Zhang set up ministries, examinations and coinage, but his regime is remembered above all for terror against officials, scholars, [[e:gentry|gentry]] and ordinary people suspected of disloyalty. [[e:sichuan|Sichuan's]] population collapsed during these years through massacre, war, famine and plague; how much Zhang himself was responsible is still debated, as later [[e:qing-empire|Qing]] accounts exaggerated.
great-xi.e: In late 1646 [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]] forces under [[e:hooge|Hooge]] entered [[e:sichuan|Sichuan]], and [[e:zhang-xianzhong|Zhang Xianzhong]] was killed in battle near [[e:xichong-county|Xichong]] in early 1647. His adopted sons [[e:sun-kewang|Sun Kewang]] and [[e:li-dingguo|Li Dingguo]] led his army south and later served the [[s:southern-ming|Southern Ming]].

german-togoland.t: Germany's smallest African colony, promoted in Berlin as a model colony, which was taken by British and French forces in the first weeks of the First World War.
german-togoland.o: On 5 July 1884 the German envoy [[e:gustav-nachtigal|Gustav Nachtigal]] signed a protection treaty with Mlapa III, a chief at [[e:togoville|Togoville]] on Lake [[e:togo|Togo]]. [[e:germany|Germany]] then pushed inland, fixing borders with the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast Colony]] and [[s:french-dahomey|French Dahomey]] in agreements of the 1890s. The capital moved to [[e:lome|Lome]] in 1897.
german-togoland.r: German officials called [[e:togo|Togo]] a model colony because it covered its own costs. They built a wharf at [[e:lome|Lome]] and three railways, including the line to [[e:kpalime|Palime]] known as the cocoa railway, and promoted [[e:cotton|cotton]], cocoa and palm products. This was achieved through taxes, forced labour and harsh punishments. Catholic and Protestant missions ran most schools, and a large radio station was built at Kamina.
german-togoland.e: British and French troops invaded in August 1914 and the Germans surrendered on 26 August. The territory was divided in 1916, and the [[e:league-of-nations|League of Nations]] later confirmed it as [[s:british-togoland|British Togoland]] and [[s:french-togoland|French Togoland]].

gauda-kingdom.t: The Bengal kingdom of Shashanka, the first ruler to unite much of Bengal and an enemy of Harsha.
gauda-kingdom.o: After the collapse of the [[s:gupta-empire|Gupta Empire]], [[e:shashanka|Shashanka]] rose in Gauda, western and northern [[e:bengal|Bengal]], in the late 6th century, perhaps beginning as a feudatory of the [[s:later-guptas|Later Guptas]]. He made [[e:karnasuvarna|Karnasuvarna]], near modern [[e:murshidabad|Murshidabad]], his capital and extended his rule over [[s:kingdom-of-magadha|Magadha]] and into [[e:odisha|Odisha]], where the [[s:shailodbhava-dynasty|Shailodbhava dynasty]] acknowledged him.
gauda-kingdom.r: [[e:shashanka|Shashanka]] was a [[e:shaivism|Shaiva]], and his gold coins show [[e:shiva|Shiva]] with his bull [[e:nandi-hinduism|Nandi]]. Allied with the king of [[e:malwa|Malwa]], he killed [[e:rajyavardhana|Rajyavardhana]] of the [[s:pushyabhuti-dynasty|Pushyabhuti dynasty]] around 606, provoking a long war with [[e:harsha|Harsha]]. Buddhist sources, including [[e:xuanzang|Xuanzang]], portray him as a persecutor who cut down the Bodhi tree at [[e:bodh-gaya|Bodh Gaya]], though this is probably exaggerated. Bengali tradition credits him with the start of the Bengali calendar.
gauda-kingdom.e: [[e:shashanka|Shashanka]] held his kingdom until his death, around 625 or later. His successors could not keep it, and [[e:bhaskaravarman|Bhaskaravarman]] of [[s:kamarupa|Kamarupa]] took [[e:karnasuvarna|Karnasuvarna]]. [[e:bengal|Bengal]] then entered a period of disorder until the rise of the [[s:pala-empire|Pala Empire]].

german-confederation.t: Loose league of German states created at the Congress of Vienna, led by Austria and the arena of its rivalry with Prussia.
german-confederation.o: After [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] fall the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] created the German Confederation in 1815 as a league of 39 sovereign states and [[e:free-imperial-city|free cities]], including [[e:austria|Austria]] and [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] for their German lands and foreign monarchs for [[e:hanover|Hanover]], [[s:county-of-holstein|Holstein]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-luxembourg|Luxembourg]]. Its [[e:federal-convention-german-confederation|Federal Diet]] met in [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] under Austrian presidency.
german-confederation.r: The Confederation had no head of state or common government and existed mainly for mutual defence and order. Under [[e:klemens-von-metternich|Metternich]] it repressed liberalism through the [[e:carlsbad-decrees|Carlsbad Decrees]] of 1819. The [[e:frankfurt-parliament|Frankfurt Parliament]] of 1848-49 tried to replace it with a united German state but failed. Economic unity came instead through the Prussian-led [[e:zollverein|Zollverein]].
german-confederation.e: [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and [[e:austria|Austria]] clashed over [[s:provisional-government-of-schleswig-holstein|Schleswig-Holstein]], and the [[e:austro-prussian-war|Austro-Prussian War]] of 1866 ended the Confederation. Prussia formed the [[s:north-german-confederation|North German Confederation]], from which the [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] arose in 1871.

granadine-confederation.t: Colombia's experiment with a confederation of sovereign states between 1858 and 1863, overthrown by a liberal civil war.
granadine-confederation.o: Pressure for federalism had grown in the [[s:republic-of-new-granada|Republic of New Granada]], and [[s:republic-of-panama|Panama]], [[e:antioquia-department|Antioquia]] and other regions had become self-governing states. The constitution of 1858, under the conservative president [[e:mariano-ospina-rodriguez|Mariano Ospina Rodríguez]], created the Granadine Confederation, a union of eight states with a weak central government in [[e:bogota|Bogotá]].
granadine-confederation.r: The states had their own constitutions, armies and elections. Laws passed by [[e:mariano-ospina-rodriguez|Ospina]]'s government to control state elections and armies were seen by liberals as an attack on state [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]]. In 1860 [[e:tomas-cipriano-de-mosquera|Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera]], governor of the [[e:state-of-cauca|State of Cauca]], rebelled and declared Cauca separate from the confederation, starting a civil war.
granadine-confederation.e: [[e:tomas-cipriano-de-mosquera|Mosquera]] captured [[e:bogota|Bogotá]] in July 1861 and took power, expelling the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] and confiscating church lands. The [[e:rionegro-convention|Rionegro Convention]] of 1863 replaced the confederation with the [[s:united-states-of-colombia|United States of Colombia]].
